theories.hypothesis: League home-field advantage has declined since 2009 and the PFF/Cole paths should use a lower 2026 HFA than the legacy ~2.5 points.
theories.method: REG-season, non-neutral games 2009-2025 joined to nfelo. Rating-adjusted HFA = margin - (nfelo QB-adjusted Elo diff)/25 (no HFA/bye/div mods), by season and 5-season block with SEs; market-implied HFA = intercept of spread_line ~ rating_dif; market residual = margin + mkt_spread. Trend by WLS (2020 excluded), Welch t-test of eras. Out-of-sample: spread = -(rating_dif + k) for a k grid, k fit on <=2021, and nfelo's per-game hfa_pts, scored on 2022-2025 with MAE/bias and paired-bootstrap CIs (4000 resamples); rolling-origin windows W=1,3,5,10.
theories.metric: Realized rating-adjusted HFA (pts) by era; OOS MAE / bias of rating-based spread vs result; market residual and home cover rate
theories.recommendation: Use a single constant HFA of 1.75 points (acceptable band 1.5-2.0) for the PFF and Cole spread paths in 2026, with no dome/outdoor split. Anything >= 2.5 is significantly worse out-of-sample; 1.5-2.0 are statistically indistinguishable, 1.75 sits between the MAE-optimal 1.5 (median-driven) and bias-optimal 2.1 (mean-driven) and 0.2 above the market's 1.55.
theories.parameter_change: HFA_PFF = HFA_COLE = 1.75 for location == Home (replace 'nfelo (hfa_mod + home_time_advantage_mod)/25' and the '1.4 dome / 1.6-2.0 outdoor' defaults). Neutral/international handled in HFA-4.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv (2009-2025 REG, location Home) joined to nfelo_games.csv via kit.merged(); rating series = nfelo starting Elo + home_net_qb_mod (no PFF/Cole history exists locally).
theories.effect_size: Realized HFA down ~0.8 pts from 2009-13 to 2014-25 (2.73 -> ~1.95); market-implied down ~0.85 (2.4 -> 1.55). OOS MAE penalty of using 2.5 instead of 2.0 = +0.04 pts (CI +0.01..+0.07); of 3.0 = +0.10.
theories.expected_impact: Small: 0.02-0.04 MAE points on the PFF/Cole components if they currently carry a 2.5-ish HFA; roughly zero vs nfelo's per-game value, but removes ~0.95 pts SD of per-game noise (see HFA-2).
theories.uncertainty: Season-level HFA has SE ~0.8 pts; the 2022-25 block CI is 1.37-2.90. Exact choice within 1.5-2.0 cannot be resolved with this n.
theories.caveats: Rating-adjusted HFA depends on nfelo Elo being unbiased in level; cross-checked with raw mean margin (2.19 in 2022-25) and market-implied (1.56), which bracket the recommendation. 2020 excluded from all fits.

theories.hypothesis: Specific venues (SEA, DEN, KC, GB, NO, BAL ...) have reliably above/below-league HFA after empirical-Bayes shrinkage, and nfelo's per-game hfa_mod captures it.
theories.method: Per home franchise, residual r = margin - rating_dif - league HFA(season). Fit 2009-2021 (2020 excl, n=2742), test 2022-2025 (n=1064). Empirical Bayes: tau^2 = var(team means) - mean(sampling var), shrink = tau^2/(tau^2+se^2). OOS tests: regress test-window team residual on (a) EB fit excess, (b) raw fit excess, (c) nfelo hfa_pts minus league mean (slope 1 = predictive); team-level split-half correlation; OOS MAE of const vs const+EB (paired bootstrap 3000); nfelo calibration regression by era; check of ORIGINATOR's (hfa_mod + home_time_advantage_mod) double count; Denver singled out (altitude mechanism).
theories.metric: OOS slope of realized team excess on predicted excess; team-level correlation; OOS MAE difference; nfelo calibration slope
theories.result: Between-team SD of true HFA excess tau = 0.67 pts in fit window, 0.00 in test window; mean EB shrink factor 0.18 (i.e., keep 18% of a team's raw excess). Team-level corr(fit excess, test excess) r=0.21 (p=0.24, 32 teams). OOS slopes: EB excess 1.35 (se 1.37, p=0.33), raw excess 0.23 (se 0.23, p=0.32), nfelo hfa excess 0.15 (se 0.40, p=0.71); corr(nfelo team excess, realized 2022-25) r=-0.08. OOS MAE: const 9.795, const+EB 9.797 (diff +0.002, CI [-0.016,+0.021]), nfelo hfa_pts per game 9.802, nfelo hfa_mod/25 9.793. nfelo calibration (resid ~ hfa_pts): slope 0.67 (se 0.20) in 2009-19 but 0.02 (se 0.36) in 2021-25 and 0.15 (se 0.40) in 2022-25 -> nfelo's per-game site variation (SD 0.95 pts, range -0.86..+4.96 in 2022-25) is uncorrelated with realized HFA in the modern era. Time-zone term: corr(hfa_mod, home_time_advantage_mod)=0.62 and hfa_mod averages 2.27 when tz>0 vs 1.32 when tz<0, so adding the tz mod again double counts; realized HFA for tz>0.2 games = 1.81 (se 0.56) vs ORIGINATOR's 2.74; tz coefficient -0.2 (se 1.3). Denver: realized excess +2.00 (se 1.21, p=0.10, n=122 full sample), +3.44 (se 2.14, n=34) in 2022-25; market prices DEN +0.64 full / +1.29 in 2022-25 above league; other named venues' market excess within +/-0.5 and realized excesses flip sign across windows (NE +2.58 fit -> -1.80 test; BAL +2.00 -> -0.29; SEA +0.84 -> -0.64).
theories.recommendation: Do not model team/stadium-specific HFA and stop importing nfelo's per-game hfa_mod/time-zone variation into the PFF/Cole paths: it is ~1 pt of noise with zero OOS predictive slope. Use the constant from HFA-1. Denver is the only venue with a mechanism and consistent sign, but n=34 OOS makes it inconclusive; if anything, mirror the market's premium there rather than nfelo's.
theories.parameter_change: Replace per-game (hfa_mod + home_time_advantage_mod)/25 with constant 1.75 in PFF/Cole spreads; drop the separate time-zone add-on entirely (it is already inside hfa_mod and has no realized effect). Optional, low-confidence: DEN home games HFA = 1.75 + 0.75 = 2.5 (matches market-implied premium); all other venues no adjustment.
theories.data_used: games + nfelo_games (hfa_mod, hfa_base_mod, home_time_advantage_mod) 2009-2025 REG home games; unit = kit-normalized franchise id (LA/LAC/LV relocations pool old and new stadiums).
theories.effect_size: tau = 0.67 pts between teams (fit) vs ~0 (test); EB adjustments range -0.65 (CLE) to +0.68 (NE) and are not validated; nfelo per-game HFA SD 0.95 pts with slope 0.15 on outcomes.
theories.expected_impact: OOS MAE neutral (within +/-0.02); benefit is removal of ~0.95 pts SD of uncorrelated noise from 54% of the spread blend and a cleaner confidence-tag SD.
theories.uncertainty: Team-level estimates have SE ~1.2 pts even with 120+ games; only Denver (p=0.10) and WAS/TB (negative, p=0.02-0.04) are near significance and none replicated cleanly OOS.
theories.caveats: nfelo's HFA looked calibrated in 2009-2019 (slope 0.67-0.94), probably because it was fit on those seasons; the 2021-25 collapse to ~0 is the relevant evidence. Franchise moves (LA 2016, LAC 2017, LV 2020) reduce n for those teams.

theories.hypothesis: HFA differs by kickoff slot (SNF, MNF, TNF, Saturday, other) and in Week 1 relative to Sunday afternoon games.
theories.method: Slot from weekday + gametime (Sunday <15:00 early, 15-19 late, >=19 SNF; MNF; TNF incl. Thanksgiving; SAT; other). Rating-adjusted HFA and market residual by slot with Welch tests vs Sunday afternoon; OLS hfa_resid ~ slot + week1 + season FE (and + rest_dif) fit on 2009-2021 (2020 excl); OOS 2022-2025: slot adjustments applied to constant-HFA spread (MAE, bias, slope of OOS residual on fitted adjustment), same for market residual, and home cover rate by slot with binomial CIs.
theories.metric: Slot HFA deviation from Sunday afternoon (pts), OOS slope of residual on fitted slot adjustment, OOS MAE, home cover rate by slot
theories.result: Full sample 2009-25 ex 2020 (n=3806): Sun-aft 2.14 (se 0.24, n=2940), SNF 3.90 (0.86, n=265, p=0.05), MNF 1.62 (0.81, n=262), TNF 2.18 (0.80, n=248), SAT 0.47 (1.27, n=82), Week 1 0.89 (0.86, n=234, p=0.16). Fit-window regression: SNF +3.01 (se 1.10, p=0.006), MNF +0.56, TNF +0.82 (unchanged with rest_dif control), SAT -2.51 (p=0.17), WK1 -1.32 (p=0.21). OOS 2022-25 deviations from Sun-aft reverse sign: SNF -0.97 (n=72), MNF -2.41 (n=79), TNF -1.13 (n=78), SAT -1.03 (n=37), WK1 -1.93 (n=62, se 1.52). OOS slope of residual on fitted slot adjustment 0.30 (se 0.34, p=0.39); on market residual 0.18 (p=0.59); OOS MAE const 9.795 vs const+slot 9.797. OOS home cover vs market by slot all CIs contain 0.50 (MNF 0.455 [0.34,0.57], SNF 0.521, TNF 0.527, Sun-early 0.500). 2021-25 primetime pooled (SNF/MNF/TNF, n=283) HFA ~1.0 vs 2.38 Sun-aft, but the fit window showed the opposite (+1.4).
theories.recommendation: Keep as is: no slot-specific HFA. The only in-sample significant effect (SNF +3.0) reversed out of sample, and the market shows no slot bias. Week 1 is the one consistently negative slot (-1.0 fit, -1.9 test, pooled -1.26, p=0.16) but is inconclusive at n=234; do not add an adjustment.
theories.parameter_change: None. (Optional, LOW confidence, not recommended now: Week-1 HFA = 1.75 - 0.5.)
theories.data_used: games weekday/gametime/week/home_rest/away_rest + nfelo ratings, REG non-neutral 2009-2025.
theories.effect_size: Slot deviations are +/-1 to 3 pts with SE 0.8-1.4 and flip sign between windows; OOS predictive slope 0.30 +/- 0.34.
theories.expected_impact: Zero (adding slot HFA left OOS MAE unchanged at 9.797 vs 9.795).
theories.uncertainty: Each primetime slot has only ~70-80 OOS games (SE ~1.4 pts); a true +/-0.5 slot effect is undetectable with this data.
theories.caveats: Thanksgiving (n=32) and Fri/Tue/Wed (n=9) too small to say anything. Short-week/rest effects are handled elsewhere in the spec; rest_dif was +0.16 pts/day (p=0.11) in the fit window.

theories.hypothesis: At neutral and international sites the designated home team has a realized edge different from the spec defaults (0 neutral, 0.5-1.0 international).
theories.method: location == Neutral games classified as international (overseas stadium, plus the 2025 overseas slate identified by game id because nflverse lists the home stadium for those), domestic neutral (relocations), and Super Bowls. Designated-home rating-adjusted edge = margin - rating_dif; market-implied edge = spread_line - rating_dif; market residual; bootstrap CIs (5000); Welch vs regular home games same seasons; fit <=2021 / test 2022-25 MAE for k in {0, 0.75, fit-window edge, 2.0, nfelo per game}; audit of nfelo hfa_pts at neutral sites.
theories.metric: Designated-home rating-adjusted edge (pts) with bootstrap CI; market-implied edge; market residual; OOS MAE by HFA constant
theories.result: International REG: 54 games (48 with ratings), 22 in 2022-25. Designated-home edge 0.96 pts, 95% CI [-2.59, 4.69]; market-implied edge 0.52; market residual -1.07 [-4.62, +2.57], home cover 26-28. Welch vs regular home HFA (2.17): diff -1.20, p=0.53. JAX in London n=12: 1.60 (se 5.05). London n=36: 1.01 (se 2.38); Germany n=4: 2.72; Mexico n=2 rated: -11.8; Brazil/Ireland/Spain/Berlin n=5: 5.24. OOS 2022-25 (n=22): k=0 MAE 8.16 bias +1.21; k=0.75 MAE 7.91 bias +0.46; k=2.0 MAE 7.67 bias -0.79; nfelo per-game MAE 8.15 bias +1.01; market MAE 7.59 bias +0.45. Domestic neutral REG n=7 (edge 5.9, se 8.1) and Super Bowls n=17 (edge -2.3, se 3.3): uninformative. nfelo assigns a non-zero HFA (|hfa|>0.25) in 34 of 55 neutral REG games (mean |hfa| 0.73, range -3.07..+2.68) and mean |hfa| 1.20 in Super Bowls, i.e., it does not zero HFA at neutral sites.
theories.recommendation: Keep the spec's neutral/international constants (they sit inside the CI and match the market's 0.5 implied edge), but stop passing nfelo's per-game hfa_pts through at neutral sites - it is non-zero and up to +/-3 pts there with no support. The n (48) is far too small to prefer any value between 0 and 2 for international games.
theories.parameter_change: If location == Neutral: HFA_PFF = HFA_COLE = 0.75 for international venues (London/Germany/Mexico/Brazil/Spain/Ireland), 0.0 for domestic neutral and playoff neutral (Super Bowl), hard-overriding any nfelo hfa_mod/home_time_advantage_mod value. Do not apply any JAX-London or country-specific tweak.
theories.data_used: games location/stadium 2009-2025 (international list: Wembley, Twickenham, Tottenham, Azteca, Allianz Arena, Deutsche Bank Park, Arena Corinthians, Rogers Centre; 2025 overseas games by game id) + nfelo ratings/hfa_pts.
theories.effect_size: Point estimate 0.96 pts vs 2.0 for regular home games (-1.0), CI width ~7 pts.
theories.expected_impact: Negligible on aggregate MAE (~5 games/season); removes up to +/-3 pt noise in individual international/Super Bowl lines.
theories.uncertainty: SE ~1.9 pts on the international edge; OOS n=22.
theories.caveats: Rating-adjusted edge relies on nfelo Elo; 6 pre-2020 international games lack nfelo rows. 2025 neutral games carry the home team's own stadium in the nflverse file, so venue was assigned by game id.

theories.hypothesis: Divisional games have smaller HFA and more compressed margins than non-divisional games (and the market/model should shrink the spread accordingly).
theories.method: div_game flag on REG non-neutral games. Rating-adjusted HFA, market-implied HFA, market residual, |margin|, SD(margin), market MAE and favourite cover rate by div in full/fit/test windows with Welch tests and binomial CIs. OLS margin ~ rating_dif*div + season FE and margin ~ spread_line*div (slope interaction = compression) fit 2009-2021, described on 2022-25. OOS 2022-25: constant-HFA spread vs div-specific HFA vs div HFA + slope compression (fit-window params), plus nfelo close line by div. Secondary: market total residual by div (fit/test, season FE, season-by-season sign count) because div games looked lower scoring.
theories.metric: Div vs non-div HFA difference (pts), rating-slope x div interaction, OOS MAE/bias by div, favourite cover rate; secondary: market total residual gap
theories.result: HFA div vs non-div: full 1.85 vs 2.36 (diff -0.51, p=0.25, n=1412/2394); fit -0.77 (p=0.14); test +0.16 (p=0.84) -> sign flips. Compression: rating slope x div +0.02 (se 0.08, p=0.79); market slope x div +0.08 (p=0.34) fit, -0.13 (p=0.34) test; SD(margin) 14.4 vs 14.6; mean |margin| 11.35 vs 11.54 (p=0.55). Favourite cover in div games 0.495 fit, 0.468 [0.417,0.520] test vs 0.481/0.516 non-div - no edge; market MAE 9.87 vs 10.27 (p=0.15). OOS: applying fit-window div-specific HFA moves bias the wrong way (div +0.54, non-div -0.39) with MAE 9.531 vs 9.571 (div) and 9.941 vs 9.921 (non-div) - a wash. nfelo applies div_game_mod = -1.05 pts against the home team in every div game; its close line is biased +0.77 (se 0.62) toward the away side in div games OOS vs +0.27 non-div, i.e., the mod is not supported (n.s.). Secondary totals finding: div games score 1.86 pts less (fit raw gap -1.98, test -1.48) while the market total gap is only -0.44; market total residual gap div minus non-div = -1.57 (se 0.50, p=0.002) in fit, -0.90 (se 0.83, p=0.28) in test, negative in 13 of 17 seasons and 3 of 4 test seasons; div-game under rate 0.535 fit / 0.517 test; shifting market totals by the fit coefficient leaves OOS totals MAE unchanged (10.237 -> 10.236).
theories.recommendation: Spread: keep as is - no divisional HFA reduction or margin compression; the data do not support nfelo's -1.05 pt div mod either, but that lives inside nfelo and is not significant enough to counter-adjust. Totals (secondary, MED-LOW confidence): divisional games are ~1.5-2 pts lower scoring and the market prices less than half of it; add a divisional adjustment to the model total (not the spread).
theories.parameter_change: Spread: none. Totals engine: model_total += (-1.0 if div_game else +0.5) applied before pace/weather adjustments (mean-preserving at the ~36% div share; magnitude = roughly half the raw gap, matching the fit/test market-residual gaps of -1.6/-0.9).
theories.data_used: games div_game, spread_line, total_line, result 2009-2025 REG non-neutral + nfelo ratings, div_game_mod and close line.
theories.effect_size: Div HFA difference -0.5 pts (se ~0.45), interaction +0.02; totals: raw gap -1.86 pts, unexplained-by-market gap -1.42 (se across seasons 0.48).
theories.expected_impact: Spread: zero. Totals: small - the adjustment is on ~36% of games at 1 pt, likely worth <0.05 MAE points, but reduces a directional bias that survived 13/17 seasons.
theories.uncertainty: Totals test-window gap has p=0.28 (se 0.83); the 2024 season went the other way (+2.6).
theories.caveats: The totals adjustment is outside the HFA remit and should be reconciled with the totals expert; it assumes the rating-sum term in the totals engine does not already encode divisional familiarity (untestable without PFF/Cole history).

experts.summary: Bottom line for HFA in ORIGINATOR: the realized league HFA is ~2.0 points (2021-25: 1.98, CI 1.29-2.67; 2022-25: 2.13, median 1.37), down from ~2.7 in 2009-13, and the market prices ~1.55 with no exploitable home bias (2022-25 residual +0.58 +/- 0.38, home cover 49.8%). Out of sample, any constant between 1.5 and 2.0 is equally good (MAE 9.76-9.78, differences inside bootstrap CIs) and 2.5+ is significantly worse (+0.04 to +0.10 MAE, CI excludes 0); nfelo's per-game site HFA (SD 0.95 pts) adds nothing (+0.019, CI [-0.04,+0.08]) and its team-level variation has a 0.02-0.15 slope on realized outcomes in 2021-25, versus 0.67-0.94 in the seasons it was presumably fit on. Team-specific HFA after empirical-Bayes shrinkage (tau 0.67 pts, shrink factor 0.18) does not replicate (team corr r=0.21, OOS MAE diff +0.002); only Denver leans consistently positive (+2.0, p=0.10; market prices +0.6-1.3). Slot effects (SNF/MNF/TNF/SAT) reverse sign between windows and the market shows no slot bias; Week 1 is consistently ~1 pt lower but not significant (p=0.16). International games (n=48 rated): designated-home edge 0.96, CI [-2.6, 4.7], market prices 0.5 - inconclusive, spec defaults are fine, but nfelo's hfa is non-zero in 34/55 neutral games. Divisional games show no HFA reduction or margin compression OOS (nfelo's -1.05 div mod is unsupported), but they are ~1.9 pts lower scoring with the market pricing only 0.4 of it (residual gap -1.57 fit p=0.002, -0.90 test p=0.28, negative 13/17 seasons). What I would change first, in order: (1) replace the nfelo per-game (hfa_mod + home_time_advantage_mod)/25 in the PFF/Cole paths with a constant 1.75 (no dome split, drop the time-zone add-on which double counts and has no realized effect) - HIGH confidence, tiny MAE gain but removes ~1 pt SD of noise from 54% of the blend; (2) hard-override HFA at location == Neutral to 0.75 international / 0.0 domestic and Super Bowl regardless of nfelo - LOW-n but strictly a noise removal; (3) add a divisional totals adjustment (-1.0 div / +0.5 non-div) - MED, coordinate with the totals expert; (4) nothing for primetime, Week 1, or site-specific HFA; optionally mirror the market's Denver premium (+0.75) but do not build a team HFA table. All numbers come from the scripts in /home/user/originator-2026-w01/research/experts/hfa/ (run_all.sh re-runs them); ratings series is nfelo Elo throughout because no PFF or Cole history exists locally.

theories.hypothesis: 25 Elo per point is the wrong nfelo->margin scale, and/or the mapping is non-linear for big favorites (|spread|>7, >10) so ratings over/under-project blowouts.
theories.method: Built proj = -nfelo_dif_base/25 (nfelo's pre-regression Elo margin incl. HFA/site/QB/bye mods; verified decomposition nfelo_dif_base == elo_dif + hfa_mod + home_net_qb_mod on 100% of REG rows). OLS and median (quantile) regression of realized margin on proj, by era and pooled, HC1 SEs; component regression margin ~ elo_dif_pts + hfa_pts + qb_pts (REG only); calibration bins of projected favorite size (mean/median realized, cover rate, bootstrap CI) for nfelo, nfelo's own mapping, and the market; piecewise hinge regression at 7 and 10; OOS 2022-25 MAE of scale candidates fit on <=2021 (OLS scale, median scale, piecewise OLS/median) plus fixed 26/27/28/30 Elo/pt and nfelo's own ~27/pt mapping, paired bootstrap vs the 25/pt baseline; rolling-origin 2013-25.
theories.data_used: nfelo_games.csv (starting Elo, mods, nfelo_dif_base) joined to games_1999_2025.csv results on normalized game id, 2009-2025, 4310 games (4114 REG + 196 POST); nfelo_scored_individual_games.csv for nfelo's own unregressed line. Rating series = nfelo Elo (no PFF/Cole history exists).
theories.metric: OLS/median slope b (25 Elo/pt <=> b=1; implied Elo/pt = 25/b); hinge coefficients; bin ratio realized/projected; OOS MAE 2022-25 (n=1139) paired vs baseline
theories.result: Scale: pooled OLS b=1.035 [0.974,1.097] -> 24.1 Elo/pt; median-regression b=0.959 [0.886,1.033] -> 26.1 Elo/pt; train<=2021 OLS 1.038 [0.967,1.109], median 0.965 [0.876,1.053]. By era OLS 0.96-1.07 and median 0.92-1.01, every CI contains 1. Components (REG n=4114): elo_dif 1.037 (SE .038), HFA 0.913 (SE .088), QB 1.273 (SE .116). Non-linearity: train hinge7 p=0.85, hinge10 p=0.77; calibration bins all seasons: favorites 7-10 realized/projected 0.984, 10-14 1.033, 14+ 1.005 (market: 1.129/1.080/1.003); 2022-25 bin 10-14 n=95 ratio 0.916 with CI [7.9,13.4] around proj 11.65 (n.s.). 2022-25 hinges are significant but opposite-signed (b7=-1.71, b10=+2.92) and absent in train: noise. OOS 2022-25 MAE: 25/pt baseline 9.774; median scale 25.9/pt 9.766 (dMAE -0.008 [-0.021,0.005] p=0.20); fixed 27 9.761 (-0.013 [-0.039,0.015] p=0.32); fixed 28 9.760; piecewise-median 9.749 (-0.025 [-0.055,0.007] p=0.105); OLS 24.1/pt 9.785 (+0.012, p=0.08); market 9.536 (-0.238 [-0.364,-0.119]). Rolling-origin 2013-25 n=3397: OLS-scaled +0.013 [0.002,0.025] p=0.026 (worse), fixed 27 -0.006 [-0.021,0.010] p=0.45.
theories.effect_size: Any alternative scale within 24-28 Elo/pt moves OOS MAE by <=0.025 pts (<0.3%); no bin shows a blowout bias beyond +/-3% of projection with CIs spanning 1.0.
theories.uncertainty: 95% CIs on slopes cover 1.0 in every era; paired bootstrap CIs on all OOS dMAE include 0 except OLS-scaling which is significantly worse in rolling-origin.
theories.recommendation: Keep 25 Elo per point and keep the mapping linear. Do not add a big-favorite shrink/expand: the 7-10, 10-14 and 14+ bins are calibrated (ratios 0.98-1.03) and hinge terms are not stable across eras. If the engine ever wants an MAE-optimal (median) rather than RMSE-optimal scale, 26 Elo/pt is the defensible value, but the OOS gain (-0.008 MAE) is not distinguishable from zero.
theories.parameter_change: keep as is: ELO_PER_POINT = 25; no piecewise/hinge terms.
theories.caveats: nfelo Elo is the only rating series available; nfelo's own published mapping is ~27 Elo/pt (reconstructed from nfelo_unregressed_se, median 27.0, IQR 26.4-27.6) and performs identically OOS (9.765 vs 9.774). The 2022-25 window shows a home-side bias in both market (+0.68, p=0.066) and nfelo (+0.43, p=0.26) that is not a scale issue (05_bias_check.py).
theories.expected_impact: None from a change; value is confirming the existing constant.

theories.hypothesis: A market-blind origin number loses materially vs the closing line, and a shrinkage weight w in w*nfelo + (1-w)*market minimizes OOS MAE at some w well below 1 (informational: spec forbids market inputs).
theories.method: MAE/RMSE by period for: nflverse close (benchmark), nfelo-file close, nfelo published regressed close, nfelo unregressed at 25/pt (nfelo_lin), nfelo's own unregressed mapping, 538 qbelo; paired bootstrap dMAE vs close. Shrinkage: grid w in [0,1] on train<=2021, evaluated on 2022-25; OLS of market error on (mkt - engine) giving w with HC1 CI; rolling-origin w (fit on seasons < t) pooled 2013-25; engine-only blend nfelo/qbelo; ATS of engine side vs close by disagreement threshold with binomial CIs. Addendum (06): scored historic_projected_spreads.csv's own pre-regression and published lines (live nfelo v3, 2021-25) against nflverse close, and read nfelo's own market_regression_factor.
theories.data_used: nfelo_games.csv + games_1999_2025.csv (4310 games 2009-25; test 2022-25 n=1139), nfelo_scored_individual_games.csv (qbelo line, unregressed SE), historic_projected_spreads.csv (1326 joined games 2021-25). Benchmark = nflverse spread_line; nfelo's market column has sign errors (e.g. 2020_01_ARI_SF +7.5 vs -7.0) and the historic file's 'close' is a mid-week snapshot (equals the true close in 41% of games).
theories.metric: MAE vs results (paired bootstrap dMAE vs close), optimal blend weight w, ATS vs close
theories.result: 2022-25 (n=1139): market 9.536; nfelo published regressed 9.601 (+0.065 [0.004,0.126] p=0.036); nfelo unregressed 25/pt 9.774 (+0.238 [0.119,0.364] p<0.001); nfelo own mapping 9.765 (+0.229); qbelo 10.017 (+0.481 [0.308,0.657]). All 2009-25 (n=4310): unregressed +0.123 [0.052,0.190]. Historic file 2022-25 (n=1076): live pre-regression +0.297 [0.155,0.442], published regressed +0.090 [0.006,0.175] p=0.037 (nfelo's regressed line was better than the close in-sample <=2021, -0.040 p=0.035, but not OOS). Mean |nfelo_unreg - close| = 1.71 pts (test). Shrinkage: train-opt w=0.25 (train MAE 10.265 vs market 10.279); applied to test: 9.558 vs market 9.536 (+0.022 [-0.009,0.056] p=0.18); test in-sample optimum w=0.00; OLS w: train 0.418+/-0.198, all 0.291+/-0.169, test -0.12+/-0.32; rolling-origin w 0.08-0.36, pooled blend MAE 9.910 vs market 9.911 (dMAE -0.001 [-0.020,0.019]). Test cost of engine weight: w=0.1 +0.006, 0.2 +0.016, 0.3 +0.030, 0.5 +0.071, 1.0 +0.238. nfelo's own engine weight (1 - market_regression_factor) fell 0.41 (2021) -> 0.31 -> 0.29 -> 0.20 -> 0.15 (2025). ATS engine side vs close, 2022-25: 0.495-0.515 at all thresholds (>=4.5: 23-22); 2009-25: 0.525 [0.508,0.541] p=0.004 at >=0.5, 0.563 [0.495,0.629] n=222 p=0.07 at >=4.5. Engine-only blend nfelo 0.80/qbelo 0.20 (train-opt): test 9.784 vs nfelo alone 9.774 (no gain).
theories.effect_size: Market-blind nfelo number is 0.24 MAE (2.5%) worse than the close OOS; the optimal engine weight vs the close is ~0.2-0.3 historically and ~0 in 2022-25.
theories.uncertainty: Loss vs close: CI [0.119,0.364], p<0.001. w: 95% CI on OLS w spans roughly 0.1-0.5 pooled; 2022-25 CI includes 0 and excludes anything above ~0.2.
theories.recommendation: No formula change (spec forbids market inputs). Use the number to calibrate expectations and confidence tags: an origin number sits ~1.7 pts from the close on average, is ~0.24 MAE worse than it, and has shown no ATS edge vs the close since 2022 (55.6% only at |gap|>=4.5 over 2009-25, n=222, INCONCLUSIVE). A 'HIGH' confidence tag based on inter-engine SD<=1.2 should not be read as beating the close; if the desk ever compares to the market, treat the engine as worth ~20-25% of a market-blended number (nfelo itself now uses 15-30%).
theories.parameter_change: keep as is (no market term). Informational constant: engine weight vs close w_engine ~= 0.25 (train), ~0 in 2022-25.
theories.caveats: nfelo's published 'close' line is itself ~73% regressed to the market, so it is not a market-blind benchmark. qbelo is a second Elo engine, not independent information like PFF/Cole; blending it with nfelo adds nothing, which says little about PFF/Cole weights.
theories.expected_impact: Zero on the number; prevents over-claiming edge in confidence tags.

theories.hypothesis: The structural clamp (pull PFF spread to within 4.5 of nfelo) is sensible because large inter-engine disagreements predict that the deviating engine is wrong.
theories.method: No PFF history exists, so two proxies. Proxy A (engine vs engine): X = FiveThirtyEight qbelo closing line, Y = nfelo_lin. Within |X-Y| bins, OLS of (margin + Y) on -(X-Y) gives the optimal weight beta on the deviating engine; share of games X is closer; interaction test with (X-Y)*|X-Y|. Clamp backtest on a blend 0.541*nfelo + 0.459*X (ORIGINATOR nfelo:PFF weights renormalised) with hard clamp k in {2,3,4.5,6,8} and soft clamp, paired bootstrap vs no-clamp, on 2022-25 and all seasons; role swap (clamp nfelo to qbelo); symmetric clamp to midpoint; rolling-origin choice of k. Proxy B (engine vs market): X = nfelo_lin, Y = close, same bin analysis.
theories.data_used: nfelo_games.csv + nfelo_scored_individual_games.csv (qbelo line, aligned row-for-row) + games results; 4310 games 2009-25, test 2022-25 n=1139; games with |qbelo-nfelo|>4.5: 228 (110 in test).
theories.metric: beta (optimal weight on deviating engine) by disagreement bin; paired dMAE of clamped vs unclamped blend
theories.result: Proxy A, |gap|>=4.5: beta on qbelo = -0.03 [-0.32,0.26] all (n=228), +0.36 [-0.04,0.75] train (n=118), -0.38 [-0.78,0.02] test (n=110) - unstable; qbelo closer to result in 41.7% (p=0.014); qbelo MAE 11.18 vs nfelo 10.19 in that bin. beta is ~0.1-0.15 in every bin (qbelo adds little anywhere); gap*|gap| interaction p=0.67 (all), 0.12 (train), 0.08 (test, opposite sign). Clamp backtest (qbelo pulled to nfelo+/-k): test k=4.5 dMAE -0.019 [-0.038,-0.001] p=0.063; all seasons -0.003 [-0.010,0.003] p=0.31; k=3 test -0.034, k=2 test -0.042 but clamps 41% of games; rolling-origin k=4.5 -0.006 [-0.013,0.002] p=0.13 (rolling pick chose 'no clamp' 2014-21, k=2 2022-25). Role swap (nfelo pulled to qbelo+/-4.5): test +0.032 [0.011,0.055] p=0.005, all +0.008 [0.001,0.016]. Symmetric midpoint clamp k=4.5: +0.002. Blend with qbelo (9.827) is worse than nfelo alone (9.774) in test. Proxy B, |nfelo-close|>=4.5 (n=225): beta on engine 0.20 [-0.09,0.49], engine closer 43.1% (p=0.045); interaction b1=-0.068+/-0.051 p=0.009 pooled (optimal engine weight falls as the gap to the market grows), not significant in 2022-25 (n=46).
theories.effect_size: <=0.02 MAE either direction; the clamp's sign is set by which engine is more accurate, not by disagreement size.
theories.uncertainty: All clamp CIs at k=4.5 include or touch 0; beta in the >4.5 bin has CI width ~0.6 and flips sign between train and test.
theories.recommendation: Keep the clamp only as cheap insurance and make its anchor conditional: pull the engine with the HIGHER recent error toward the one with the lower error (currently PFF -> nfelo is fine only if nfelo backtests better than PFF over the last 3 seasons; if PFF is better, the clamp costs ~0.03 MAE OOS as the role swap shows). Threshold 4.5 is not distinguishable from 3 or 6 (all within 0.02 MAE); do not tune it. The real lever is the engine weight, which should be set by rolling backtest, not by a clamp.
theories.parameter_change: keep as is (k=4.5, hard clamp) with one rule added: anchor = engine with lower trailing-3-season MAE; if PFF beats nfelo, clamp nfelo to PFF+/-4.5 instead (or drop the clamp).
theories.caveats: qbelo is a weaker, correlated Elo engine (corr 0.92 with nfelo), not a PFF proxy; only 5.3% of games exceed the 4.5 gap so n is small; against the market, large gaps do predict engine error, but that reference is forbidden by spec.
theories.expected_impact: +/-0.02 MAE depending on relative engine accuracy.

theories.hypothesis: nfelo's QB adjustment (home_net_qb_mod = home_538_qb_adj - away_538_qb_adj, in Elo) adds out-of-sample accuracy beyond base Elo + HFA.
theories.method: Compare nfelo_lin (with QB) against nfelo_noqb = nfelo_lin + qb_pts (QB term removed, exact for playoff rows too); paired bootstrap dMAE by period, by |qb| size, RMSE, gap to close; OLS margin ~ (-nfelo_noqb) + qb_pts by era (coefficient 1 = correctly scaled); market-residual regressions err_mkt ~ qb_pts and partial given (mkt - nfelo_noqb); optimal multiplier k on the QB term fit on <=2021 by MAE and rolling-origin, evaluated OOS; ATS vs close with/without QB and a QB-side-only signal.
theories.data_used: nfelo_games.csv (home_net_qb_mod, verified == home_538_qb_adj - away_538_qb_adj, 100% coverage 2009-25 incl. post-538 seasons) + games results; 4310 games, test 2022-25 n=1139; mean |qb| = 1.15 pts, 23% of games >=1.5, 9.5% >=3.
theories.metric: paired dMAE with vs without QB term (OOS), coefficient on qb_pts, optimal multiplier k, ATS vs close
theories.result: No parameters fitted, so every window is OOS for this comparison: 2022-25 with QB 9.774 vs without 9.887, dMAE -0.113 [-0.209,-0.019] p=0.019 (RMSE 12.68 vs 12.86); all 2009-25 -0.108 [-0.159,-0.059] p<0.001; rolling pooled 2013-25 (n=3397) -0.120 [-0.177,-0.057]; 2023-25 post-538 era (n=855) -0.153 [-0.252,-0.048] p=0.003. Large adjustments: |qb|>=1.5 test n=298 -0.423 [-0.752,-0.104]; |qb|>=2 test n=199 -0.547 [-1.008,-0.072]; |qb|>=3 all n=410 -0.724 [-1.146,-0.300]. Gap to close shrinks 2.18 -> 1.71 pts. Coefficient on QB term: 1.24 [1.02,1.46] all, 1.32 [0.86,1.78] test, 0.88 [0.46,1.31] in 2019-21. Optimal multiplier: train k=1.1 -> test 9.771 vs 9.774 at k=1.0 (rolling +0.004 [-0.004,0.013], no gain); test grid flat 1.0-1.4 (9.774-9.769). Market already prices it: err_mkt on qb_pts 0.25 (p=0.02) pooled but 2022-25 partial 0.04 (p=0.90). ATS vs close: with QB 0.524 [0.509,0.539] vs without 0.509 (2009-25); 2022-25 0.500 vs 0.498; QB-side-only signal 0.513 (p=0.42).
theories.effect_size: -0.11 MAE overall, -0.4 to -0.7 MAE in games with a >=1.5-3 pt QB adjustment; QB term is scaled correctly (coef ~1.0-1.3).
theories.uncertainty: CIs exclude zero in every window (test p=0.019, pooled p<0.001); multiplier CI ~[1.0,1.5] with no OOS MAE difference across it.
theories.recommendation: Keep nfelo's QB adjustment at full weight (multiplier 1.0; 1.1-1.2 is statistically equivalent, do not tune). It is necessary for a market-blind number (-0.11 MAE, up to -0.7 in backup-QB games) even though it yields no edge vs the close, which already prices QB changes fully since 2022. This also validates the section-5 QB starter->backup range: nfelo's adjustments of 2-4.5 pts are realized at coefficient ~1.0-1.3, i.e. not overstated.
theories.parameter_change: keep as is: QB_MOD_MULTIPLIER = 1.0 (points = home_net_qb_mod/25).
theories.caveats: The adjustment is nfelo's/538's QB Elo, not a PFF or Cole QB table; pre-2023 values come from 538, 2023+ from nfelo's replacement, and the effect holds in both eras.
theories.expected_impact: Removing it would cost ~0.11 MAE; no change recommended.

experts.summary:
Scripts (all re-runnable, print every number cited): /home/user/originator-2026-w01/research/experts/calibration/{common.py, 01_scale_by_era.py, 02_shrinkage.py, 03_clamp.py, 04_qb_adj.py, 05_bias_check.py, 06_historic_file_check.py}. Data: nfelo_games.csv + nflverse results 2009-25 (4310 games; test 2022-25 n=1139), nfelo scored file for the 538 qbelo line and nfelo's own unregressed line, historic_projected_spreads.csv for the live-version check. Rating series is nfelo Elo throughout (no PFF/Cole history exists). Benchmark is nflverse -spread_line; sign check corr(mkt, margin) = -0.435.

Bottom line: the calibration chain of the current v5 build passes every test, so my first-order recommendation is to change nothing in it. (1) 25 Elo/pt is correct: OLS slope 1.035 [0.974,1.097] (24.1/pt) and median slope 0.959 [0.886,1.033] (26.1/pt) bracket it in every era; big-favorite bins are calibrated (7-10: 0.98, 10-14: 1.03, 14+: 1.00), hinge terms are unstable, and no alternative scale/piecewise beats the baseline OOS by more than 0.025 MAE (all CIs include 0). (2) The QB adjustment is worth keeping at multiplier 1.0: -0.113 MAE OOS 2022-25 (p=0.019), -0.12 rolling 2013-25 (p<0.001), -0.55 in games with a >=2-pt adjustment; coefficient on the term 1.24 [1.02,1.46]. (3) The 4.5 clamp is INCONCLUSIVE: it moves MAE by <=0.02 and its sign is entirely determined by which engine is more accurate (clamping the weaker qbelo to nfelo: -0.019, p=0.06; clamping nfelo to qbelo: +0.032, p=0.005; symmetric clamp: 0). Keep k=4.5 but anchor the clamp on whichever engine has the lower trailing 3-season MAE, and set engine weights by backtest rather than relying on the clamp.

The most useful number for the panel is from theory 2: a market-blind nfelo number is 0.238 MAE [0.119,0.364] worse than the close in 2022-25 (2.5%), sits 1.7 pts from it on average, and has no ATS edge since 2022 (49.5-51.5% at every disagreement threshold; 52.5% over 2009-25). The MAE-optimal engine weight vs the close is ~0.25 on <=2021 and ~0 on 2022-25 (nfelo itself now regresses 85% to market). Even nfelo's published regressed line no longer beats the close OOS (+0.065, p=0.036). Implication: confidence tags built on inter-engine SD (<=1.2 = HIGH) describe engine agreement, not edge, and should be labeled as such. A second Elo-style engine adds nothing to nfelo (blend 9.784 vs 9.774), so the blend only earns its keep if PFF/Cole carry information nfelo lacks; that should be verified once PFF/Cole history exists.

Data caveats for other experts: kit.py's hfa_pts = (hfa_mod + home_time_advantage_mod)/25 double counts the time-zone mod because hfa_mod already contains it (hfa_mod = hfa_base + surface + time + div + bye mods, verified from raw rows); nfelo_games' market column has sign errors in a handful of games; historic_projected_spreads.csv's 'home_line_close' is a mid-week snapshot (matches the true close in 41% of games) and its Elo is a different nfelo version (mean 1.1-pt difference from the backfilled series). Side observation (05_bias_check.py, not significant): home teams beat the close by +0.68 ppg in 2022-25 (p=0.066) and nfelo by +0.43 (p=0.26); worth a look by the HFA expert.

theories.hypothesis: The engine's implied total = 46.0 + 0.35*(home_pts_vs_avg + away_pts_vs_avg) is calibrated: combined Elo strength predicts totals with slope ~0.35 around a fixed 46.0 league level.
theories.method: OLS total_pts ~ a + b*elo_sum (nfelo starting Elo, 25 Elo = 1 pt) on REG games 2009-2021 (HC1 SE, with and without season FE), tested 2022-2025; rolling-origin b for 2019-2025; market's own slope (mkt_total ~ elo_sum); market-residual regression to test whether the market already prices elo_sum; OOS MAE/bias of spec vs alternatives with paired bootstrap CI vs the closing total.
theories.metric: OOS MAE vs closing total (test n=1087, fit n=3027); slope b with 95% CI; bias
theories.result: b = 0.285 (se 0.049, 95% CI 0.19-0.38) on 2009-2021; rolling-origin b stable 0.27-0.29; the MARKET's own slope is 0.274. corr(elo_sum,total)=+0.11 (p=1e-9) so combined strength is predictive but explains only 1.2% of variance; market residual slope on elo_sum = +0.007 (p=0.88) -> fully priced. OOS 2022-25: spec 46.0+0.35*elo MAE 10.820, bias +1.32 pts (constant is the problem: 2022-23 realized 43.8/43.5); lg_prev+0.28*elo MAE 10.709 bias +0.07; lg_blend+0.28*elo MAE 10.658 bias +0.01; market 10.189. Per-season bias of constant 46: 2020 -3.5, 2022 +2.3, 2023 +2.6 vs lg_blend 2020 -1.9, 2022 +1.2, 2023 +0.3. Curvature (elo_sum^2 p=0.06) and mismatch |elo_dif| (p=0.70) add nothing; home/away asymmetry (0.35 vs 0.22) not significant.
theories.recommendation: Keep the additive combined-strength form but change both constants: slope 0.35 -> 0.28 (point estimate; 0.35 is inside the CI but the market and every rolling fit sit at 0.27-0.29) and replace the fixed 46.0 with a league prior = prior-season REG mean total (46.0 for 2026 = 2025 mean 45.96), blended in-season: LG = (128*prior + n*season_to_date_mean)/(128+n), n = league games already played. This removes the +1.3 pt OOS bias (dMAE -0.16).
theories.parameter_change: implied_total = LG + 0.28*(rating_home + rating_away) where LG = (128*L_prev + n*L_ytd)/(128+n); L_prev = prior-season REG mean total; b 0.35 -> 0.28.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv (REG, scored, closing total_line), nfelo_games.csv starting_nfelo_home/away; PFF/Cole have no history so nfelo Elo is the only rating series tested
theories.expected_impact: -0.16 MAE and removal of a +1.3 pt level bias in 2022-25; no O/U edge vs market either way (~50%)
theories.uncertainty: slope CI 0.19-0.38; the league-prior improvement is driven by the level, not the slope
theories.caveats: Only nfelo Elo tested; if PFF/Cole ratings are on a different points scale the 0.28 applies to the points-vs-average conversion, not raw ratings. lg_blend needs K=128 to avoid over-reacting to early-season noise (2021 after COVID-2020 still carried +2.3 bias for half a season).

theories.hypothesis: Rolling points-for / points-against (offense/defense proxies from nflverse scores) add information beyond combined Elo for totals, and offense and defense need separate weights.
theories.method: Leak-free team scoring rates: blend of prior-season mean and season-to-date mean (K_team chosen on a validation window 2015-2021 with fit <=2014; K=1 selected, K=1..6 within 0.03 MAE). OLS of (total - lg_blend) on pf_dev = (h_pf + a_pf - league), pa_dev = (h_pa + a_pa - league), elo_sum, fit 2009-2021, test 2022-2025; Wald test pf_dev = pa_dev; single game-total term (gt_dev) alternative; drop-one OOS ablation; market-residual regressions.
theories.metric: OOS MAE vs closing total; coefficient CIs; Wald p
theories.result: pf_dev +0.340 (se 0.065), pa_dev +0.272 (se 0.057): difference +0.07, p=0.51 -> separate offense/defense weights are NOT needed; a single 'both teams' game-total term (gt_dev +0.304, se 0.033) gives identical OOS MAE (10.295 vs 10.288). But the scoring proxies DO add beyond Elo: OOS MAE L+E 10.657 -> L+E+S 10.521 (K=1) ; drop-one of pf/pa from the full model +0.11-0.13 MAE. Once pf/pa and QB are in, the Elo term shrinks to +0.105 (se 0.092, p=0.25); dropping Elo entirely costs only +0.02 MAE. Market residual does not load on pf/pa (p=0.08-0.57), i.e. the market already knows them. Prior-season-only pf/pa is much weaker (OOS 10.777).
theories.recommendation: Add a team scoring-rate term to the total; do NOT split into offense and defense coefficients (use one weight ~0.30 on the sum of both teams' points-for and points-against deviations from league average, or 0.34/0.27 if you want the split). Update the rates in-season with the prior season counting as ~1-3 games.
theories.parameter_change: total += 0.34*(h_pf + a_pf - 2*lgppg) + 0.27*(h_pa + a_pa - 2*lgppg) [or 0.30*(sum of all four - 4*lgppg)], lgppg = LG/2; team rate = (K*prior_season_mean + gp*season_to_date_mean)/(K+gp), K=1..3; Elo coefficient drops to 0.10 when this term is present.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv scores (rolling, leak-free), nfelo Elo
theories.effect_size: -0.14 to -0.27 OOS MAE vs Elo-only (10.664 -> 10.388 with QB, 10.401 without)
theories.expected_impact: closes ~half the gap to the market total
theories.uncertainty: K_team: validation picked 1, test mildly prefers 3-6 (10.288 vs 10.262); differences within noise
theories.caveats: Raw PF/PA are not opponent-adjusted; Elo carries the opponent adjustment, which is why both terms are kept.

theories.hypothesis: A simple market-free totals model from local data (league prior, Elo, rolling PF/PA, QB adj, roof, div, rest, week, temp/wind, pace from pbp) can approach the closing total's MAE; identify which features matter.
theories.method: OLS of (total - lg_blend) on feature groups, fit 2009-2021 REG (n=3027), test 2022-2025 REG (n=1087); cumulative and drop-one ablations; paired bootstrap CI of MAE difference vs market; O/U record vs market; rolling-origin by season; regression of market error on (model - market) and optimal blend weight; pace (plays, sec/play, no-huddle, pass rate, EPA) on the pbp subset (train 2009-2019 n=2498, test 2023-2025 n=815).
theories.metric: OOS MAE vs closing total; dMAE vs market with 95% bootstrap CI; O/U vs market
theories.result: Final formula V3 (LG + 0.10*elo_sum + 0.34*pf_dev + 0.27*pa_dev + 0.72*qb_sum - 1.36*div + ENV table): OOS MAE 10.288 vs market 10.189, dMAE +0.099 [-0.038, +0.235] -> statistically indistinguishable from the market; spec formula 10.820. Feature value (drop-one OOS): QB adj +0.11 to +0.13, PF/PA +0.11 to +0.14, ENV table +0.10 [0.01,0.19], Elo +0.01 to +0.02, div small; rest/bye/short-week/week/late-season/neutral/grass add NOTHING (dropping the group improves MAE 0.03); pace group HURTS OOS (+0.045), plays-per-game 0.00, EPA off/def -0.03 only. No information beyond the market: (total-mkt) ~ (model-mkt) slope 0.20 (p=0.21); optimal blend weight on model 0.10-0.15; O/U vs market 547-532 (50.7%), |diff|>=4 pts 74-61 (54.8%, n=137, n.s.). Per season OOS: 2022 10.45/10.40, 2023 10.17/10.24, 2024 9.83/9.73, 2025 10.71/10.39 (model/market).
theories.recommendation: Adopt V3 as the originator total. Drop the pace adjustment (no OOS value from pbp pace 2009-2019/2023-25). Do not add rest/bye/week terms for totals. Treat the number as a fair-pricing tool, not an edge: expect ~0.1 pt worse MAE than the close and ~50% O/U vs close.
theories.parameter_change: total = LG + 0.10*elo_sum + 0.34*pf_dev + 0.27*pa_dev + 0.72*qb_sum - 1.36*div_game + ENV(roof, wind, temp); qb_sum = (home_538_qb_adj + away_538_qb_adj)/25 from nfelo_games; remove pace adj +/-1..2.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv, nfelo_games.csv (Elo, 538 QB adj), pbp nflscrapR 2009-2019 + nflfastR 2023-2025 (pace/EPA via 00_build_pace.py); precip flags 2023-25 from nflfastR weather strings
theories.expected_impact: -0.53 MAE vs current spec OOS; O/U ~50.7% vs market (no edge)
theories.uncertainty: dMAE vs market CI [-0.04, +0.24]; single-season MAE swings +/-0.3
theories.caveats: QB term uses 538/nfelo QB adjustment, not the engine's injury-only adjustment; 2022 has missing weather for 32% of outdoor games (imputed 8 mph, flagged); pbp unavailable 2020-2022 so pace tested on 2023-25 only (n=815).

theories.hypothesis: Wind lowers totals; thresholds 10/15/20/25 mph; the spec's table (15-20: -1.0, 21-30: -2..-3, 30+: -3.5..-5) is the right size.
theories.method: Outdoor REG games with OBSERVED wind/temp (no imputation). (i) market residual total - mkt_total by wind bin and linear (1999-2025 n=4835; fit 1999-2021 n=4193; test 2022-25 n=642), t-tests at 10/15/20/25. (ii) originator effect: residual of the team model WITHOUT weather (fit 2009-2021) by wind bin, linear and stepped fits, larger-n 1999-2021 version (n=4193), 3-mph resolution curve. OOS: LEAN + spec table / fitted linear / fitted step vs no-weather, paired bootstrap; windy-subset MAE.
theories.metric: mean residual by bin (se), linear slope per mph, OOS MAE change
theories.result: Market residual: 0-9 mph +1.02, 10-14 +0.06, 15-19 -1.41 (n=447), 20-24 +1.39 (n=128), 25+ -9.35 (n=40, under 82%); wind>=15: -1.34 vs +0.77 (diff -2.11, p<0.001, n=615, under 56.1%); linear -0.166/mph (p<0.001) in 1999-2021, -0.162/mph in 2022-25 (p=0.17, n=642) -> the closing total does NOT fully price wind. Team-controlled originator effect: -0.20/mph (se 0.057, 2009-21), -0.214/mph (se 0.040, 1999-2021 n=4193), -0.30/mph (se 0.13) in 2022-25; bins vs <10 mph: 10-14 -1.1, 15-19 -2.7, 20-24 -1.2 (n=119), 25+ -13.3 (n=38). Effect is roughly linear from ~7 mph up, no clean threshold. OOS 2022-25: ENV table vs no ENV dMAE -0.099 [-0.189, -0.009] (n=1087); windy test games (>=15 mph, n=60): bias +4.07 -> +1.17, MAE 10.86 -> 10.27 (market 9.53). Spec table alone: -0.015 [-0.036, +0.004] (too small).
theories.recommendation: Replace the spec's wind table with a linear -0.2 pts per mph relative to an average outdoor game (8.4 mph), or the binned equivalent; start adjusting at 10 mph, not 15. Keep 25+ at -5.0 (conservative: data say -9 to -13 but n=40).
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv wind/temp (outdoor only; 2023-25 gaps filled from nflfastR weather strings, r=0.97 agreement)
theories.effect_size: -0.20/mph team-controlled (se 0.04-0.06); market residual -0.17/mph; >=15 mph market residual -2.1 pts
theories.expected_impact: -0.10 MAE overall OOS, -0.6 MAE and -2.9 bias on windy games; market under-rate 56% at >=15 mph is the one environment where the market residual is exploitable in-sample
theories.uncertainty: 20-24 mph bin is noisy (n=128, +1.4 market residual) so the curve is not monotone bin-by-bin; test-period slope p=0.17 on n=642
theories.caveats: Wind is the game-time recorded value, not the pre-game forecast the engine will have; 2022 weather missing for 46% of outdoor games.

theories.hypothesis: Cold (<32F, <20F) and precipitation lower totals beyond wind; the spec's cold -0.5..-1.5 and rain/snow -1..-2.5 are right.
theories.method: Same samples as T3a; cold bins on market residual and team-controlled residual with wind held linear; precipitation from nflfastR weather strings 2023-2025 only (precip_strict = rain/snow/showers/sleet not hedged), Welch t-tests vs dry; OOS check of dropping each term from the ENV table.
theories.metric: mean residual (se), p-value; OOS MAE change
theories.result: Cold: <32F has NO effect after wind (team-controlled -0.02, p=0.99; market residual +1.1, p=0.34; n=199-265). <20F: team-controlled -1.3 (se 3.3, n=27 in 2009-21), -2.1 (se 2.4, 1999-2021 n=51); 2022-25 -8.4 (se 2.2, n=15). Precipitation 2023-25 outdoor: wet n=39 vs dry n=510 market residual -3.27 vs +1.18 (diff -4.45, p=0.067, under 67.6%); team-controlled wet -4.5 (se 2.3). OOS table pieces: dropping <20F term +0.009 MAE, dropping precip term +0.024 MAE (both within noise).
theories.recommendation: Drop the <32F adjustment (zero effect once wind is in). Keep a small <20F term (-1.0) and a provisional precipitation term (-1.5) pending more data; both are directionally supported but n=15-51 is far below the 150-game bar.
theories.parameter_change: cold: <32F 0 (was -0.5..-1.5 for <20F only, keep -1.0 at <20F); precipitation: -1.5 flat (was -1..-2.5) — provisional.
theories.data_used: games temp; nflfastR weather strings 2023-2025 (no precipitation field exists for 1999-2022 locally)
theories.expected_impact: ~0.01-0.02 MAE; negligible except in the handful of games affected
theories.uncertainty: n=15-51 for <20F, n=39 for precipitation
theories.caveats: Precipitation flag is a text-string proxy for 3 seasons; no snow/rain data before 2023.

theories.hypothesis: Favorites cover less in wind (compressed scoring), so spreads should be adjusted toward the underdog in wind.
theories.method: Outdoor REG games with observed wind and a non-zero closing spread (n=4818); favorite cover margin = favorite's actual margin - points laid; by wind bin, t-tests at >=15/>=20, OLS with wind x |spread| interaction, big favorites (|spread|>=7) ATS; fit <=2021 (n=4176) vs test 2022-25 (n=642); spread MAE and margin SD by wind.
theories.metric: favorite cover margin (pts), favorite ATS rate, spread MAE by wind
theories.result: Fit <=2021: wind>=15 favorite cover margin -0.75 vs +0.48 (p=0.05, n=551), fav ATS 47.9% vs 49.7%; 25+ mph fav ATS 44.7% (n=38). Test 2022-25: REVERSED, wind>=15 +2.38 vs +0.24 (n=60), fav ATS 62.7%. Interaction wind x |spread| p=0.27-0.39; big favorites in wind ATS 52.6% (n=176). Spread MAE flat across wind bins (10.3/10.3/10.3/11.6/10.3), margin SD 14.5-15.0 -> wind does not shrink margin variance.
theories.recommendation: No wind adjustment to spreads and no change to spread confidence in wind; keep as is.
theories.parameter_change: keep as is (no spread weather term).
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv closing spread_line, wind
theories.effect_size: -1.2 pts favorite cover margin at >=15 mph in-sample (p=0.05), +2.1 out-of-sample (n=60)
theories.expected_impact: none
theories.uncertainty: sign flips between periods; test n=60
theories.caveats: A -0.1/mph favorite effect cannot be excluded but is not robust enough to act on.

theories.hypothesis: Dome / closed-roof games have higher totals after controlling for the teams involved, and the effect is more than the absence of bad weather.
theories.method: Participant team-season fixed effects (one effect per team-season, shared by home and away appearances, so identification comes from the same teams playing under different roofs) on y = total - league prior, REG non-neutral 1999-2025 (n=6653), by era and fit/test; roof type split; dome vs outdoor good-weather (wind<10, temp>=50) vs mid vs bad; dome with linear wind control; market residual by roof; OOS effect of a dome term in the LEAN model and of the ENV table dome level (1.0-3.0).
theories.metric: FE coefficient (HC1 se); market residual difference; OOS MAE/bias in dome games
theories.result: Dome/closed vs outdoors with participant FE: +2.15 (se 0.52, p<0.001) all years; +1.80 (se 0.58) fit <=2021; +3.59 (se 1.15) test 2022-25; by era 1999-2010 +0.57 (n.s.), 2011-2021 +2.83; dome +2.27, closed +2.59, open-retractable +3.14 (se 1.4). vs outdoor GOOD weather: +1.47 (se 0.56, p=0.009); vs zero-wind outdoor: +0.18 (se 0.61) -> a dome is essentially 'no weather', and dome vs AVERAGE outdoor (8.4 mph) = +1.8 to +2.0; V3 fit gives +2.59 (se 0.57) vs average outdoor. Market residual dome +1.36 vs outdoors +0.44, diff +0.80 (p=0.035; test +1.01, p=0.25) -> market slightly underprices domes (over-rate 52%). Not a home-team artifact: interaction with visitor being a dome team -1.27 (se 0.87). OOS: dome level +1.0 to +2.5 in the ENV table all give MAE 10.286-10.297 (flat); dome-game bias -2.87 (no ENV) -> -0.87 (dome +2.0).
theories.recommendation: Include a roof term: dome/closed +2.0 relative to the league-average game (equivalently +2.5 vs an average-wind outdoor game, ~+1.5 vs a calm warm outdoor game); treat retractable-closed the same as fixed domes.
theories.parameter_change: ENV(dome or closed) = +2.0; outdoor base -0.5 at 8.4 mph (see T3a); no separate 'open' category.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv roof, scores, wind/temp
theories.effect_size: +2.15 pts (se 0.52) vs outdoors; +1.47 (se 0.56) vs good-weather outdoors; market residual +0.80 (p=0.035)
theories.expected_impact: removes a -2.9 pt bias in dome games; MAE effect ~0 OOS because PF/PA rates already carry part of it
theories.uncertainty: era heterogeneity (1999-2010 ~0, 2011+ ~2.8); test-period estimate +3.6 (se 1.15)
theories.caveats: Identification relies on cross-venue games (dome teams away, outdoor teams visiting domes); a first version with separate home/away FE was collinear with the dome flag and was replaced.

theories.hypothesis: A concrete replacement totals formula + environment table beats the current spec OOS and matches the closing total.
theories.method: Rounded coefficients from the 2009-2021 fit (05 re-prints the exact fit and the rounded set); evaluate V0 spec, V1 (LG+0.28*elo), V2 (V1+ENV), V3 (full) and variants OOS 2022-2025 (n=1087) with paired bootstrap vs market; per-season table 2016-2025; league-prior comparison 2010-2025 with no fitting; playoff games 2022-25 (n=52, never used); sensitivity (06) to K_team, table pieces, dome level, prior choice.
theories.metric: OOS MAE vs closing total, bias, dMAE with 95% CI, O/U vs market
theories.result: OOS 2022-25 MAE: market 10.189 | V0 spec 10.820 (bias +1.32) | V1 10.664 | V2 10.590 | V3 10.288 (bias -0.74; dMAE vs market +0.099 [-0.038, +0.235]; O/U 547-532) | V3 with single gt term 10.295 | V3 no ENV 10.388 | no QB 10.401 | no Elo 10.307. ENV table vs none -0.099 [-0.189, -0.009]. League prior inside V3: lg_blend 10.288, lg_prev 10.307, constant 46.0 10.364 (bias +0.53). Per-season V3 vs market: 2022 10.45/10.40, 2023 10.17/10.24, 2024 9.83/9.73, 2025 10.71/10.39. Playoffs 2022-25 (n=52): V3 10.15 vs market 10.19 vs spec 11.10. Error scale of V3: MAE 10.3, RMSE 13.1 (same as market). Team-total identity T/2 -/+ S/2 with market lines: MAE 7.5 home / 7.2 away, bias -0.3/-0.2 (identity fine).
theories.recommendation: Implement V3 with the ENV table. Order of value: (1) league prior + slope 0.28 (removes bias), (2) team scoring-rate + QB terms, (3) ENV table, (4) delete pace adjustment. Keep O/U expectations at ~50% vs close; the model is for pricing when no market exists, not for beating the close.
theories.parameter_change: total = LG + 0.10*elo_sum + 0.34*pf_dev + 0.27*pa_dev + 0.72*qb_sum - 1.36*div + ENV. LG = (128*L_prev + n*L_ytd)/(128+n) with L_prev = prior-season REG mean (46.0 for 2026). pf_dev = h_pf + a_pf - LG; pa_dev = h_pa + a_pa - LG; team rates = (K*prior_season + gp*ytd)/(K+gp), K=1..3. qb_sum = (home_538_qb_adj + away_538_qb_adj)/25. ENV: dome/closed +2.0; outdoor wind 0-5 +0.5 | 6-9 -0.5 | 10-14 -1.5 | 15-19 -2.5 | 20-24 -3.5 | 25+ -5.0; temp <20F -1.0; precipitation -1.5 (provisional). If only ratings are available: total = LG + 0.28*elo_sum + ENV.
theories.data_used: all of the above; sensitivity in 06_sensitivity.py; run_all.sh re-runs 00-06
theories.expected_impact: engine total within 0.1 pt MAE of the closing line without using the market
theories.uncertainty: K_team 1 vs 3-6 changes MAE by 0.02-0.03; dome level 1.5-2.5 flat; coefficients rounded from n=3027 fit
theories.caveats: PFF and Cole totals cannot be validated (no history); the 0.10 Elo weight assumes the PF/PA and QB terms are present, otherwise use 0.28. Residual -0.7 bias in 2022-25 comes from the 2022 scoring drop and the K=128 prior lag.

experts.summary:
Scripts: /home/user/originator-2026-w01/research/experts/totals/ (00_build_pace.py, common.py, 01-06 *.py, run_all.sh, *.log). Sign checks pass (corr(mkt_spread, margin) = -0.43; corr(mkt_total, total) = +0.32). Benchmark closing-total MAE 2022-25 = 10.189 (n=1087 REG).

What I would change first, in order:
1. The constant 46.0 and slope 0.35. Combined Elo strength IS predictive of totals but the fitted slope is 0.28 (CI 0.19-0.38; the market's own slope is 0.27) and a fixed 46.0 carries a +1.3 pt OOS bias (2022-23 scored 43.8/43.5). Use a league prior = prior-season mean, blended in-season with K=128 games, and b=0.28. OOS MAE 10.820 -> 10.658. The market already prices Elo fully (residual slope p=0.87), so this is about bias, not edge.
2. Add team scoring rates and a QB term. Rolling PF/PA (prior season counted as ~1-3 games vs season-to-date) and the 538/nfelo QB adjustment are the two features that matter (drop-one +0.11 to +0.14 MAE each). Offense and defense do NOT need separate weights (0.34 vs 0.27, p=0.51). With them present Elo's weight drops to 0.10. Full formula: total = LG + 0.10*elo_sum + 0.34*pf_dev + 0.27*pa_dev + 0.72*qb_sum - 1.36*div + ENV -> OOS MAE 10.288, statistically indistinguishable from the closing total (+0.10 [-0.04, +0.24]), O/U 50.7% vs close, optimal blend weight vs market only 0.10-0.15. This is the ceiling for a market-free originator with local data; pace (plays, sec/play, no-huddle, pass rate) and rest/bye/week terms add nothing OOS and should be dropped.
3. Environment table (validated, -0.10 MAE [-0.19, -0.01] OOS). Wind is linear, -0.20/mph after controlling for teams (se 0.04-0.06, n=4193), starting around 7-10 mph rather than 15; the market itself leaves -2.1 pts on the table at >=15 mph (n=615, under 56%, p<0.001) and -9 at 25+ (n=40). Table: dome/closed +2.0; outdoor 0-5 +0.5 | 6-9 -0.5 | 10-14 -1.5 | 15-19 -2.5 | 20-24 -3.5 | 25+ -5.0; <20F -1.0; <32F nothing (zero effect once wind is in); precipitation -1.5 provisional (n=39, p=0.07). Dome effect with participant team-season fixed effects is +2.15 (se 0.52) vs outdoors, +1.5 vs calm warm outdoors and ~0 vs zero-wind outdoors: a dome is 'no weather', and the market underprices it by ~0.8 (p=0.035).
4. No wind adjustment on spreads: favorites-in-wind effect is -1.2 pts in-sample (p=0.05) but +2.1 out-of-sample (n=60), and spread MAE is flat across wind bins. REJECTED.

Data caveats: only nfelo Elo has history (PFF/Cole untestable); 2022 lacks weather for 46% of outdoor games (imputed 8 mph, flagged); pbp missing 2020-22 so pace was tested on 2023-25; precipitation exists only as 2023-25 text strings.

theories.hypothesis: The favorite's share of points differs from the linear identity (home = T/2 - S/2, away = T/2 + S/2): coefficients are not 0.5/-0.5 and 0.5/+0.5, and big favorites score more (or less) than the identity implies.
theories.method: OLS of home_score / away_score / fav_score / dog_score on (S, T) with HC1 SEs, Wald tests of the identity slopes; residuals by spread bin (11 bins) and |S| bin; OOS 2022-2025 MAE of identity vs OLS-linear vs OLS with |S|, S|S|, S*T terms vs identity+train shift, paired bootstrap CIs; rolling-origin refit every season 2010-2025; modern-era (2009-2021 fit) replication.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv closing spread_line/total_line via kit.load_games (S = -spread_line, ORIGINATOR sign). Sign check corr(S, margin) = -0.426.
theories.metric: OLS slopes vs 0.5; team-total MAE vs actual score (home and away), paired bootstrap of dMAE; over-rate vs identity.
theories.result: Train 1999-2021 (n=6137): home S -0.517 (se 0.021), T +0.466 (0.025); away S +0.524 (0.020), T +0.453 (0.024). Wald test slopes = identity: p=0.27 home, p=0.07 away. Modern era 2009-2021 (n=3491): p=0.19 home, 0.73 away, 0.33 fav, 0.085 dog. Only the intercepts differ from 0 (+1.8 home, +2.5 away, i.e. the market total is under-dispersed and under by +0.7 on average, a totals matter). OOS 2022-2025 (n=1139): identity MAE 7.230 home / 7.080 away; OLS-nonlinear dMAE +0.014 [-0.006,+0.035] home, -0.027 [-0.053,-0.002] away (worse). Rolling-origin 2010-2025 pooled (n=4363): identity beats nonlinear OLS by 0.014 [0.001,0.027] home and 0.020 [0.006,0.033] away; identity best in 11/16 (home) and 14/16 (away) seasons. Bin residuals are not monotone in |S| (train r_fav: 1-3 -0.11, 3.5-6.5 +0.57, 7-9.5 +1.13, 10-13.5 +0.01, 14+ +0.10).
theories.effect_size: Slope deviations from 0.5: -0.017 (home S), -0.034 (home T), +0.024 (away S), -0.047 (away T); fitted alternatives change team-total MAE by <0.03 pts and in the wrong direction OOS.
theories.uncertainty: Wald p 0.07-0.73; OOS dMAE CIs all include 0 or favor the identity; rolling-origin paired t p=0.06-0.34 in favor of identity.
theories.recommendation: Keep the identity exactly: home = T/2 - S/2, away = T/2 + S/2 (means). No favorite/dog nonlinearity. The +0.7 average under-bias of the market total and its shrinkage (E[total|T] ~ 4.2 + 0.92 T) are for the totals expert; they flow into team totals automatically through T.
theories.parameter_change: keep as is (allocation coefficients 0.5/-0.5 and 0.5/+0.5, intercept 0)
theories.caveats: Benchmark is the identity applied to the market close (no market team totals in the kit). Team-score residual SD ~9 pts, so effects <0.3 pts are undetectable even with n=7k.

theories.hypothesis: Team totals are bet as over/under so the fair number is the MEDIAN; team scores are right-skewed at low expected totals, so the identity (a mean) sits above the median for low team totals and should be shaded down.
theories.method: Team-game long table (14,552 rows). Skew, mean and median residual, and P(score > identity) by expected-score bin; median (quantile) regression score ~ identity vs OLS on train; OOS 2022-2025 MAE and over-rate of candidate shift rules (median-reg line, bin median table, piecewise -1/-0.5/0, flat -0.5); per-season robustness 2009-2025.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv closing lines (kit.load_games).
theories.metric: P(over identity) with binomial CI/p; MAE vs actual score with paired bootstrap.
theories.effect_size: Implied median shade <= 0.4 pts at identity 14 and ~0 above 20; not recoverable OOS.
theories.uncertainty: binomial p=0.08 pooled; direction reverses in the test period.
theories.recommendation: Keep as is. If the engine ever prices team totals below 15, at most -0.5 could be justified; no rule tested improves OOS.
theories.parameter_change: keep as is (no skew/median shade)
theories.caveats: Low-total bin is small (n=586 train, 57 test).

theories.hypothesis: At a fixed spread the home team scores more of the total than the identity implies (home share > (T/2 - S/2)/T), i.e. a home favorite / home dog should get a larger share than an away team with the same line.
theories.method: Algebra: r_home - r_away = market spread error, so asymmetry = half the conditional spread error. Tests: mean r_home vs r_away (non-neutral), home-share residual; OLS r_fav, r_dog, sp_err, tot_err ~ home_fav + |S| + T (train and test separately); home-fav vs away-fav residuals by |S| bin; neutral-site games; OOS home shift fit on train; spread error by era block.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv (kit.load_games), location for neutral flag.
theories.metric: Mean residual difference with 95% CI; regression coefficient on home_fav (HC1); OOS MAE.
theories.result: Train non-neutral (n=6071): r_home +0.350, r_away +0.357, difference -0.006 [-0.341,+0.329]; home share residual +0.0010 [-0.003,+0.005]. home_fav coefficient: r_fav -0.129 (se 0.268, p=0.63), r_dog +0.057 (p=0.83), sp_err -0.007 (p=0.99). Test 2022-2025 (n=1111): r_fav home_fav +1.244 (p=0.028) but it is a totals effect (tot_err +1.391, p=0.086; sp_err +0.502, p=0.52) and the spread error by era flips sign (+0.40, -0.30, +0.32, -0.52, +0.66). Neutral games (n=94): r_home -0.61, r_away -0.50. OOS home shift fit on train k=-0.003 -> zero MAE change.
theories.effect_size: Home allocation asymmetry = -0.003 pts (train); 2022-25 +0.33 pts, not significant and unstable across eras.
theories.uncertainty: 95% CI on the asymmetry [-0.17,+0.16] pts in train.
theories.recommendation: Keep the symmetric identity; do not add a home-side share. Any home effect belongs in the spread (HFA expert), which the identity then propagates.
theories.parameter_change: keep as is (home share adjustment = 0)
theories.caveats: 2022-2025 home favorites did outscore the identity (+1.2), but that is a period-specific totals/spread bias, not an allocation rule.

theories.hypothesis: Given market S and T, the split is predictable from offense/defense profiles: an explosive/high-scoring offense facing a weak (high points-allowed) defense should be allocated more than the identity (the spec's +/-0.5..1.5 matchup reallocation).
theories.method: Rolling last-10 team-game points-for / points-against strictly before the game (min 5, vs prior-season league mean), 1999-2025. Regress r_home, r_away, tot_err, sp_err on h_off, h_def(allowed), a_off, a_def + S + T (HC1); single-index X_home = h_off + a_def per-SD effect; top/bottom-decile over rates; OOS 2022-2025: identity vs identity + 4-profile reallocation fit on train, and sum-preserving reallocation on (X_home - X_away).
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv scores and closing lines.
theories.metric: Regression coefficients (pts per profile point and per SD), decile over rate, OOS team-total MAE with paired bootstrap.
theories.result: Train (n=6050): r_home ~ profiles: h_off +0.058 (p=0.13), h_def -0.088 (p=0.02, sign opposite to hypothesis), a_off -0.014, a_def +0.022 (p=0.55); R2=0.002. X_home per SD +0.195 pts (p=0.29); X_away +0.080 (p=0.65). Top-decile X_home P(over identity)=0.474 train / 0.614 test (bottom decile 0.506 / 0.604 - both deciles over in test, i.e. period bias not matchup). OOS 2022-2025 (n=1139): full 4-profile reallocation dMAE home +0.021 [-0.007,+0.049], away -0.022 [-0.047,+0.005]; sum-preserving reallocation (train coef +0.047, p=0.011) OOS dMAE -0.002 [-0.011,+0.006]. Sanity: profiles predict margin (R2 0.13) but add nothing once S is included (all p>0.05).
theories.effect_size: <= 0.2 pts per SD of matchup index in-sample; ~0 OOS.
theories.uncertainty: All OOS dMAE CIs include zero.
theories.recommendation: No reallocation from PF/PA profiles; the market S and T already price them.
theories.parameter_change: matchup reallocation from scoring profiles: set to 0
theories.caveats: PF/PA is a coarse proxy; see TT3b for pbp-based features.

theories.hypothesis: Play-by-play matchup features (explosive-play rate offense vs allowed, red-zone TD rate offense vs allowed, EPA/play, pace and pace mismatch, pass rate) predict the identity residuals and justify +/-0.5..1.5 reallocations (explosive O vs weak D up; strong red-zone D down; pace for the total).
theories.method: Built per team-game stats from nflscrapR 2009-2019 and nflfastR 2023-2025 (04a), rolling last-10 sums strictly prior (min 5, windows reset at the 2019->2023 gap), z-scored on train; matchup indices e.g. expl_home = z(home off explosive) + z(away def explosive allowed). Regressions of r_home, r_away, tot_err, sp_err on indices + S + T (HC1), fit 2009-2019 and re-estimated independently on 2023-2025; per-SD effects and decile over rates; OOS reallocation rules fit on 2009-2019 applied to 2023-2025 with paired bootstrap.
theories.data_used: reg_pbp_2009..2019.csv (nflscrapR), play_by_play_2023..2025.parquet (nflfastR), joined to games_1999_2025.csv on old_game_id / game_id; 2020-2022 pbp unavailable locally.
theories.metric: pts per SD of matchup index; decile P(over identity); OOS team-total MAE (2023-2025, n=773).
theories.result: Train 2009-2019 (n=2733): expl_home -> r_home -0.455 pts/SD (p=0.035) and epa_home -0.725 pts/SD (p=0.006): OPPOSITE sign to the hypothesis (market over-prices explosive/high-EPA home offenses); away side +0.31 (p=0.11). Test 2023-2025 (n=773): expl_home +0.162 (p=0.65), epa_home -0.034 (p=0.94), expl_away -0.010 (p=0.98) - no replication. Red zone: rz_away -0.347 (p=0.07) train vs +0.581 (p=0.09) test (sign flip); rz_home -0.257 / +0.275. Pace: tot_err ~ pace_avg +0.34 pts/SD (p=0.19) train, +0.33 (p=0.50) test; pace_mismatch -0.37 (p=0.18) / -0.76 (p=0.10); fastest-decile games P(over)=0.528 train, 0.519 test. OOS full reallocation: dMAE home -0.005 [-0.032,+0.021], away -0.024 [-0.063,+0.015]; sum-preserving single-index rules |dMAE| < 0.003. R2 of every residual regression <= 0.006 in train.
theories.effect_size: No feature has a stable sign; magnitude at the 90th percentile of the train point estimates would be -0.3 to -0.9 pts (i.e. AGAINST the spec's direction) and does not survive OOS.
theories.uncertainty: Test-period coefficients have p 0.09-0.98 and opposite signs to train; OOS dMAE CIs include zero.
theories.recommendation: Do not apply explosive-offense, red-zone-defense or pace-mismatch reallocations to team totals. Pace does not move the total residual OOS either.
theories.parameter_change: explosive/red-zone/pace matchup reallocation: 0 (remove the +/-0.5..1.5 block or set its default to 0 with a +/-0.5 hard cap)
theories.caveats: pbp features are last-10-game proxies, not PFF grades; test window is 3 seasons (n=773); 2020-2022 not testable.

theories.hypothesis: Unvalidated +/-0.5..1.5 sum-preserving reallocations are costly: if uncorrelated with truth they raise team-total error, and because a sum-preserving shift of delta equals a spread change of 2*delta they make the published team totals inconsistent with the published spread.
theories.method: Simulation on 2022-2025 (n=1139): add delta = sign*U(lo,hi) to home and -delta to away, 200 replications, measure MAE change; Normal-approximation table of the expected MAE change from reallocating x when the true shift is t (residual SD 8.99).
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv closing lines and scores.
theories.metric: OOS team-total MAE change (home/away average, baseline 7.155).
theories.result: Random reallocation U(0.5,1.5) on all games: dMAE +0.043 (sd 0.020); on 50% of games +0.021; U(0.5,1.0) +0.022; fixed 0.5 +0.006; fixed 1.5 +0.091. A reallocation of x only lowers MAE if the true expected shift exceeds x/2; no matchup index tested reaches +0.25 pts OOS (TT3a/TT3b). Implied hidden spread change of the spec's block: up to 3.0 pts.
theories.effect_size: +0.02 to +0.09 MAE per game from noise reallocations; break-even true effect = half the reallocation.
theories.uncertainty: Simulation sd 0.01-0.03 across replications.
theories.recommendation: Derive team totals from the FINAL spread and total after all context adjustments (QB, injuries, weather) and apply no separate matchup reallocation. If a reallocation block is kept for discretionary use: default 0, hard cap +/-0.5, and any sum-preserving delta must be mirrored in the published spread (spread -= 2*delta) or it is rejected. Rounding to .0/.5 with sum preserved is fine.
theories.parameter_change: reallocation range: [-1.5,+1.5] -> default 0, cap [-0.5,+0.5], coherence rule spread_final = spread - 2*delta
theories.caveats: Context adjustments validated by other experts (QB backup, WR1 out) are not matchup reallocations and are out of scope here; they should enter via S and T.

theories.hypothesis: Favorites of 7 to 9.5 points score about one point more than the identity implies (the only spread-bin pattern that held in every era block), so a favorite team-total bump in that bin is justified.
theories.method: Residual of favorite score vs identity in the |S| in [7, 9.5] bin, train 1999-2021 and test 2022-2025; per-season sign count 1999-2025; decomposition into total error and favorite spread error; OOS rules fav_tt += 0.5 / += 1.0 in the bin and monotone fav_tt += k*|S| with paired bootstrap.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv closing lines and scores.
theories.metric: Mean residual with CI, P(fav over identity), OOS MAE change, binomial sign test across seasons.
theories.result: Train (n=1129): r_fav +1.13 [+0.57,+1.70], P(fav over)=0.518, r_dog -0.02. Test (n=170): r_fav +0.75 [-0.60,+2.09], P(fav over)=0.541 (binomial p=0.32). Positive in 24/27 seasons (p<0.001). All years (n=1299): +1.08 = 0.5*total_err (+0.59) + 0.5*favorite spread error (+0.50). OOS rule fav_tt += 0.5 in the bin: dMAE +0.035 [-0.038,+0.109] (n=170), P(fav over) after shift 0.521. Not monotone in |S| (10-13.5 bin r_fav +0.01 train); monotone rules fav_tt += 0.03|S| / 0.05|S| OOS dMAE +0.004 [-0.007,+0.014] / +0.006 [-0.012,+0.024].
theories.effect_size: +1.1 pts in-sample on the favorite's team total; half of it is a totals bias (games at 7-9.5 go over by ~1.1) and half a spread bias (favorite covers by ~1.0).
theories.uncertainty: Test CI [-0.60,+2.09] with n=170; OOS MAE gain CI includes 0.
theories.recommendation: Keep the allocation as is; route the finding to the totals and spread experts (a +0.5 to +1.0 total and a 0.5 favorite lean for |S| in [7, 9.5] would be the shrunk implementation) since it is a bias in S and T, not in the split. Re-test after 2026.
theories.parameter_change: keep as is (optional, coordinated with totals/spread: total +0.5 and spread toward favorite 0.5 when 7 <= |S| <= 9.5)
theories.caveats: n=170 OOS is below the discipline threshold for a confident finding; era consistency (24/27 seasons) is the only reason it is not simply REJECTED.

experts.summary:
Team-total allocation, ORIGINATOR v5. Every result comes from scripts under /home/user/originator-2026-w01/research/experts/teamtotals/ (run_all.sh re-runs all ten; sign check corr(S, margin) = -0.43 confirmed). Benchmark = identity applied to the market closing spread/total (no market team totals exist in the kit).

Findings: (1) The linear identity home = T/2 - S/2, away = T/2 + S/2 is correct. OLS slopes are 0.52/0.47 (home) and 0.52/0.45 (away) with Wald tests of slope = 0.5 not rejected (p 0.07-0.73, both 1999-2021 and 2009-2021 fits); no favorite/dog nonlinearity; the identity beats every fitted alternative OOS (2022-25 n=1139) and in rolling-origin 2010-2025 (pooled n=4363, identity better by 0.014-0.020 MAE, CIs exclude 0). The nonzero intercepts are the market total's +0.7 under-bias and shrinkage, which belong to the totals engine and flow into team totals through T. (2) No home/away asymmetry: home allocation residual -0.003 pts in train, home_fav coefficient -0.13 (p=0.63); the 2022-25 home-favorite excess (+1.2) is a period totals bias with era-flipping sign. (3) No matchup reallocation signal: rolling PF/PA profiles (n=7189) and pbp explosive-play, red-zone TD, EPA, pace and pass-rate matchups (2009-2019 fit n=2733, 2023-25 test n=773) explain <0.6% of residual variance; the in-sample explosive/EPA effects are NEGATIVE (market over-prices them) and flip sign OOS; reallocation rules change OOS MAE by -0.02 to +0.02 with CIs spanning zero; pace does not move the total. (4) Unvalidated +/-0.5..1.5 sum-preserving reallocations cost +0.04 MAE per game if they are noise and are a hidden spread change of up to 3 points. (5) Median-vs-mean shading for low team totals (P(over) 0.482 for tt<20, p=0.08) and the favorite 7-9.5 bin (+1.1 in-sample, 24/27 seasons positive, OOS n=170 not significant) are INCONCLUSIVE; the latter is a bias in S and T, not the split.

What I would change first and why: remove the matchup reallocation block (set default 0, hard cap +/-0.5, and require that any sum-preserving delta be mirrored as spread -= 2*delta) and derive team totals strictly from the final adjusted spread and total. This is the only change with positive expected value: the split itself is already optimal, and every proposed reallocation tested is indistinguishable from noise, which measurably costs accuracy and breaks spread/team-total coherence. Second, hand the 7-9.5 favorite/total pattern to the totals and spread experts for a coordinated, shrunk adjustment (total +0.5, favorite lean 0.5) rather than implementing it in the allocation.

theories.hypothesis: A starter->backup QB change is worth -2.0..-4.5 points (spec); measure (a) closing-market movement vs the team's no-QB rating-implied line and (b) realized margin residual vs that line, split 2009-2015 / 2016-2025.
theories.method: Team-game QB table from games.csv (home/away_qb_name, 1999+ for career-start counts). Rating-implied line WITHOUT QB = -(nfelo_dif_base - home_net_qb_mod)/25 (NB: nfelo_dif_base INCLUDES home_net_qb_mod; verified by identity in 00_explore_identities.py, 95.7% of rows reconcile to <0.01 Elo). Three backup definitions: D1 = task's 'starter != team-season most-starts QB' (look-ahead), D2 = D1 + fewer career starts than primary, D3 = PROSPECTIVE: a mid-season (week>=2) QB change where the new starter has fewer career starts than the displaced starter; flags persist for the stint, reset each week 1. OLS of outcome on backup_net (+1 home backup, -1 away) with HC1 SE, by era and by stint index (1st start / 2nd-3rd / 4th+), in-season (REG wk<=16) vs wk17+/playoff rest games. OOS: penalty fitted on 2009-2021, applied to 2022-2025 with paired-bootstrap MAE CI and ATS vs close.
theories.metric: points of market movement and margin residual (home perspective), MAE, ATS vs close
theories.result: D3 prospective, in-season, opponent not also a backup: 1st backup start (n_event=296): market charges +2.80 +/-0.18 pts vs the no-QB rating line; realized penalty vs that line +3.47 +/-0.78. 2nd-3rd start (n=342): market +1.71 +/-0.16, realized +2.31 +/-0.69. 4th+ start (n=359): market +0.62 +/-0.14, realized +1.51 +/-0.69 (the Elo has absorbed the backup by then). Rest games (wk17+/playoffs, n=59): market +4.91 +/-0.75, realized +9.49 +/-1.67. Era, 1st start in-season: 2009-2015 market +2.57 +/-0.29 / realized +2.72 +/-1.39 (n=109); 2016-2025 market +2.94 +/-0.22 / realized +3.89 +/-0.94 (n=187); era differences not significant (0.37 +/-0.36 market; 1.17 +/-1.68 realized). OOS (fit<=2021 in-season, test 2022-25, n=960): no-QB line + fitted 1st-start penalty 2.01 lowers MAE 9.6522 -> 9.6012, dMAE -0.051 [-0.087,-0.014]; on the 86 event games dMAE -0.57. nfelo's continuous 538 QB adj beats any flat penalty OOS (dMAE -0.113 [-0.21,-0.02] vs no-QB line, full sample). The task's D1 definition gives inflated numbers (realized -4.26, residual vs market -2.2, fade-backup ATS 55.5% p=0.0004): look-ahead artifact - D1-only games (benched/early-hurt starters) show -2.5 vs market whereas prospective D3 games show -1.1; D1 numbers should not be used.
theories.recommendation: Spec range -2.0..-4.5 holds for the FIRST backup start (point estimate 2.8 market / 3.5 realized, 95% CI of market value 2.4-3.2). It does not hold as a flat value: decay it by stint. Use a stint table instead of a single range, and prefer a QB-value-gap (continuous) adjustment when nfelo's 538 adj is available, since it beats the flat table OOS.
theories.parameter_change: Replace 'QB starter->backup -2.0..-4.5' with a stint-indexed penalty on the backup team (points, spread; applied only to blend inputs that do NOT already carry a QB adjustment - see qb-4 rule): 1st start with team this season = 3.0 (band 2.5-3.5; 3.5 when the displaced starter's nfelo 538 adj was >= +3 pts, 2.5 when <= +1); 2nd-3rd start = 1.75; 4th+ start = 0.5 (ratings have absorbed the backup); playoff-locked team resting its starter in wk17-18 = 5.0 (see qb-2b). Team-total split: apply 60% to the backup team's TT, 40% as a reallocation to the opponent (not validated locally; TT data absent).
