theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv (QB names, closing spread, results), nfelo_games.csv (starting Elo, hfa_base_mod, mods, home_net_qb_mod, nfelo_dif_base, nfelo lines, market lines), 2009-2025, 4,310 games with both nfelo and market
theories.effect_size: 1st start: 2.8 pts market-implied, 3.5 realized; 2nd-3rd: 1.7 / 2.3; 4th+: 0.6 / 1.5; rest game: 4.9 / 9.5
theories.uncertainty: 1st-start market value SE 0.18; realized SE 0.78; rest-game numbers n=59
theories.caveats: nfelo's pre-game Elo partly reflects the backup after a few starts, so stint-4+ values understate the raw starter->backup gap but are the right values to add to a current rating. D3 misses backups who are MORE experienced than the displaced starter (those 'upgrade' stints show ~0 effect: market +0.13 +/-0.10, realized -0.55 +/-0.42). 'Backup' includes benchings, not only injuries. kit.py hfa_pts uses hfa_mod + time adv but nfelo_dif_base reconciles with hfa_base_mod (hfa_mod = base + time in only 28% of rows) - I used the reconciled identity.
theories.expected_impact: Affects ~14% of team-games (D3) / ~7% of games at the 1st-start stage; correcting the flat -2..-4.5 to a decaying table removes 1.5-3 pt errors on 2nd+ starts.

theories.hypothesis: nfelo's 538-style QB adjustment (home_net_qb_mod) fully prices in-season backup starts, i.e. the residual after the adjustment is ~0 and no top-up is needed on the nfelo component.
theories.method: Residual vs nfelo's unregressed line WITH the QB adj (resid_base = margin + line_nfelo_base) regressed on D3 backup_net by stint, in-season (REG wk<=16), fit window 2009-2021 vs test window 2022-2025. Scale test: resid_noqb ~ qb_adj_pts slope (1 = correctly scaled). OOS: stint-1 and all-stint top-ups fitted <=2021 applied 2022-25 on the 538-adj line, on nfelo's regressed close, and on the market close; paired bootstrap MAE CI.
theories.metric: points residual after the 538 QB adj; MAE; ATS vs close
theories.result: nfelo's 538 adj charges 2.30 +/-0.14 pts at a 1st backup start in-season (market 2.80), 1.64 at 2nd-3rd (market 1.71), 0.91 at 4th+ (market 0.62): it covers ~85-100% of the market-implied penalty. Residual after the adj at 1st start: fit window 2009-2021 +0.31 +/-0.89 (p=0.73, n=221) - i.e. fully priced; test window 2022-2025 +3.69 +/-1.64 (p=0.02, n=75). All in-season stints: +0.79 +/-0.41 (p=0.05). Scale: slope 1.22 (<=2021; rolling 1.46 -> 1.19), i.e. the adj is ~20% small on average, but rescaling x1.22 improves OOS MAE only 9.7737 -> 9.7689. OOS top-ups: stint-1 top-up fitted in-season <=2021 = -0.23 -> no improvement (dMAE +0.005); fixed +1.0 top-up on the 538-adj line dMAE -0.019 [-0.038,+0.001], on nfelo close -0.013 [-0.031,+0.006], on market close -0.009 [-0.028,+0.009] - none significant. Residual vs the MARKET for in-season backups: +0.72 +/-0.41 (p=0.08) any stint, +0.66 +/-0.77 at 1st start; fade-backup ATS 51.5% [48.5,54.4] overall, 57.8% (48-35, p=0.19) at 1st start in 2022-25. Market + any penalty never lowers OOS MAE (dMAE +0.003 to +0.036).
theories.recommendation: Do NOT add a backup top-up to the nfelo component for in-season backup starts; nfelo's 538 adj already carries ~2.3 pts at the first start and the fit-window residual is zero. The 2022-25 residual (+3.7, n=75) is a watch item, not a parameter. The market prices backups to within ~0.7 pt: never add a QB penalty on top of a market-anchored (regressed) line.
theories.parameter_change: nfelo component: top-up = 0 for in-season backup starts (optionally scale nfelo's QB adj by 1.15-1.2 when it is applied on the UNREGRESSED nfelo line; gain is ~0.005 MAE, cosmetic). Any input that is market-regressed (nfelo close): QB top-up = 0.
theories.data_used: nfelo_games.csv home_538_qb_adj/away_538_qb_adj/home_net_qb_mod (Elo, /25 = points), games.csv results and closing lines, 2009-2025
theories.effect_size: residual after 538 adj at 1st start: +0.31 (2009-21) / +3.69 (2022-25); any stint +0.79
theories.uncertainty: SE 0.89 (fit) / 1.64 (test); 2022-25 stint-1 has only 75 events
theories.caveats: Full-sample stint-1 residual (+1.70 +/-0.66) and the significant OOS gain of a 0.99 top-up (dMAE -0.0215 [-0.039,-0.003]) are driven by wk17+/playoff rest games, not in-season injuries - see qb-2b.
theories.expected_impact: Prevents a 2-3 pt double count on ~7% of games (see qb-4).

theories.hypothesis: Week 17-18 / playoff 'rest' backup starts (playoff-locked team sits its starter) are under-priced by nfelo's QB adj and by the market.
theories.method: Same D3 stint-1 regressions restricted to REG week>=17 or playoffs (late==1), fit vs test windows.
theories.metric: points penalty (market-implied, realized, 538-assigned, residual after 538, residual vs market)
theories.result: n_event=59: market charges +4.91 +/-0.75; realized +9.49 +/-1.67; nfelo 538 adj only +3.06 +/-0.34; residual after 538 +6.43 +/-1.73; residual vs MARKET +4.59 +/-1.71 (p=0.007). Fit window (n=32): after-538 +8.30 +/-2.14, vs market +7.16 +/-2.24; test window (n=27): after-538 +4.20 +/-2.74, vs market +1.52 +/-2.51 (p=0.54).
theories.recommendation: n=59 is below the 150-game bar, but the market-implied value (4.9 +/-0.75) is well measured and the realized penalty is larger in both windows; a conservative separate rest-game rule is warranted, sized at the market value, not the realized one.
theories.parameter_change: Add a 'starter rested (playoff-locked, wk17-18 or meaningless game)' rule: penalty 5.0 pts on the resting team (band 4.0-6.0), applied net of what nfelo already carries (nfelo 538 adj ~3 pts -> nfelo-share top-up 0.46*(5.0-3.0) = +0.9); apply the full 5.0 to PFF/Cole components unless their rating is dated after the rest announcement. Also set the confidence tag to LOW for these games.
theories.data_used: same as qb-1, subset REG week>=17 or playoffs
theories.effect_size: market 4.9, realized 9.5, residual vs market 4.6 pts
theories.uncertainty: SE 1.7 on realized/residual; n=59
theories.caveats: Rest games conflate QB rest with whole-roster rest and motivation; the QB parameter alone should not absorb it all - hence sizing at the market value (4.9) rather than realized (9.5).

theories.hypothesis: Week 1: teams with a new starter (vs previous-season primary) or a rookie/first-career-start QB show a margin residual vs the market.
theories.method: Week-1 REG games 2009-2025 (253 with nfelo+market). new = week-1 starter != team's previous-season most-starts QB; first = 0 prior career starts in games.csv 1999+ (rookie proxy; no draft data locally). OLS with HC1 of resid vs market / vs no-QB line / market movement on net flags; era split; fit(<=2021)/test(2022-25) split; extensions: weeks 1-4 of the new starter's tenure, and all-weeks '<10 career starts'.
theories.metric: points residual vs market close; ATS
theories.result: Week 1 new starter (115 team-events): residual vs market +2.24 +/-1.11 (p=0.045) - new starters BEAT the number; fade-new-starter ATS 48-65 (42.5%, p=0.13); fit window +2.27 (p=0.10, n=81), test +2.25 (p=0.21, n=34). Market movement vs no-QB Elo line for new starters only +0.37 +/-0.23 and nfelo's 538 adj only -0.20: neither the market nor nfelo penalizes offseason QB changes much. First-career-start in week 1 (32 events): +1.22 +/-2.01 (p=0.54), ATS 16-16. Weeks 1-4 new starter (429 events): +0.71 +/-0.63 (p=0.26). Weeks 1-4 new starter with <4 career starts (181 events): +2.06 +/-1.02 (p=0.044), back-the-rookie ATS 109-68 = 61.6% (p=0.003); but fit window +2.52 (p=0.027, n=139) vs test +0.57 +/-2.26 (p=0.80, n=42). All-weeks inexperienced (<10 starts, 1083 events): -0.71 +/-0.39 (p=0.07) - opposite sign. ~20 tests in this family; Bonferroni alpha ~0.0025; nothing survives.
theories.recommendation: No Week-1 new-starter or rookie adjustment. The point estimates lean toward the market slightly OVER-penalizing brand-new starters early in the season (+2 pts, n=115-181), not under-penalizing, so a negative 'new starter' adjustment would be the wrong sign; the evidence is too thin and not stable across windows to add a positive one.
theories.parameter_change: Keep as is: QB context adjustment = 0 for Week-1 new starters and rookies; rely on the rating inputs' QB values. Do not add a rookie penalty.
theories.data_used: games.csv QB names 1999-2025 (career starts), nfelo_games.csv, week-1 games 2009-2025
theories.effect_size: +2.2 pts (week-1 new starter), +2.1 (wk1-4 rookie proxy); both n<200 and not replicated OOS
theories.caveats: 'First career start' cannot distinguish rookies from never-started veterans; nflverse has no draft/age fields locally. 2022-25 week-1 rookie events n=9 (-3.8, opposite sign).

theories.hypothesis: Injury proxies beyond QB (WR1, OL, pass rush) can be validated locally, and the QB adjustment must not double-count QB effects already embedded in the blend inputs.
theories.method: Scanned every column of every research/data csv for injury/WR/OL/status fields. Computed the QB penalty nfelo embeds (A_nfelo = -qb_adj_pts on D3 backup_net, fit window 2009-2021, by stint) vs the market-implied target (P), and the overshoot of adding the spec's -2.0..-4.5 on top of a blend whose inputs are already QB-adjusted.
theories.metric: points embedded per input vs market-implied target; overshoot in points
theories.result: No injury, WR, OL, pass-rush or status columns exist in any local file (games.csv has only home/away_qb_name/id; cole/pff files have none). WR1/OL/pass-rush adjustments in spec section 5 are unvalidatable here. Double-count arithmetic (fit window): at a 1st backup start the market-implied target is P=2.76 while nfelo already embeds A_nfelo=2.31 (2nd-3rd: P=1.39 vs A=1.57; 4th+: P=0.12 vs A=0.37). If ORIGINATOR adds the spec's -2.0/-3.0/-4.5 on top of a blend whose three inputs are all QB-adjusted, the effective penalty is 4.8/5.8/7.3 vs market 2.8 - an overshoot of 2.0/3.0/4.5 pts; if only nfelo is QB-adjusted the overshoot is 0.3/1.3/2.8 pts. The stated cap (sum <= 2.5 spread) does not fix this because the embedded nfelo amount is outside the cap.
theories.recommendation: Implement an explicit net-of-embedded rule so the QB adjustment is only the gap between the target penalty and what each input already carries. Keep WR1/OL/pass-rush spec values but tag them LOW confidence and log them for later validation (need nflverse injuries/depth-chart data, not available locally).
theories.parameter_change: QB_adj = sum_i w_i * clip(P_stint - A_i, -1.0, P_stint), with w = (0.46 nfelo, 0.39 PFF, 0.15 Cole); P_stint from qb-1 (3.0 / 1.75 / 0.5; rest game 5.0). A_nfelo = -(home_net_qb_mod_now - home_net_qb_mod_last_week_with_starter)/25 in points (observable in nfelo_games.csv; typical 2.3 at 1st start) - if the nfelo line used is the market-regressed close, set A_nfelo = P_stint (treat as fully priced). A_PFF = A_Cole = P_stint when the rating was published after the QB news (their weekly power ratings are QB-adjusted), else 0. Total QB_adj then also counts toward the existing 2.5-pt spread cap. Practical default when only nfelo's status is known: QB_adj = 0.46*max(0, P - A_nfelo) + 0.54*P*(1 - qb_adjusted_flag_pff_cole). Never apply the raw -2.0..-4.5 on top of the blend.
theories.data_used: all files in research/data (column scan); nfelo_games.csv home_net_qb_mod; qb_games_defs.csv
theories.effect_size: overshoot 2.0-4.5 pts (all inputs QB-adjusted) or 0.3-2.8 pts (nfelo only) per backup game
theories.uncertainty: A_nfelo SE 0.17; P SE 0.21
theories.caveats: Whether PFF/Cole ratings post-date the QB news must be handled by the engine's timestamps; assumption that both are QB-adjusted is from their published methodology, not verified locally (no history exists).

experts.summary: Data facts first: (1) nfelo_dif_base INCLUDES home_net_qb_mod (identity verified: elo_dif + hfa_base_mod + all mods incl. QB = nfelo_dif_base in 95.7% of rows), so the 'no-QB' rating line is nfelo_dif_base - home_net_qb_mod; (2) the task's 'most-starts primary' backup definition is look-ahead (benched QBs are labeled backups because they were bad) and inflates every number (-2.2 vs market, 55.5% fade ATS); all conclusions use a prospective definition (mid-season change to a less-experienced QB), which the critic can rebuild from 02b. What I would change first, in order: (A) the double-count rule (qb-4) - ORIGINATOR currently adds -2.0..-4.5 on top of an nfelo input that already carries ~2.3 pts at a first backup start (and PFF/Cole are QB-adjusted too), overshooting the market by 2-4.5 pts on ~7% of games; apply the adjustment only net of what each input embeds. (B) replace the flat range with a stint-decaying table (qb-1, HIGH confidence, OOS-confirmed on a no-QB line: dMAE -0.051 [-0.087,-0.014]): first start 3.0 (market-implied 2.80 +/-0.18, realized 3.47 +/-0.78; era 2009-15 2.6/2.7 vs 2016-25 2.9/3.9, not significantly different), 2nd-3rd 1.75, 4th+ 0.5; the spec range is right only for the first start. (C) a separate rest-game rule ~5.0 pts for playoff-locked teams sitting the starter (qb-2b; market 4.9 +/-0.75, realized 9.5, n=59 -> INCONCLUSIVE but sizable). (D) nothing on top of nfelo for in-season backups (qb-2a: nfelo's 538 adj prices ~85-100% of the market value, fit-window residual +0.31 +/-0.89; OOS top-ups do not help; the market itself prices backups to within ~0.7 pt and no market-relative penalty improves OOS MAE). (E) no Week-1 new-starter/rookie adjustment (qb-3 INCONCLUSIVE; if anything new starters beat the number by ~2 pts, n=115-181, not replicated). Non-QB injury data (WR1, OL, pass rush) do not exist locally; those spec values stay untested and should be tagged LOW confidence. Scripts 00-08 in research/experts/qb/ are numbered, re-runnable, and print every number above.

theories.hypothesis: A team on short rest (Thursday after Sunday, rest<=5 days) facing a normally-rested opponent underperforms by 0.6-1.2 pts (spec section 5 'short week').
theories.method: REG weeks 2+ (week-1 rest is a placeholder) 2009-2025, nfelo-joined. Residuals vs market close, nfelo close, nfelo raw (unregressed) and a rating-only line (nfelo ratings + base HFA + QB + div + surface, no rest/tz mods). Signed 'rested side' means, OLS with all rest dummies (HC1), ATS vs close. Fit <=2021, test 2022-25.
theories.metric: mean signed residual (pts) for the rested side vs market/ratings; ATS vs close
theories.result: Only 8 games in 17 seasons had one team on <=5 days rest and the other not (0 since 2021): rested side vs market -1.38 (se 4.27), vs ratings +0.74 (se 4.67), ATS 3-5. 235 of 246 Thursday games have BOTH teams on 4 days rest, where the spread effect nets to zero (TNF home residual vs market -0.60, se 0.82).
theories.recommendation: Keep a short-rest term only as a special case of the linear rest rule (T3); it will essentially never fire under modern scheduling. Never apply it to both teams (nets to zero).
theories.parameter_change: Delete the standalone 'short week -0.6..-1.2' clause; a 4-day team vs a 7-day opponent gets -0.45 from the rest rule adj = -0.15 x clip(home_rest - away_rest, -7, +7).
theories.effect_size: unestimable (n=8); market prices -1.97 (se 0.94) on those 8 games
theories.uncertainty: se 4.3 pts
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv + nfelo_games.csv via common.py
theories.caveats: Not applicable in practice: the NFL schedules Thursday games with both teams off Sunday.

theories.hypothesis: Thursday games with both teams on 4 days rest are lower-scoring / higher-variance than the market total implies (ORIGINATOR totals should adjust TNF).
theories.method: TNF both-short games vs Sunday games: total residual (total_pts - closing total), over rate, spread MAE, by era. Fit <=2021 / test 2022-25.
theories.metric: mean total residual (pts) vs closing total; spread MAE
theories.result: TNF total residual +0.35 (se 0.87, p=0.68) all; fit +0.01 (se 1.03), test +1.11 (se 1.59). Market TNF total line 44.9 vs Sunday 44.8; realized 45.2 vs 45.5. Over rate 0.481 vs 0.494. Spread MAE on TNF 9.79 vs Sunday 10.18 (not noisier). Era splits -1.35/-1.13/+2.27/+1.11, all n.s.
theories.recommendation: Keep as is: no TNF-specific total or variance adjustment.
theories.parameter_change: keep as is
theories.effect_size: +0.35 pts on the total (95% CI about -1.4..+2.1)
theories.uncertainty: se 0.87 (all), 1.59 (test)
theories.data_used: games + nfelo merge, REG weeks 2+

theories.hypothesis: A team off a bye (rest >= 13) beats a normally-rested opponent by +0.5..+1.0 more than ratings imply (spec bye clause); question is whether the market/nfelo already price it.
theories.method: One-team-bye games (both-bye excluded). Signed 'bye team' residual vs market close, nfelo close, nfelo raw, rating-only line; OLS with 6-day/10-day dummies (HC1); market pricing regression mkt_spread ~ rate_line + home_bye + away_bye; ATS bye team vs close; era splits; OOS 2022-25 grid of k on the rating-only line (MAE/RMSE/bias). Fit <=2021, test 2022-25.
theories.metric: mean signed residual for the bye team (pts); market-pricing coefficient; OOS MAE/RMSE/bias on bye games
theories.result: Gross effect vs ratings +1.00 (se 0.59, p=0.09; fit +0.82, test +1.59 se 0.96). Vs market close -0.05 (se 0.59); bye team ATS 204-213-13 (0.489) -> fully priced. Market moves 1.05 (se 0.15) for a home bye and 1.02 (se 0.14) for an away bye, i.e. symmetric ~1.0. nfelo already applies +0.34 (home) / +1.52 (away) and its residual is -0.08 (se 0.59): right on average, asymmetry unsupported (gross home +0.70 se 0.79, away +1.29 se 0.87). OOS 102 bye games: MAE 7.362 (k=0) vs 7.384 (k=1.0), RMSE 9.764 -> 9.651; bye-team bias +1.59 -> +0.59 (market's own bias +0.56). Fit-set MAE-optimal k=1.00.
theories.recommendation: The bye effect is real and ~1.0 pt, and the market prices exactly that. The engine should carry a TOTAL of ~1.0 for the bye team, not the spec's +0.5..1.0 on top of nfelo's own mod (currently 0.46*nfelo_mod + spec = ~0.8-1.8, over-adjusting). Implement once via the linear rest rule (T3).
theories.parameter_change: Strip nfelo's bye mods from the nfelo component (subtract (home_bye_mod + away_bye_mod)/25 from its line), then apply adj = -0.15 x clip(home_rest - away_rest, -7, 7) to the blended spread (bye vs 7-day opponent = 1.05 pts to the bye team). If stripping is impossible: apply 0.54 x 1.0 = +0.55 to the bye team on the blend and drop the spec's +0.5..1.0.
theories.effect_size: +1.0 pt for the bye team (gross); market-priced 1.0; net vs market 0.0
theories.uncertainty: se 0.59 (all-sample gross), 0.96 (test); market coefficient se 0.14
theories.data_used: games + nfelo merge, REG weeks 2+, 2009-2025
theories.caveats: Era-unstable gross estimates (+3.0 in 2009-12, -0.6 in 2018-21, +1.6 in 2022-25); market pricing is stable at 1.0 in every window, so match the market. MAE tests on 100 games cannot resolve a 1-pt adjustment; the bias and market-pricing tests are the evidence.

theories.hypothesis: Rest differential (home_rest - away_rest) has a continuous linear effect on margin beyond the bye dummy, including the 6-day (Mon->Sun) and 10-day (Thu->Sun) cases.
theories.method: OLS residual ~ rest_diff clipped to +-7 (HC1) for each residual series; binned means; specific 6-day/10-day asymmetries with ATS; market pricing mkt_spread ~ rate_line + rest_diff; OOS 2022-25 comparison of linear / bye-only / dummies / sqrt specs (k fit on <=2021) with paired bootstrap CI; rolling-origin 2016-2025 refit each season.
theories.metric: pts per rest day (slope); rested-side bias on affected games; MAE
theories.result: Slope vs ratings +0.177/day (se 0.077, p=0.02); fit +0.153 (p=0.10), test +0.244 (p=0.07). Market prices +0.145/day (se 0.014); residual vs market +0.031/day (p=0.69) -> fully priced. Excluding bye games slope +0.27/day (se 0.17, n.s.), market prices 0.11. 6-day/10-day asymmetries pooled n=851: rested side +0.64 vs ratings (se 0.44), +0.43 vs market (se 0.44), ATS 424-408. Rolling-origin (915 affected games, 2016-25): rested-side bias +0.45 -> +0.04, MAE 9.431 -> 9.427. Full test-set MAE change of any rest spec within +-0.004 (bootstrap CI [-0.020, +0.022]).
theories.recommendation: Use one linear rest term, sized to the market's pricing (0.15/day, max +-1.05). It subsumes short-week and bye clauses and removes the current bye double count. It will not move season MAE measurably; its value is unbiased affected games and consistency with the market.
theories.parameter_change: spread_adj (ORIGINATOR sign, negative = home favored) = -0.15 x clip(home_rest - away_rest, -7, +7), applied once to the blended spread after removing nfelo's bye mods from the nfelo input; if nfelo's mods cannot be removed use -0.08/day on the blend. Week 1: no rest adjustment (rest field is a placeholder).
theories.effect_size: +0.15..0.18 pts per rest day; bye (7-day gap) = 1.0-1.2 pts
theories.uncertainty: se 0.077/day (all), 0.135 (test)
theories.data_used: games + nfelo merge, REG weeks 2+; rolling-origin in 06_recommendation.py
theories.caveats: Market prices it fully, so it adds no edge vs the close; it matters for the PFF/Cole 54% of the blend which has no rest term at all.

theories.hypothesis: West-coast (PT/MT) teams kicking at 1pm ET (10-11am body clock) underperform by 0.4-0.8 pts (spec 'west-to-east 10am kick').
theories.method: Non-neutral REG games; team home time zones (ARI DST-aware) and ET gametime define body-clock kickoff. Groups: PT away team at 12:30-13:30 ET (n=287), MT/PT (n=383). Residuals vs market/nfelo/ratings, ATS fading the west team, OOS MAE of the spec's -0.6 on the ORIGINATOR proxy with bootstrap CI.
theories.metric: mean home residual (pts) when the visitor is a west team at 1pm ET; ATS; OOS MAE
theories.result: PT team at 1pm ET: home vs ratings -0.47 (se 0.78) i.e. the west team did slightly BETTER than ratings; vs market -0.05 (se 0.77); fade-west ATS 129-148-10 (0.466). MT/PT pooled: -0.50 (se 0.68) vs ratings, ATS 172-200-11 (0.462). Test 2022-25 (n=106): +0.21 vs ratings, +0.66 vs market, ATS 49-55. nfelo's tz mod gives the home +0.9 here and its residual is -1.27 (se 0.78, p=0.10): nfelo over-adjusts. Spec's -0.6 OOS: full-test MAE +0.0044 (CI [-0.007, +0.016]), affected ATS 46-58.
theories.recommendation: Remove the west-to-east 10am clause. Also fix ORIGINATOR's site HFA for the PFF/Cole paths: hfa_mod already contains home_time_advantage_mod (verified in 00b), so (hfa_mod + home_time_advantage_mod)/25 double-counts a term that does not help OOS (re-applying nfelo's tz mod to the blend: MAE +0.006, CI [-0.016, +0.029]).
theories.parameter_change: Delete 'west-to-east 10am kick -0.4..-0.8'. Site HFA for PFF/Cole = hfa_mod/25 (drop the + home_time_advantage_mod term).
theories.effect_size: -0.5 pts to the HOME side (wrong sign for the theory); 95% CI for the west team's disadvantage excludes anything beyond ~1.0 and centres on a small advantage
theories.data_used: games + nfelo merge, non-neutral REG, time-zone table in common.py
theories.caveats: Body-clock definition uses franchise home zone; ARI treated as Pacific before the November DST change.

theories.hypothesis: Away teams crossing 3 time zones (cross-country trips) underperform ratings/market (travel fatigue).
theories.method: Non-neutral REG games with |tz_diff| = 3 (n=464; fit 317, test 147). Residuals vs market/nfelo/ratings; OLS with home-team, away-team and season fixed effects (HC1); leave-one-team-out; per-season and era splits; excess over league-season residual; west-team-quality confound check (west teams at 0/1-2/3 zones); OOS k grid fit <=2021 -> 2022-25; paired-bootstrap MAE on the ORIGINATOR proxy.
theories.metric: home residual (pts) in 3-zone games (negative = traveller beat the line); traveller ATS; OOS MAE/bias
theories.result: OPPOSITE sign. Home vs market -1.73 (se 0.83, p=0.04) east-bound and -1.63 (se 0.99) west-bound; team+season FE: -2.26 (se 0.77, p<0.01); fit -1.77 (p=0.07), test -3.14 (p=0.01). LOTO range -1.3..-2.2. Not a west-team quality effect (west teams at 1-2 zones: -0.08 vs market). Regime: 2009-17 n=187 ~ +0.2; 2018-25 n=277 -2.94 (se 0.80), excess vs league -2.95 (p<0.001), traveller ATS 159-113 (0.585, p=0.006); test 2022-25 n=147: -2.01 (se 1.05), ATS 79-65. Market leans -0.04 and nfelo +0.50 toward the home in these games. OOS +1.0 to the traveller on the proxy: full-test MAE -0.0137 (CI [-0.036, +0.008]); affected MAE 10.447 -> 10.330 on the rating-only line, bias -2.41 -> -1.41; 3 of 4 test seasons improved. Fit-optimal k = 2.5 (3.25 on 2018-21).
theories.recommendation: Do not add any travel penalty. The reverse effect (3-zone traveller +2 to +3 pts vs ratings since 2018) is the single largest unpriced schedule residual in the data and is confirmed out-of-sample, but is absent 2009-17; implement conservatively at half size as a reviewed flag.
theories.parameter_change: Optional (LOW-MED confidence): if |home_tz - away_tz| = 3 and the site is not neutral, add +1.0 pt to the AWAY team (spread_adj = +1.0 in ORIGINATOR sign). Re-estimate after 2026; drop if 2026 traveller ATS < 0.50.
theories.effect_size: traveller +2.0 (all, FE) / +2.9 (2018-25) pts vs market; +1.0 recommended
theories.uncertainty: se 0.77 (FE all), 1.05 (test 2022-25); bootstrap MAE CI includes 0
theories.data_used: games + nfelo merge, non-neutral REG; also 04_travel.py and 04c_travel_rules_oos.py
theories.caveats: Mechanism unknown (possible over-pricing of HFA/travel by market and nfelo, or scheduling changes); 2-zone games show the opposite sign (+1.3 home, se 0.6), so no distance dose-response. Related: ET teams in the 4pm window out west beat the line by 1.3 (se 1.0, n=228, INCONCLUSIVE) - also the opposite of 'travel hurts'.

theories.hypothesis: In primetime (kick >= 19:00 ET) the more-western team has a circadian edge (playing closer to its body-clock peak).
theories.method: Non-neutral REG primetime games with tz_diff != 0 (n=447; fit 312, test 135). West-team signed residual vs market/ratings by zones apart; day-game placebo; era splits; ATS backing the west team; OOS +0.5/1.0/1.5 rules on the ORIGINATOR proxy with bootstrap CI.
theories.metric: west team's signed residual vs market (pts); ATS; OOS MAE
theories.result: West edge vs market: 1 zone +1.65 (se 0.78, n=276), 2 zones +1.69 (se 1.22, n=94), 3 zones +1.22 (se 1.44, n=77): flat, no per-zone slope (-0.17, se 0.78). Fit +1.60 (se 0.75, p=0.03), test +1.54 (se 0.96, p=0.11); west ATS 164-139 fit, 72-58 test. Day-game placebo: +0.69/-1.18/-0.03 (null). Era: +2.58, +0.61, +1.56, +1.54. Market prices ~0.05/zone; nfelo prices 0.35/zone and its residual still shows +0.7..1.2. OOS +1.0 to the west team: full-test MAE -0.0119 (CI [-0.033, +0.009]); affected MAE 8.628 -> 8.585, ATS 71-59.
theories.recommendation: Suggestive but not decisive (test p=0.11, no dose-response). Do not hard-code yet; carry as an optional +1.0 flag to the more-western team in primetime, reviewed with T4b after 2026. Combined with the T4b flag the OOS MAE gain is -0.026 (CI [-0.057, +0.001]).
theories.parameter_change: Optional: if kick >= 19:00 ET, site not neutral, and the teams' home zones differ, add +1.0 pt to the more-western team (any number of zones). Otherwise keep as is.
theories.effect_size: +1.5 pts to the western team vs market (fit and test)
theories.uncertainty: se 0.75 (fit), 0.96 (test)
theories.data_used: games + nfelo merge; 04b_travel_robustness.py section E
theories.caveats: Flat effect across zones argues against a pure circadian mechanism; 77 games overlap with the 3-zone rule.

theories.hypothesis: Week 1 ratings are uncertain: engine error and residual variance are larger than mid-season, so ORIGINATOR should shrink to the market or widen confidence tags in week 1.
theories.method: MAE of market, nfelo raw, nfelo close, rating-only by week bucket; paired difference of absolute errors (engine minus market) week 1 vs weeks 4-16; Levene test on residual SD; home/favourite bias; combination regression margin ~ rating line + market line.
theories.metric: MAE difference engine minus market (pts); residual SD; bias
theories.result: Week 1: market MAE 9.82 vs nfelo raw 9.85 (diff +0.03, se 0.13) - the engine is NOT relatively worse in week 1; weeks 4-16 diff +0.12 (p=0.002). Residual SD 13.15 vs 13.08 (Levene p=0.62). Home bias -0.77 (se 0.83), favourite cover -0.88 (se 0.83), dogs ATS 130-118 - n.s. Test 2022-25 (n=64): diff -0.04. Combination weights week 1: rating 0.41 (se 0.45) vs market 0.55 (se 0.39) (vs 0.34/0.76 mid-season).
theories.recommendation: No week-1 special handling: no extra shrink to market, no wider SD/confidence tags, no home/favourite bias term.
theories.parameter_change: keep as is
theories.effect_size: engine-minus-market MAE +0.03 (week 1) vs +0.12 (weeks 4-16)
theories.data_used: games + nfelo merge, REG 2009-2025
theories.caveats: Lines are compressed in week 1 (|line| 4.5 vs 5.1-5.4) by both market and ratings; nothing to fix.

theories.hypothesis: In the final regular-season week (17 pre-2021, 18 from 2021) rest/motivation (resting starters, eliminated teams) makes engine lines worse than the market; favourites/home bias may exist.
theories.method: MAE market vs nfelo raw/close by week; |market - rating line| gap final week vs weeks 4-16 (Welch t); combination regression; favourite cover by line size; totals; OOS shrink-to-market weights a in {1, .5, .25, 0} on the ORIGINATOR proxy, 2022-25.
theories.metric: MAE engine vs market (pts); gap; combination weights; OOS MAE
theories.result: Final week: market MAE 10.15 vs nfelo raw 10.57 (+0.42); test 2022-25 n=64: 8.57 vs 9.85 (+1.28, the largest weekly engine deficit). |market - rating line| gap 2.97 vs 1.71 in weeks 4-16 (p<0.001): the market is pricing information the ratings cannot see. Combination weights final week: rating 0.24 (se 0.22) vs market 0.92 (se 0.21); test: -0.40 (se 0.30) vs 1.42 (se 0.28). Big favourites (|line| >= 7, n=103) beat the nfelo raw line by +3.11 (se 1.42) but only +1.63 (se 1.36) vs market. Home bias +1.27 (se 0.82; test +2.15 se 1.36, n.s.). Totals +0.47 (se 0.83) n.s. OOS: final-week MAE 9.84 -> 8.73 with a=0.25 (n=64); full-test MAE 9.7435 -> 9.6784 (-0.065); a=0 gives 8.57.
theories.recommendation: Treat the final week as a market-anchored week: publish LOW confidence and shrink the originator line hard toward the market close (or cap its deviation) unless explicit lineup/resting information is modelled. This is the largest OOS MAE gain of any schedule change tested.
theories.parameter_change: Final REG week: spread = 0.25 x model + 0.75 x market close (equivalently cap |model - market| at ~1.5 pts); confidence tag = LOW regardless of blend SD. No total or home-bias adjustment.
theories.effect_size: engine minus market MAE +0.42 (all) / +1.28 (test); shrink gains 1.1 pts MAE on final-week games
theories.uncertainty: test n=64; gap test p<0.001; combination-weight se 0.2-0.3
theories.data_used: games + nfelo merge; OOS in 06_recommendation.py section (d)
theories.caveats: An originator that defers to the market in week 18 has no edge that week by construction; the alternative is modelling rest/clinch status explicitly (standings not built here). Penultimate week shows a smaller version (gap and +0.25 MAE deficit).

theories.hypothesis: Some schedule effects are already inside the market and/or the nfelo component, so the spec should not add them again; identify which and the residual sizes.
theories.method: Market-pricing regressions (mkt_spread ~ rating-only line + schedule dummies), nfelo-mod decomposition (00b), residuals after nfelo's mods (err_nraw), OOS proxy comparison of the spec table vs candidates (06), rolling-origin rest refits.
theories.metric: pts priced by market / nfelo vs realized; OOS MAE and affected-game bias on the ORIGINATOR proxy (0.46 nfelo + 0.54 rating-only)
theories.result: Market prices: rest 0.145/day (se 0.014), bye 1.0 (se 0.14) symmetric, 6-day/10-day rests 0.25, primetime west edge ~0, 3-zone travel ~0 (leans -0.04 to home), distance +0.16/1000mi toward home. nfelo prices: bye asymmetric (home 0.34 / away 1.52, net correct), tz mod +0.9 to hosts of 1pm west visitors (overshoots; re-applying it to the blend: OOS MAE +0.006, CI [-0.016, +0.029]). Spec table as written OOS: MAE +0.0076 vs no adjustments (bye double count and the wrong-sign west clause); candidate (strip nfelo bye/tz mods + 0.15/day rest): MAE -0.0004, rested-side bias on affected games +0.14 (vs +0.45 unadjusted in rolling-origin).
theories.recommendation: Rest and bye are fully priced by the market; the engine should match the market's sizes once (not nfelo + spec). Travel/time-zone terms are not priced by the market and, where signal exists, run opposite to the spec. Remove the spec's travel clause and the tz double count.
theories.parameter_change: Consolidated schedule table: (1) rest: -0.15 x clip(home_rest - away_rest, -7, 7) applied once (strip nfelo bye mods; week 1 exempt); (2) delete short-week and bye clauses (subsumed) and the west-to-east 10am clause; (3) PFF/Cole site HFA = hfa_mod/25 (no + tz term); (4) final REG week: 0.25 model / 0.75 market, LOW tag; (5) optional flags, LOW-MED: +1.0 to the 3-zone traveller, +1.0 to the more-western team in primetime; (6) no TNF total or week-1 terms. Cap of the schedule adjustments: |sum| <= 2.0.
theories.effect_size: spec table vs candidate: OOS MAE 9.7515 vs 9.7435; affected-game bias -0.65 vs +0.14
theories.uncertainty: MAE differences are within bootstrap noise (+-0.02); bias and pricing coefficients are the decisive evidence
theories.data_used: games + nfelo merge 2009-2025; proxy uses nfelo raw (primary) and nfelo published close (secondary) as the nfelo component
theories.caveats: PFF and Cole have no history locally; the rating-only nfelo line stands in for both, so the 0.54 share is a proxy. All scripts re-run via run_all.sh (log: _run_all.log).

experts.summary:
Setup: REG games 2009-2025 (4,431 with closing lines; 3,861 nfelo-joined weeks 2+; test 2022-25 n=1,023-1,087), residuals measured against four lines - market close, nfelo published close (market-regressed, ~0.7 toward market), nfelo unregressed (-nfelo_dif_base/25, which I verified decomposes into ratings + hfa_base + tz + QB + div + surface + bye mods) and a rating-only line with nfelo's bye/tz mods stripped (a stand-in for the PFF/Cole paths, which carry no rest or travel terms). Sign checks pass (corr(mkt_spread, margin) = -0.44). PFF/Cole history does not exist locally; nfelo Elo is the rating series throughout.

What I would change first, in order:
1. Delete the 'west-to-east 10am kick -0.4..-0.8' clause (T4a, REJECTED, HIGH): PT/MT teams at 1pm ET do slightly better than ratings (home -0.5, se 0.7, n=383; fade-west ATS 0.462) and the spec's rule is OOS-negative. In the same edit fix the site-HFA double count: hfa_mod already contains home_time_advantage_mod, and re-applying nfelo's tz mod does not help OOS (+0.006 MAE).
2. Replace the short-week and bye clauses with one linear rest term, -0.15 x clip(home_rest - away_rest, -7, 7), applied once after stripping nfelo's bye mods (T2/T3, SUPPORTED, MED). Rest is worth +0.18/day vs ratings (p=0.02) and the market prices exactly +0.145/day (bye = 1.0, symmetric); the current spec adds +0.5..1.0 on top of nfelo's 0.46 x (0.3..1.5) and over-adjusts. Rolling-origin: rested-side bias +0.45 -> +0.04 on 915 games. Asymmetric short rest never occurs (n=8 in 17 seasons, 0 since 2021) and TNF both-short games show no total or variance effect (T1, INCONCLUSIVE/REJECTED) - no TNF term.
3. Final regular-season week: shrink to the market (0.25 model / 0.75 close) and tag LOW (T5b, SUPPORTED, MED). The engine's MAE deficit vs market is +0.42 all-sample and +1.28 in 2022-25, the market-vs-ratings gap is 3.0 vs 1.7 pts (p<0.001), and combination weights put ~0.9-1.4 on the market; this is the largest OOS MAE gain available (-0.065 on the full test set, -1.1 on affected games). Week 1 needs nothing (T5a, REJECTED): engine-minus-market MAE +0.03 (se 0.13), residual SD identical, no bias.
4. Optional, reviewed annually (T4b MED / T4c LOW): the travel data run opposite to folklore. Away teams crossing 3 zones beat the market by ~2 pts (team+season FE -2.3 to home, p<0.01; 2018-25 traveller ATS 159-113, 0.585; OOS 2022-25 -2.0, se 1.05) but the effect is absent 2009-17, so I recommend a half-size +1.0 to the 3-zone traveller as a flag. The more-western team in primetime shows +1.5 (fit p=0.03, test p=0.11, flat across zones, day-game placebo null) - INCONCLUSIVE, optional +1.0 flag. Neither is priced by the market; MAE bootstrap CIs include zero (individually -0.012..-0.014, jointly -0.026 [CI -0.057, +0.001]).

Caveat on metrics: 1-pt adjustments on 10-15% of games cannot move season MAE detectably (bootstrap +-0.02), so the decisive evidence is signed bias on affected games, market-pricing coefficients, and ATS - all reported with n, se and p. Scripts: /home/user/originator-2026-w01/research/experts/schedule/ (00..06, common.py, run_all.sh -> _run_all.log).

theories.hypothesis: The closing line misses systematically in identifiable segments (favorite size, home/away favorite, primetime, divisional, Week 1, playoffs; totals by size and roof), so an originator can legitimately shade those segments.
theories.method: For every segment: mean closing-line error (margin + mkt_spread; total - line), 95% CI, one-sample t-test, MAE, and the cover rate of the natural side (home / favorite / over) with an exact binomial test. Everything reported for ALL, fit era (2009-2021) and test era (2022-2025) so a bias must persist out of sample to count. 31 spread segments and 17 total segments.
theories.metric: mean error (pts) vs close with CI/p; ATS cover rate of home/favorite/over; MAE
theories.result: Market spread bias overall +0.06 (CI -0.31..+0.44), home cover 49.0%. Only 3 spread cells and 1 total cell reach p<0.05 in the fit era, about what chance predicts for 48 segments (~2.4 expected); none persists at p<0.05 in 2022-25. Details: home fav 0-2.5: bias -1.32 (p=0.017, n=548), fit -1.58 (p=0.02) -> test -0.64 (p=0.50), test home cover 50.0%. |spread|>=10: bias +1.27 (p=0.014), test +2.69 (p=0.013) BUT favorite cover 49.7% (test 50.0%): a blowout-tail (mean) effect, not a cover edge. SNF +2.17 (p=0.025) in fit -> -0.05 in test. Primetime overall +0.31 (p=0.46), divisional -0.19 (p=0.55), Week 1 -0.86 (p=0.28, home cover 47.7%), playoffs +0.68 (p=0.46; favorite cover 45.1%, n=195, p=0.20). Totals: overall +0.51 (p=0.009) but over rate 49.4% (right skew, not edge); dome +1.40 (p=0.007) with over 52.3% (p=0.24), fit +1.58 -> test +0.97 (p=0.31, over 49.8%); closed roof test +2.70 (p=0.013) but over 53.3% ns; total-size bins: no bias, MAE rises 10.3 (<=40) to 11.9 (53.5+); wind>=15: -1.31 (p=0.050), under 55.1% (p=0.055), same sign both eras (fit -1.37, test -1.00) - the only same-sign cover-rate lean, n=377.
theories.recommendation: Keep as is: do not shade the origin spread for favorite size, home/away favorite, primetime, divisional, Week 1 or playoffs; do not shade totals by size or roof. Treat the market close as unbiased in every segment tested. The mean-vs-median gap on 10+ favorites and dome totals is skew: the origin number should target the median (cover probability), not the mean. Hand the wind>=15 under lean (-1.3 pts, 55% under, borderline) to the totals expert; it is consistent with the spec's existing wind adjustment, not an additional shade.
theories.parameter_change: None to the spread/total formulas. Optional confidence-tag tweak: spread error SD is flat across |spread| (13.1-13.6) so no size-dependent SD is needed; total error SD rises from 12.9 (line<=40) to 14.6 (line>=53.5), so widen the totals MED/LOW SD thresholds by ~10% for lines >= 53.5.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv 2009-2025 scored games with closing spread/total (4630), joined to nfelo_games.csv via kit.merged()
theories.effect_size: All persistent segment biases |bias| < 1 pt and cover rates within 47-53% of 50%; largest same-sign OOS effect is wind>=15 unders at 55.1% (n=377)
theories.expected_impact: Zero improvement available from segment shading; avoiding false shades prevents ~0.5-1.5 pt self-inflicted errors in those segments
theories.caveats: 48 segments tested; p<0.05 hits are at the multiple-comparison noise floor. Playoff n=199, neutral n=79, Week-1 n=271 are too small to exclude 1-pt effects. Cover rates exclude pushes.
theories.uncertainty: 95% CIs on segment biases are typically +/-0.5 to +/-1.5 pts; a true 0.5-pt segment bias could not be detected here.

theories.hypothesis: The direction of open-to-close movement predicts results beyond the closing line, so an originator should lean with steam (publish past the close in the direction of the move).
theories.method: nfelo_games.csv home_line_open/close (same source, negative = home favored), move = close - open. (a) MAE open vs close and ATS of betting the close's side at the OPEN (value of the move vs the opener); (b) OLS of residual-vs-close (margin + close) on move, HC1 SE, fit<=2021 / test 2022-25; (c) ATS of betting WITH steam at the close by |move| bucket and era, plus per-season stability; (d) nfelo-pick x steam-agreement cross-tab; (e) totals move (only 2024-25 have an opener).
theories.metric: OLS coefficient of residual on move; ATS rate with steam at the close (binomial p); MAE open vs close
theories.result: The move carries information vs the OPEN: close MAE 10.07 vs open 10.19; betting the close's side at the open wins 56.0% (n=3291, CI 54.3-57.7) for |move|>=0.5, 58.1% (n=2176) for >=1, 59.6% (n=1032) for >=2. Beyond the CLOSE there is nothing: OLS coef +0.043 (SE 0.109, p=0.70); fit +0.13 (p=0.28), test -0.19 (p=0.43). With-steam ATS at the close 50.4% (n=3291, p=0.67); |move|>=1: 51.2% (n=2176, p=0.30), fit 50.9%, test 52.1% (n=467, p=0.40); only 9 of 17 seasons above 50%. Steam agreeing with nfelo's pick: 53.9% (n=690) vs 50.4% when disagreeing (n=597), diff +3.4%, z=1.21, p=0.23; both below 50% in the test era. Totals (2024-25, n=418 with a move): FADING the move wins 56.4% (CI 51.6-61.1, p=0.010; 58.0% in 2024, 53.5% in 2025), OLS coef -0.76 (p=0.054), and the close is not better than the open (MAE 10.09 vs 10.04): only two seasons, single opener source, labelled inconclusive.
theories.recommendation: Do not lean with steam. Benchmark the origin number against the latest available market line (the close fully incorporates the move); never anchor to the opener. No steam parameter in the engine. Keep a watch item: totals line moves faded at 56% over 2024-25 (n=418) - re-test after the 2026 season before acting.
theories.parameter_change: None. Explicitly: steam_lean = 0 for spreads. Use closing (latest) line as the comparison benchmark; if an opener is used for early-week numbers, expect it to be ~0.12 pts/game worse in MAE and 56-60% ATS-inferior to the close.
theories.data_used: nfelo_games.csv home_line_open/close 2009-2025 (4310 scored games), nfelo_home_line_close for the model-pick test; total_line_open/close 2024-25 (559 games, 418 with a move)
theories.effect_size: Beyond the close: 50.4-51.2% ATS, OLS +0.04 pts per point of move (CI about -0.17..+0.26). Vs the open: +6 to +10 pts of ATS rate.
theories.expected_impact: No gain from a steam lean; using the latest line instead of the opener avoids ~0.12 pts/game of benchmark error.
theories.caveats: nfelo's opener/closer source is a single consensus feed; reverse-line-movement (bet-%) data not available locally, so 'sharp vs public' steam cannot be separated. Totals opener exists only for 2024-25.
theories.uncertainty: With-steam ATS 95% CI at |move|>=1 is roughly 49.1-53.3% (n=2176); a residual 1-2% steam effect cannot be ruled out but is below the vig.

theories.hypothesis: Final margins pile on 3, 7, 6, 10, 4, 1; given the push probabilities, a key-number-aware rounding rule for origin spreads at x.25/x.75 near 3 or 7 beats the spec's half-up rule in EV vs the market.
theories.method: (1) Distribution of |margin| and push probability P(fav_margin == line | line == k) with Wilson CIs, by era. (2) Pooled-EV calculator: a latent origin at x.75/x.25 is represented by the pooled games whose closing line was on the two adjacent grid numbers (favorite frame), giving empirical P(win/push/loss) for any grid market m near x; rules A half-up (2.75->3, 3.25->3.5), B away-from-key-to-half (2.75->2.5, 6.75->6.5), C toward-key (3.25->3, 7.25->7), E probability-space (landing masses fit on <=2021), D in-sample ceiling; bets triggered when |published - market| >= T; cells weighted by the empirical market-vs-model gap distribution (historic_projected_spreads.csv, SD 2.42); 1000-draw bootstrap CIs and fit/test era split. (3) OOS backtest 2022-25 with a continuous Elo+HFA+QB origin fit on <=2021. (4) Backtest of nfelo-vs-market gaps that cross 3/7 vs equal gaps that do not.
theories.metric: push/landing probabilities; EV per game evaluated (units per unit risked at -110) by rule; ATS units in OOS backtest
theories.result: Distribution: |margin|=3 in 14.6% of games (CI 13.7-15.7), 7: 8.8%, 6: 6.5%, 10: 5.1%, 14: 5.0%, 4: 5.0%, 1: 4.3%; 23.4% of games end on exactly 3 or 7. Push at the line: 3: 8.9% (n=665, CI 6.9-11.3), 7: 6.1% (n=294, CI 3.9-9.5), 10: 7.9% (n=139), 6: 4.2%, 4: 1.4%, 1: 1.6%. Fair prices from the pools: at latent 2.75 laying 2.5 is fair -102 but laying 3 is +118 and 3.5 is +139 (n=1064); at latent 3.25 laying 3 is -104 and 3.5 is +115 (n=1125); 6.75: lay 6.5 -104, 7 +108 (n=504); 7.25: lay 7 -101, 7.5 +114 (n=514). Rule EV averaged over the 8 key-adjacent latents, T=1.0: A 0.0490, B 0.0512, C 0.0495, E 0.0496, ceiling 0.0559 per game evaluated. B-A at 2.75: +0.0142 (boot CI +0.002..+0.026, P>0=0.99) at T=1.0, +0.0092 (P=0.88) at T=0.5, +0.0077 (P=0.955) at T=1.5; era split fit +0.019 / test +0.003 at T=1.0 (test -0.006 at T=0.5). B-A at 6.75: +0.0035 (ns). C-A at 3.25/7.25: +0.001 to +0.007 (ns). Same-size gaps differ enormously by key crossing: latent 2.75 vs market 3.5 (0.75 pt across 3) dog EV +0.111, vs market 2.0 (0.75 pt, no key) favorite EV +0.001. OOS backtest (1139 games; 7.8% land on 2.75/3.25/6.75/7.25): rules change the decision in 7-21 games, units A vs B +2.7 vs +1.6 (T=0.5) and -1.1 vs -2.4 (T=1.0) - noise. Key-cross backtest with nfelo: gap 0.5-1.0 crossing 3/7 50.0% (n=50) vs 49.4% no key (n=475), p=0.93; gap>=1.5 crossing 48.5% (n=198) vs 54.8% (n=453) - no directional edge from crossing.
theories.recommendation: Adopt rule B for the published number: an origin spread at x.75 directly below a key number rounds DOWN to the half (2.75 -> 2.5, 6.75 -> 6.5); all other quarters keep half-up (3.25 -> 3.5, 7.25 -> 7.5 are already right). It is costless, weakly positive (+0.9 to +1.4% EV per game in the 2.75 cell, bootstrap P 0.88-0.99), never materially negative, and matches the fair prices (a 2.75 number is priced like a 2.5, not a 3). Do NOT expect the rounding rule to matter much: the affected cells are ~8% of games and the total effect is ~0.1% of EV. The substantive change is in T4 (price edges in probability space).
theories.parameter_change: round(x): if frac(x)==0.75 and floor(x)+1 in {3,7}: return floor(x)+0.5; else half-up (frac 0.25-0.74 -> .5, 0.75-1.24 -> next .0). Apply in the favorite frame (|spread|), then restore sign.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv 2009-2025 (4630 games with close); nfelo_games.csv nfelo_home_line_close and starting Elo (as the model series - no PFF/Cole history exists); historic_projected_spreads.csv (2021-2026, 1431 games) for the gap-weight distribution
theories.effect_size: Rule B vs half-up: +0.014 EV/game evaluated at latent 2.75 (T=1.0), ~0 at 6.75; averaged over all key-adjacent quarters +0.002 per game; about 0.1% of total EV
theories.expected_impact: Negligible on MAE (rounding does not change the continuous number); small positive on EV of triggered bets; main value is consistency with the key-number price structure
theories.caveats: The pooled-EV method assumes a latent x.75 behaves like the mixture of games closed at x.5 and x+1 (empirical, but it inherits the market's own cover rates at those numbers, e.g. favorites at exactly -3 cover only 42.7%, n=665, dog rate 53.1%, p=0.13, which is not established as persistent). OOS rounding backtest n is far below 150 decisions and is uninformative by construction. nfelo's line is itself grid-rounded and market-regressed, so the key-cross backtest tests small gaps only.
theories.uncertainty: Bootstrap CIs on rule differences are about +/-0.012 EV/game at 3 and +/-0.02 at 7; era split flips sign in one of four cells.

theories.hypothesis: The value of a half point depends on which integer it crosses; an empirical table around 3 and 7 should replace the spec's implicit 'every half point is equal' edge accounting.
theories.method: Landing mass m_k = P(favorite margin == k | closing line within +/-2 of k) for k=1..14, with Wilson CIs, era split, and window sensitivity (+/-1, +/-2, +/-3). Half-point value = m_k in cover-probability points; cents equivalent at ~50% via d(price)/dp ~ 400 cents per unit probability. Validated against the exact empirical pool outcomes (latent 2.75 vs markets 1.5-4.5).
theories.metric: landing mass per integer (cover-probability points), cents per half point, formula-vs-empirical EV check
theories.result: m_3 = 0.088 (CI 0.078-0.099, n=2627; fit 0.081, test 0.108; windows +/-1/2/3: 0.087/0.088/0.087), m_7 = 0.062 (CI 0.050-0.076, n=1409; 0.063/0.058), m_6 = 0.041, m_10 = 0.037, m_14 = 0.052, m_4 = 0.030, m_8 = 0.032, m_2 = 0.028, m_5 = 0.027, m_1 = 0.022, m_9 = 0.006, m_11 = 0.014, m_12 = 0.016, m_13 = 0.033. Generic (non-3/7) mean 0.028. Half point across 3 = 18 cents, across 7 = 12 cents, 6 = 8c, 10 = 7c, 14 = 10c, generic = 6c. Edge formula (favorite frame, fair line x, grid market m): if m > x bet dog with P(win) = 0.5 + sum of m_k over integers strictly between x and m, P(push) = m_m if m is an integer; symmetric on the favorite side; EV per unit at -110 = (P(win) - 1.1 P(loss))/1.1. Formula vs empirical pool at latent 2.75: market 3.5 +0.109 vs +0.111, 4.0 +0.139 vs +0.139, 4.5 +0.166 vs +0.164, 3.0 +0.036 vs +0.032, 2.5 -0.045 vs -0.036; it overstates laying the key from the near side (latent 3.25 vs market 3: formula +0.036, empirical -0.025) - the one cell to guard.
theories.recommendation: Replace point-distance edge thresholds with the probability-space EV from the mass table (masses fit on <=2021 differ from full-sample by <=0.007 at 3 and 7, so the table is stable). A 0.75-pt gap crossing 3 is worth EV +0.11; the same gap not crossing any key is worth ~0.00, and current point-space thresholds cannot tell them apart. Add one guard: do not lay exactly -3 or -7 when the origin number is within 0.5 above it (3.0-3.5, 7.0-7.5) - the formula's +0.036 there is empirically -0.025.
theories.parameter_change: MASS = {1:0.022, 2:0.028, 3:0.088, 4:0.030, 5:0.027, 6:0.041, 7:0.062, 8:0.032, 9:0.006, 10:0.037, 11:0.014, 12:0.016, 13:0.033, 14:0.052, >=15: 0.020}. edge_prob(x, m) = sum(MASS[k] for integer k strictly between x and m); push = MASS[m] if m integer else 0; P(win) = 0.5 + edge_prob; P(loss) = 0.5 - edge_prob - push; EV = (P(win) - 1.1*P(loss))/1.1; act when EV >= 0.02 (equivalent to a 0.5-pt gap across 3, a 1-pt gap across 7, or ~1.5 pts across generic integers). Guard: no bet laying m in {3,7} when m <= x <= m+0.5. Confidence tags can use the same EV rather than point gaps.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv 2009-2025, favorite-frame margins vs closing spread
theories.effect_size: Half point at 3 is 3.1x a generic half point (8.8 vs 2.8 cover-prob points, 18c vs 6c); at 7 it is 2.2x (6.2 pts, 12c); 6 and 10 are 1.3-1.5x; 4 and 1 are generic
theories.expected_impact: Reclassifies which origin-vs-market gaps are actionable: e.g. 0.75-pt gaps across 3 (EV +0.11) become plays and 1.0-pt gaps that cross nothing (EV 0 to +0.03) become passes; per-bet EV in the calculator rises from 0.082 (half-up, T=1) to 0.086 at equal bet frequency
theories.caveats: Masses are conditional on the line being within 2 pts of the integer; for gaps > 3 pts the mass at a distant key is somewhat lower (window +/-3 gives m_7 = 0.057). Masses at 13-14 rest on n=249-301. The table describes the margin distribution, not a market inefficiency: the T3 key-cross backtest showed no directional edge from crossing keys with nfelo's small gaps.
theories.uncertainty: m_3 CI 0.078-0.099, m_7 0.050-0.076; cents conversions are linear approximations valid near 50%.

theories.hypothesis: Totals have key numbers (41, 44, 47, 51) with enough mass that the totals rounding rule should be key-number-aware.
theories.method: Unconditional distribution of total points 30-60 with a local 5-point moving baseline; landing mass P(total == k | line within +/-3 of k) with CIs and era split; push probability at integer lines; comparison with spread masses; pooled-EV rounding comparison (same method as T3) for latents at k+/-0.25 around 41/44/47/51 (rules: half-up vs away-from-key vs toward-key), with 500-draw bootstraps and a placebo at non-key totals 43/46/49.
theories.metric: landing mass and push probability per total; EV difference between rounding rules
theories.result: Key totals carry modestly more mass: 41: 4.0%, 44: 4.1%, 47: 3.5%, 51: 5.1% (mean 4.2%) vs 2.7% for other integers 34-57 (ratio 1.53); 40 (3.8%), 43 (3.6%) and 55 (4.4%, n=321) are just as heavy. Push at integer lines pooled 2.3%: key 2.9% vs other 2.0%. Odd totals are 53% of games. Extra half-point value at a key total = 1.4 cover-prob points (~3 cents) vs 8.8 points (18c) at spread-3. Rounding EV: mean (alt - half-up) +0.001 (T=0.5) / +0.002 (T=1.0) per game evaluated, mean |diff| 0.011-0.012, all 16 bootstrap CIs include 0, signs inconsistent (40.75: -0.018, 46.75: +0.022), and the placebo at non-key totals shows the same range (-0.013 to +0.022).
theories.recommendation: Keep half-up rounding for totals; do not add a key-number rule. The push probability at any integer total (2-3%) is small enough that the .0 vs .5 choice is worth ~1 cent; the team-total 'sum preserved' rounding can stay as specified.
theories.parameter_change: None. Optional for EV accounting only: push_prob_total(m) = 0.029 if m in {41,44,47,51} else 0.020 for integer m, 0 for half totals.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv 2009-2025 totals vs closing total line
theories.effect_size: Key-total mass 4.2% vs 2.7% generic: +1.4 cover-prob points per half point; rounding-rule EV differences ~0 +/- 0.012 per game (noise)
theories.expected_impact: No EV or MAE gain available from totals rounding changes
theories.caveats: Pools per latent total are 131-469 games; the placebo shows the same magnitude of apparent 'effects', which is why the point estimates are not trusted.
theories.uncertainty: Landing-mass CIs are +/-1 pt; the key vs generic difference (1.4 pts) is real but economically small.

experts.summary: Market microstructure verdicts (all scripts and logs in /home/user/originator-2026-w01/research/experts/market/, run_all.sh re-runs everything; nfelo Elo/lines used as the model series since no PFF or Cole history exists locally). 1) Closing-line efficiency by segment (n=4630, 2009-2025, fit/test split): REJECTED - no segment (favorite size, home/away favorite, primetime, divisional, Week 1, playoffs, total size, roof) shows a bias that survives out of sample; the p<0.05 hits (home fav 0-2.5 at -1.3, |spread|>=10 at +1.3, dome totals at +1.4) are at the multiple-comparison noise floor or are mean/skew effects with ~50% cover rates. Keep the number unshaded; only wind>=15 unders (55%, borderline) leans the same way in both eras and belongs to the totals adjustment already in the spec. 2) Open-to-close steam (n=4310): REJECTED beyond the close - OLS coef +0.04 (p=0.70), with-steam ATS 50.4-51.2%; but the move is worth 56-60% ATS versus the OPENER, so always benchmark against the latest line and never the opener. Totals moves faded at 56.4% over 2024-25 (n=418, p=0.01) - two seasons only, monitor, do not act. 3) Key numbers: 3 lands 14.6% of games (push 8.9% at the line), 7 8.8% (push 6.1%); 6, 10, 14 are secondary (4-5%); 4 and 1 are generic. Half point across 3 = 8.8 cover-prob points (18 cents), across 7 = 6.2 (12c), generic integer 2.8 (6c). Fair prices show an origin 2.75 is a 2.5 (lay 2.5 fair -102, lay 3 +118), so the one rounding tweak worth making is x.75 just below 3 or 7 rounds DOWN to the half (2.75->2.5, 6.75->6.5), everything else half-up; it is weakly positive (+1.4% EV/game in that cell, bootstrap P 0.99 at T=1) and never materially negative, but affects ~8% of games for ~0.1% of total EV, so INCONCLUSIVE as a lever. 4) The change I would make first: replace point-distance edge thresholds with the probability-space EV from the landing-mass table (formula and constants given in T4) - the same 0.75-pt gap is worth EV +0.11 when it crosses 3 and ~0.00 when it does not, and the engine currently cannot tell them apart; guard against laying exactly -3/-7 from the near side. 5) Totals key numbers (41/44/47/51): mass 4.2% vs 2.7% generic, worth ~3 cents per half point; rounding-rule EV differences are indistinguishable from a placebo at 43/46/49 - REJECTED, keep half-up. Order of implementation: T4 probability-space edges (HIGH confidence, substantive), then the T3 2.75/6.75 rounding tweak (free), nothing for segments, steam or totals rounding.

theories.hypothesis: Larger model/market disagreement (|nfelo close - market close|, |nfelo open - nfelo close|, market open->close move, or a genuine engine-vs-engine SD) predicts a larger absolute error of the MARKET closing number, i.e. disagreement flags games whose outcome is more uncertain.
theories.method: Frame = nflverse games joined to nfelo (4310 games 2009-25 with closing spread and nfelo line). Model number nfelo_b = -(nfelo_dif_base/25) = the UNREGRESSED nfelo line (validated: r=0.96 vs home_line_pre_regression in historic_projected_spreads; the README's 'nfelo close' is market-regressed and sits only 0.54 pts from the close on average, so it understates disagreement). Proxies: D_base=|nfelo_b-close|, D_reg=|nfelo_close-close|, D_nmove=|nfelo open-close|, D_mmove=|mkt open-close|; and sd2 = |nfelo_b - published 538 qbelo line|/sqrt(2) (a real 2-engine SD, script 08; a 3-engine version reconstructed from squared errors in script 06 is flagged as biased and not used). OLS |e_mkt| ~ D fit on <=2021, slope re-estimated on 2022-25 with HC1 SE; Spearman; tercile means (fit-era edges) with 2000-rep bootstrap CIs; Welch T3-T1; joint F-test of 8 candidate drivers on the full sample; per-season RMSE by D band (script 10c).
theories.metric: OOS slope of |err| per point of disagreement; Spearman rho; T3-T1 mean |err|; realized RMSE by tercile; joint F p-value
theories.result: Market spread |err| vs D_base: OOS slope +0.019 pts per pt of D (se 0.165, p=0.91), Spearman +0.028 (p=0.35), terciles 9.12/9.80/9.71 mean |err| (RMSE 12.12/12.44/12.76), T3-T1 = +0.60 (p=0.33). D_reg: slope -0.33 (p=0.21). D_nmove: +0.30 (p=0.24). D_mmove: +0.03 (p=0.88). Genuine engine SD sd2 -> market |err|: slope +0.185 (p=0.33), fit-era -0.12 (p=0.45). Joint F-test of D_base, |spread|, total, dome, early, late, playoff, market move on |e_mkt| over n=4310: p=0.71, R^2=0.001. Per-season market RMSE by D band shows no consistent ordering (2019: 12.4/12.9/15.4; 2022: 10.8/13.2/10.4). Totals: D_tot -> market total |err| slope -0.011 (p=0.91), Spearman -0.013. Outcome variance is homoscedastic w.r.t. everything available.
theories.recommendation: Stop treating engine disagreement as a measure of game uncertainty. It carries no information about how far the result will land from the closing line, for spreads or totals.
theories.parameter_change: Remove 'spread SD <=1.2 HIGH / 1.2-2.2 MED / >2.2 LOW' (and 1.8/3.0 for totals) as a statement about outcome uncertainty. Use a single per-season base sigma for the outcome (see T4) with no disagreement, favorite-size, total, roof or week modifiers.
theories.effect_size: +0.02 pts |err| per point of disagreement (95% CI approx -0.30 to +0.34); tercile RMSE 12.1 vs 12.8; variance ratio LOW/HIGH tag 0.95-1.04
theories.uncertainty: Test n=1139, fit n=3171, joint test n=4310; all p>0.2; four proxies and a real engine SD agree
theories.caveats: Only nfelo (+538 qbelo) is available as an engine; PFF/Cole history does not exist locally, so the model's actual 3-engine SD is not observed. The 2-engine sd2 (nfelo vs qbelo) is the closest analog and is null as well. D_reg and D_nmove are compressed because nfelo regresses to the market.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv, nfelo_games.csv (nfelo_dif_base, lines open/close), nfelo_scored_individual_games.csv (qbelo_home_line_close_rounded), historic_projected_spreads.csv (validation only)

theories.hypothesis: Larger |model - market| predicts a larger absolute error of the MODEL's own number.
theories.method: Same frame and estimators as T1a with target |e_nb| = |margin + nfelo_b| (and |e_telo| for the spec's Elo-implied total T_elo = 45.69 + 0.35*(home_pts_vs_avg + away_pts_vs_avg)). Plus a decomposition check: e_model = e_mkt + (model - mkt), so E[e_model^2] = E[e_mkt^2] + D^2 + 2*cov; predicted vs realized RMSE by tercile. Engine SD sd2 tested jointly with distance-to-market D2_mkt (script 08).
theories.metric: OOS slope; Spearman; T3-T1; predicted sqrt(RMSE_mkt^2 + mean D^2) vs realized RMSE
theories.result: Spread model |err| vs D_base: OOS slope +0.364 (se 0.175, p=0.038; fit-era +0.302, p=0.003), Spearman +0.067 (p=0.025), T3-T1 = +1.18 pts (Welch p=0.056), tercile RMSE 12.13/12.60/13.39. corr(e_mkt, nfelo_b - mkt) = +0.03, so the identity predicts 12.13/12.53/13.31: the model's extra error IS the disagreement, not extra outcome variance. Same for the 2-engine mean vs D2_mkt: predicted 12.55/12.19/13.31 vs realized 12.57/12.18/13.56; engine-vs-engine sd2 adds nothing once D2_mkt is in (sd2 coef +0.18, p=0.39; D2_mkt +0.46, p=0.015). Totals: Elo-total |err| vs D_tot slope +0.330 (p=0.0004), Spearman +0.075, T3 RMSE 14.47 vs T1 13.22. D_nmove predicts model |err| OOS (slope 0.56, p=0.027) but not in-sample (p=0.43) -> inconclusive proxy.
theories.recommendation: Redefine the confidence tag as 'distance of the published number from the market close' = expected EXCESS error of our number vs the market, which is what disagreement actually measures. The engine-vs-engine SD should not drive the tag.
theories.parameter_change: Tag driver: D = |published spread - market close| (and |published total - market total|), not the SD across nfelo/PFF/Cole. Expected excess RMSE of a number D points from the close = sqrt(BASE^2 + D^2) - BASE (BASE 12.5 spread: D=1.5 -> +0.09, D=3 -> +0.35, D=5 -> +0.96; total BASE 13.1: D=2.5 -> +0.24, D=5 -> +0.92, D=7 -> +1.75).
theories.effect_size: +0.36 pts mean |err| per point of D (95% CI +0.02 to +0.71); T3 vs T1 RMSE +1.26 spread, +1.25 total
theories.uncertainty: n=1139 test; p=0.038 for the slope, but the mechanical decomposition matches to within 0.1 RMSE in all terciles and in both eras
theories.caveats: This is an accounting identity given the market is unbiased; it does not mean disagreement 'predicts' anything about the game. Holds against the CLOSE; against the OPEN line c must be shrunk (see T4).
theories.data_used: same as T1a

theories.hypothesis: The SD thresholds (spread 1.2/2.2, total 1.8/3.0) are sensible, i.e. they separate games into materially different error levels; disagreement levels can be mapped to 10th/50th/90th-percentile errors.
theories.method: Unconditional |err| percentiles; quantile regression |err| ~ D_base at q=.1/.5/.9 fit on <=2021 with OOS coverage of the fitted quantiles by D bin; |err| by D bin including the bins implied by the literal thresholds (for two numbers SD=|diff|/sqrt(2): 1.2 -> 1.70, 2.2 -> 3.11); the literal thresholds applied to the genuine 2-engine SD sd2 (script 08) with realized RMSE per tag and one-sided F-tests; same for totals with D_tot (SD 1.8 -> 2.55, 3.0 -> 4.24).
theories.metric: realized RMSE / |err| quantiles per tag; variance ratio LOW/HIGH with F-test; OOS coverage of fitted quantiles by D bin
theories.result: Market |err| percentiles (test) p10/p50/p90 = 1.0/7.5/21.5; model number 1.4/7.5/21.9; totals 1.5/8.0/21.5. Quantile regression on D_base: market q90 slope +0.58/pt (p=0.02 in fit) but OOS coverage of the fitted q10/q50/q90 by D bin is flat (0.07-0.17 / 0.48-0.60 / 0.89-0.96) -> no usable mapping; model q10 slope +0.31/pt (p<0.0001), q50 +0.27 (p=0.016) = an offset by D, not variance. Literal thresholds on the real engine SD sd2: HIGH 51% / MED 27% / LOW 22% of games; realized market RMSE 12.48/12.21/12.71 (LOW/HIGH ratio 1.04, p=0.37); engine-mean RMSE 12.65/12.34/13.60 (ratio 1.16, p=0.089), and in the fit era LOW had the LOWEST RMSE (13.15 vs 13.29) -> unstable sign. SD-equivalent cuts on D_base: 60/26/14% with market RMSE 12.39/12.72/12.01. Games at D_base p10/p50/p90 (0.26/1.37/3.47) show mean market |err| 7.8/9.9/10.0 and model |err| 7.8/10.0/10.5. Totals: market total RMSE by D_tot bin 12.6/13.5/12.7/12.6/13.7 (no order); Elo-total RMSE 12.5/13.4/13.2/13.6/15.5 (offset effect).
theories.recommendation: The thresholds do not correspond to different error levels for the market number or the engine mean; they only sort games by how far our number sits from the market. Replace them with distance-to-market bands whose meaning is 'expected excess RMSE vs the close' and whose LOW band is where the model has been consistently wrong OOS.
theories.parameter_change: Spread: HIGH if |published - close| < 1.5 (54% of 2022-25 games; realized excess RMSE +0.03, ATS vs close 303-296), MED 1.5-3.0 (30%; +0.11 realized, +0.19 predicted; 171-165), LOW >= 3.0 (16%; +1.25 realized, +0.80 predicted; ATS 81-94, excess positive in all four test seasons: +1.37/+0.74/+1.28/+1.45). Total: HIGH |published total - close| < 2.5 (44%; -0.04), MED 2.5-5 (31%; +0.56), LOW >= 5 (25%; +1.51, predicted +1.89). Drop the SD-based cuts.
theories.effect_size: variance ratio LOW/HIGH under current cuts 0.95-1.04 (market), 1.16 (engine mean, p=0.089, sign flips in-sample); under proposed D bands the model's own RMSE is 12.47/12.56/13.57 (spread) and 13.09/13.18/14.83 (total)
theories.uncertainty: n=1139 (spread and total); tag shares 505-616 / 290-351 / 163-283 games
theories.caveats: SD-to-|diff| mapping assumes two numbers; with three engines the literal SD is a different scale, but the real 2-engine SD gives the same null. Band cut points 1.5/3.0 and 2.5/5.0 were chosen for round numbers and ~55/30/15 shares, not optimized.
theories.data_used: same as T1a; nfelo_scored_individual_games.csv for qbelo line

theories.hypothesis: Disagreement predicts WHO is right (market vs model): the blend weight on the model should shrink (or grow) when engines disagree.
theories.method: Blend line = mkt + w*(model - mkt). Regress e_mkt on x = -(model - mkt) (no intercept) so the coefficient is w (0 = market right, 1 = model right). Fit on <=2021 overall, by D_base tercile, and with interaction w(D)=w0+w1*D; evaluate 2022-25 MAE/RMSE of blends vs market with 3000-rep paired bootstrap; ATS of the model side vs close by D bin with binomial p; rolling-origin w (fit all prior seasons, test each season 2016-25); w-grid 0..1 in the test era with paired t-tests; w by genuine engine-SD (sd2) tercile; model vs OPEN line ATS as a caveat.
theories.metric: blend weight w (and its slope in D); OOS MAE difference blend minus market with 95% CI; ATS of model side vs close
theories.result: Fit era: w=0.418 (se 0.10); interaction w(D)=0.78-0.08*D (p=0.007) i.e. in-sample the model deserved less weight when far from the market. This did not transfer: test-era w=-0.12 (se 0.16); the w(D) rule vs constant-w blend: +0.0055 MAE [-0.021,+0.032]; the constant-w=0.42 blend vs market: +0.052 MAE [+0.001,+0.106]; w-grid: every positive w hurts (w=0.3 +0.030, p=0.13; w=0.5 +0.071, p=0.028; w=1.0 +0.238, p=0.0002). Rolling-origin 2016-25: w_hat 0.32-0.50, blend better than market in 3/10 seasons, mean +0.019 MAE. ATS of model side vs close by D band: 50.6% (n=616) / 50.9% (344) / 46.3% (179), none significant; by D bin [2,3) 56.2% (p=0.10) and [3,4.5) 44.6% (p=0.25) -> noise. By real engine-SD tercile the test-era w is +0.16 / -0.07 / -0.47 (se 0.25-0.31): if anything trust the market MORE when engines disagree. Regressed nfelo_c: fit w=1.05 but OOS blend +0.071 MAE [+0.008,+0.135]. Caveat for the market expert: vs the OPEN line the model is 594-519 ATS (53.4%, p=0.027) — the market moves toward the model — but 555-555 vs the close.
theories.recommendation: Do not vary the model weight with disagreement; there is no OOS evidence that disagreement identifies who is right, and the in-sample 'shrink with D' pattern reversed. Keep any market-anchoring weight constant.
theories.parameter_change: Keep as is with respect to disagreement-dependent weighting (no w(D) term). If the engine is ever blended with the market close, use a constant w <= 0.3 (rolling-origin optimum 0.32-0.50 but no OOS MAE gain); in 2022-25 w=0 was best.
theories.effect_size: w1 = -0.08 per point of D in-sample (p=0.007) -> -0.04 OOS (p=0.50); constant blend costs +0.03 to +0.24 MAE per game OOS depending on w
theories.uncertainty: n=1139 test; blend-minus-market CIs from paired bootstrap; ATS binomial p all > 0.09
theories.caveats: Only the nfelo engine (and 538 qbelo) is testable; the ORIGINATOR blend with PFF/Cole may behave differently. The negative test-era w partly reflects nfelo's weak 2022-25 (market MAE 9.54 vs nfelo_b 9.77). The 53.4% vs-open result is a market-timing effect, not a disagreement effect.
theories.data_used: same as T1a

theories.hypothesis: A per-game error SD for spread and total can be built from disagreement, favorite size, total size, roof and week, and tag thresholds can be set so HIGH/MED/LOW mean different realized error.
theories.method: Fit on <=2021, test 2022-25: (A) OLS on |err| (sigma = sqrt(pi/2)*E|err|) and (B) Gamma GLM log-link on err^2, with features D_base, |spread|, total, dome, early (wk<=4), late (wk>=15), playoff, market move (totals: D_tot, total, |spread|, dome, early, late, playoff, wind>=15). OOS metrics: Spearman(sigma_hat,|err|), decile calibration, Gaussian log-score vs constant, 50/80/90% coverage, LOW/HIGH variance ratio with F-test. Then the mechanical rule sigma = sqrt(BASE^2 + D^2) with BASE = trailing-3-season RMSE of the market-close error, empirical multipliers k_p = quantile(|e|/sigma, p) from <=2021, paired-bootstrap log-score comparison vs base-only; season drift check; shrink factor c for D computed against the OPEN line (script 11).
theories.metric: OOS Spearman(sigma_hat,|err|); coverage of 50/80/90% intervals; mean Gaussian log-score gain per game; realized RMSE by tag
theories.result: For the market number nothing predicts the error size: full-feature models give Spearman 0.00 to -0.02 (p>0.5), log-score gain <=0.002/game, LOW/HIGH variance ratio 0.87-0.95 (wrong direction), decile calibration flat (pred 11.9-13.8 vs realized 10.9-13.7 unordered). Totals: only mkt_total is individually significant (+0.070 |err| per point, p=0.024 on n=4310; ~+1 SD point between totals 40 and 52) but OOS Spearman 0.02-0.04 (p>=0.17) -> not adopted. Season drift is bigger than any per-game effect: realized spread RMSE 11.5-14.3 by season; fit-era constant 13.32 over-covers 2022-25 (realized 12.42), trailing-3 base gains log-score in 3/4 seasons. Proposed rule for the model's own number: spread sigma=sqrt(BASE_s^2+D^2), total sigma=sqrt(BASE_t^2+D_tot^2). OOS 2022-25: spread coverage 0.514/0.796/0.882 with k=0.61/1.25/1.62 (Gaussian k over-covers the 50% interval: 0.557); total coverage 0.498/0.811/0.910 with k=0.66/1.26/1.63; total quintile calibration 13.10->12.31, 13.29->13.77, 13.49->13.18, 13.93->13.03, 15.23->15.37; log-score gain vs fit-era constant +0.0020 (spread) / +0.0038 (total); vs trailing-base-only +0.0012 [-0.0017,+0.0050] and +0.0047 [-0.0010,+0.0110] (not significant). Fitted c in sqrt(BASE^2+(c*D)^2): 0.85 vs close (c=1 marginally best OOS); vs the OPEN line c=0.00 in-sample and 0.5-1 OOS (LOW band by D_open realized 12.29 vs 13.54 predicted at c=1).
theories.recommendation: Publish a per-game sigma that is a constant per season for the outcome plus the mechanical excess for the model's distance from the market; drop favorite-size, total-size, roof and week modifiers (all null). Make the tag a statement about expected excess error vs the close.
theories.parameter_change: BASE_spread = trailing-3-season RMSE of (margin + closing spread) = 12.72 for 2026 (5-season 12.66); BASE_total = trailing-3-season RMSE of (total - closing total) = 12.96 for 2026 (5-season 13.08). sigma_spread(g) = sqrt(BASE_spread^2 + (c*D_g)^2), sigma_total(g) = sqrt(BASE_total^2 + (c*Dtot_g)^2) with D = |published number - market line|, c = 1.0 when the reference is the closing/latest line, c = 0.5 when only the opener is available. Interval half-widths: spread 50/80/90% = 0.61/1.25/1.62 * sigma; total 0.66/1.26/1.63 * sigma (empirical, not Gaussian 0.674/1.282/1.645). Tags: spread HIGH D<1.5, MED 1.5-3.0, LOW >=3.0; total HIGH D<2.5, MED 2.5-5.0, LOW >=5.0 (realized model RMSE 12.47/12.56/13.57 and 13.09/13.18/14.83). Recompute BASE each August.
theories.effect_size: sigma ranges 12.7 (D=0) to 13.6 (D=5) spread and 13.0 to 14.7 (D=7) total; LOW-band excess RMSE +1.25 (spread) / +1.51 (total) OOS
theories.uncertainty: n=1139 test; coverage within 0.02 of nominal at 80/90%; log-score gains have CIs crossing 0, so the D term is justified by the identity and band-level calibration, not by a significant likelihood gain
theories.caveats: Model number tested is nfelo_b (single engine) and the spec's Elo-implied total; the ORIGINATOR blend has PFF/Cole components whose distance from the market is unobserved here, but the identity e_model = e_mkt + (model - mkt) holds for any number. Bases drift by season (11.5-14.3), which dominates all per-game effects; a trailing window is a judgment call (3 vs 5 seasons differ by 0.06-0.12).
theories.data_used: same as T1a; weather (wind) from games_1999_2025.csv

experts.summary:
Setup: nflverse games joined to nfelo, 4310 games 2009-25 (fit <=2021 n=3171, test 2022-25 n=1139); signs verified (corr(line, margin) -0.42 to -0.44 for every line). The disagreement proxy is the UNREGRESSED nfelo number (-nfelo_dif_base/25, r=0.96 with the historic pre-regression line) vs the market close; the README's 'nfelo close' is market-regressed and sits 0.54 pts from the close, so it hides disagreement. A genuine engine-vs-engine SD was built from nfelo and the published 538 qbelo line (script 08); a 3-engine reconstruction from squared errors (script 06) is flagged as biased and not relied on. No PFF/Cole history exists, so nfelo (+qbelo) stands in for the engines.

Findings. (1) Disagreement does not predict the size of the market's error at all: OOS slope +0.02 pts/pt (p=0.91), Spearman 0.03, and a joint F-test of disagreement, favorite size, total, roof, week, playoff and market move on |market error| over n=4310 gives p=0.71, R^2=0.001; totals likewise (mkt_total is the only marginal driver, +0.07 |err|/pt, p=0.024, not validated OOS). The engine-vs-engine SD is equally null for the market number, the engine mean and nfelo (p=0.10-0.33), and the current SD-style tags sort games into HIGH/MED/LOW whose realized market RMSE is 12.48/12.21/12.71 (variance ratio 1.04, p=0.37). (2) Disagreement DOES predict the error of the model's own number (+0.36 pts/pt, p=0.038; T3-T1 RMSE +1.26), but only mechanically: e_model = e_mkt + (model - mkt) with corr 0.03, so RMSE_model = sqrt(RMSE_mkt^2 + D^2) to within 0.1 in every tercile, both eras, spreads and totals. (3) Disagreement does not tell who is right: in-sample w(D)=0.78-0.08D (p=0.007) reversed OOS (w=-0.12; w(D) rule +0.006 MAE vs constant, CI spans 0); every positive market-blend weight hurt in 2022-25 (w=0.3 +0.03 MAE, w=0.5 +0.07 p=0.03); model-side ATS vs close by band 50.6/50.9/46.3%. (4) The only OOS-calibrated interval rule is sigma = sqrt(BASE^2 + D^2) with BASE = trailing-3-season RMSE of the market-close error (12.72 spread, 12.96 total for 2026) and empirical multipliers 0.61/1.25/1.62 (spread) and 0.66/1.26/1.63 (total) for 50/80/90% intervals; OOS coverage 0.51/0.80/0.88 and 0.50/0.81/0.91. Against the opening line D must be shrunk (c~0.5) because the market moves toward the model (model 53.4% ATS vs open, 50.0% vs close).

What I would change first: replace the engine-SD confidence tag with a distance-to-market tag (spread HIGH <1.5 / MED 1.5-3 / LOW >=3; total <2.5 / 2.5-5 / >=5), documented as 'expected excess RMSE vs the close' (+0.03/+0.19/+0.80 spread; +0.07/+0.51/+1.89 total; realized OOS +0.03/+0.11/+1.25 and -0.04/+0.56/+1.51, LOW-band excess positive in all four test seasons). Second, publish sigma from the sqrt rule with a trailing base, no favorite/total/roof/week modifiers. Third, keep any model-vs-market weighting constant (and low): nothing in disagreement identifies who is right, and the market was right in 2022-25.

experts.expert: pace — Pace, play-style & explosiveness (scripts: /home/user/originator-2026-w01/research/experts/pace/, run_all.sh re-runs 00-06 in ~5 min)

theories.hypothesis: Prior pace of both teams (neutral-situation seconds/play, plays/game, no-huddle, drives) predicts the realized game total beyond the market closing total, and a fast/fast vs slow/slow matchup warrants the spec's +/-1..2 total adjustment.
theories.method: Built per team-game pbp features (nflscrapR 2009-19, nflfastR 2023-25; 2020-22 pbp missing): neutral sec/play = game-clock gap between consecutive offensive snaps of the same drive in Q1-Q3, |score diff|<=8, excl. last 2:00 of H1, 0<dt<=60 (also after-run gaps only), plays, game plays, drives, no-huddle. Prior-only, league-relative versions: rolling prior-8 games (min 4, never crossing the 2019->2023 gap) and a K=4 prior-season/season-to-date blend. Validated vs Kevin Cole table (drives r=0.99, pass rate r=0.96, score r=1.00). (B) residual OLS (HC1) of total - market close on each feature, train 2009-19, test 2023-25 REG; OOS MAE of market + train-fit adjustment with paired bootstrap CI and O/U record. (C) market-free LEAN baseline (lg_blend + elo_sum + pf_sum + pa_sum + qb_sum + dome + wind + div, same spec the totals expert used) +/- pace; OOS calibration slope of the train-fit adjustment; rolling-origin 2013-19. (D) quartile buckets FF/SS/mixed with cutoffs from train; concrete rules (spec +/-1.5 FF/SS, +/-0.75 mixed; half-size; linear -0.5*spp capped +/-1; -0.25*spp capped +/-0.5) scored OOS.
theories.metric: MAE (paired bootstrap 95% CI), RMSE, O/U vs market close, HC1 coefficients, calibration slope
theories.result: VS MARKET: nothing. Single-feature residual coefficients all p>0.10 in train and p>0.4 in test (spp_avg train -0.30 pts/s p=0.146, test +0.03 p=0.95; plays_sum p=0.22/0.44; no-huddle p=0.24/0.76; drives p=0.18/0.59). Joint pace/style model OOS: dMAE vs market +0.041 [-0.005,+0.084] (r8) and +0.051 [+0.006,+0.098] (blend), O/U 354-393 (0.474) — worse. MARKET-FREE: spp_avg coefficient -0.541 pts per second of two-team avg (se 0.215, p=0.012; -0.70 pts per SD) in 2009-19 and stable in rolling-origin (-0.40..-0.56 for 2015-19), BUT 2023-25 in-sample coefficient is +0.13 (se 0.52, p=0.80), OOS calibration slope -0.27 (se 0.91), and adding it RAISES OOS MAE: +0.064 [+0.021,+0.106]. Spec bucket rule (+/-1.5 FF/SS, +/-0.75 mixed): MAE 10.368 vs 10.290, dMAE +0.078 [+0.027,+0.125], dRMSE +0.041; half-size rule +0.033 [+0.009,+0.058]; -0.25*spp capped 0.5: +0.025 [+0.006,+0.043]. Rolling-origin 2013-19 (pre-2020): every rule helped slightly (mean dMAE -0.010..-0.013, 5/7 seasons) — the effect existed in the 2010s and is gone now.
