Buckets: train FF vs SS market-free residual +3.0 pts (Welch p=0.058, n=165/147; blend +1.6, p=0.30); test +0.2 (p=0.96, n=25/55; blend -2.9, p=0.50, n=14/51). Market residual FF vs SS train +2.2 (p=0.15). Why it vanished (06): dispersion of prior pace fell (SD 1.30 -> 1.02 s), prior-pace->realized-plays slope fell -2.10 -> -0.95 plays/s, pace->total chain -0.94 -> -0.47 pts/s, team-level persistence of pace 0.35 -> 0.23, and the market's own pace slope went from -0.20/s (p<0.001) to +0.07 (p=0.42). Sanity: corr(mkt_spread, margin) = -0.441; corr(spp, plays) negative; corr(prior spp, realized plays) -0.29 train.
theories.recommendation: Delete the +/-1..2 pace adjustment; set pace_adj = 0. Pace is fully priced (and now barely predictive of plays); every sized version of the rule raised 2023-25 OOS MAE with CIs excluding zero. Keep computing spp_neut weekly as a diagnostic only.
theories.parameter_change: totals.pace_adj: +/-1..2 -> 0 (remove). If the engine must carry a market-consistency term, the largest defensible form is adj = clip(-0.25 * spp_avg_dev, -0.5, +0.5), spp_avg_dev = mean of both teams' prior-8 neutral sec/play minus prior-season league mean — and even that cost +0.025 MAE OOS, so the recommended value is 0.
theories.effect_size: 2009-19 fit: -0.54 pts per second of two-team average neutral sec/play (SD 1.3 s -> 0.7 pts per SD); implied FF (+/-2.2 s) +1.3 / SS -1.2 pts in-sample. 2023-25: +0.13 +/- 0.52 pts/s, i.e. zero. Spec rule mean |adj| 0.54 pts.
theories.uncertainty: spec-rule OOS dMAE +0.078 [95% CI +0.027,+0.125]; train coefficient -0.541 (se 0.215); test coefficient +0.132 (se 0.516); calibration slope -0.27 (se 0.91)
theories.caveats: 2020-22 pbp unavailable so the OOS window is 2023-25 only (752 games r8 / 816 blend; 2023 early weeks lack rolling windows, r8 coverage 78%). FF/SS test cells are small (n=14-55). The effect was real but small in 2013-19 rolling-origin (-0.01 MAE), so this is era-dependent; re-check the calibration slope after 2026 if pace dispersion widens again.
theories.data_used: nflscrapR reg pbp 2009-2019; nflfastR pbp 2023-2025; games_1999_2025.csv closing lines; nfelo_games.csv (Elo, 538 QB adj); totals expert common.py leak-free baseline (pf/pa/lg_blend/env); cole_team_games for validation

theories.hypothesis: An explosive offense (>=20-yd pass / >=10-yd rush rate) facing a defense that allows many explosive plays scores more than the market-implied team total (home T/2 - S/2, away T/2 + S/2), justifying the +/-0.5..1.5 matchup reallocations.
theories.method: Team-game long format (2 rows per game, SEs clustered by game). Prior-only league-relative explosive rate for the offense and explosive rate allowed by the opponent's defense (rolling-8 and K=4 blend), plus an expl20 variant and a product 'mismatch' term; controls: prior EPA/play for/against, points for/against. (a) residual regression team_pts - implied_tt on features, train 2009-19 / test 2023-25, OOS MAE of implied_tt + train-fit adjustment. (b) market-free team-points baseline (lg_blend/2 + team Elo, opp Elo, team pf, opp pa, team/opp QB adj, home, dome, wind, div) +/- explosive features; calibration slope; rolling-origin 2013-19. (c) quartile cells: explosive O (X) vs weak D (W) against non-explosive O (x) vs stingy D (s).
theories.metric: MAE of team points (paired bootstrap CI), cluster-robust coefficients, calibration slope, Welch t-tests on cells
theories.result: VS IMPLIED TEAM TOTAL: train (n=4884): off_expl -1.3 (se 7.2, p=0.86), opp_def_expl +7.1 (p=0.36), mismatch product +1.0 (p=0.82), expl20 variants p>=0.39, EPA/pts controls ns. Test (n=1504): off_expl +25.1 (se 11.4, p=0.028; blend +26.6, p=0.076), mismatch +8.4 (p=0.17; blend p=0.56), opp_def_expl -12.5 (p=0.33). OOS MAE of train-fit rules: -0.001..+0.008 (all CIs straddle 0) — no exploitable edge. Cells: XW vs xs market residual train +0.77 (p=0.29) / test +2.24 (p=0.057, n=100/117) with r8, but blend train +0.34 (p=0.64) / test +0.84 (p=0.48). MARKET-FREE: explosive-plays ALLOWED is a strong in-sample coefficient (+31.6 per unit rate, se 9.1, p<0.001; +0.55 pts per SD; rolling-origin 25-58 every year) yet its OOS calibration slope is +0.08 (se 0.41) and dMAE -0.002 [-0.027,+0.023]; capped rule 30*(rate - league) +/-1.5: dMAE +0.005 [-0.021,+0.031]. Offense explosiveness adds +0.11 per SD (p=0.44). Rolling-origin mean team-pts MAE 7.415 BASE vs 7.410 with explosive terms. Offensive EPA/play instead: +4.1 (p=0.05), +0.43 per SD, calibration slope 0.72 (se 0.51), dMAE -0.010 [-0.025,+0.004].
theories.recommendation: Do not drive the +/-0.5..1.5 team-total matchup reallocation with explosive-play rates: the interaction is null everywhere and the defense-allowed term, though significant in-sample, has zero OOS calibration once Elo/pf/pa/QB are in the model. Keep the reallocation cap but set the explosive-play weight to 0. Flag for monitoring: in 2023-25 only, explosive offenses beat their implied total by ~+0.5 pts per SD (p=0.03) — not present in 2009-19, so INCONCLUSIVE, not actionable.
theories.parameter_change: team_total.matchup_realloc: explosive-play component weight = 0 (keep as is otherwise). If a data-driven team-total term is wanted, use tt_adj = clip(4.0 * off_epa_dev, -1.0, +1.0), off_epa_dev = team's prior-8 EPA/play minus league (SD 0.1 -> ~0.4 pts per SD).
theories.effect_size: Defense-allowed explosive rate: +0.55 pts per SD in-sample, 0 OOS. Offense explosive rate: +0.1 pts per SD in 2009-19, +0.47 per SD in 2023-25 only. XW vs xs cell: +2.2 pts test (r8) vs +0.8 (blend).
theories.uncertainty: test off_expl coefficient +25.1 (se 11.4); OOS dMAE of any rule within [-0.03,+0.03]; calibration slope of the defense term +0.08 (se 0.41)
theories.caveats: No historical team-total lines exist locally, so the market benchmark is the implied team total from spread and total (MAE 7.19 vs my baseline 7.27). Two rows per game are correlated (cluster SEs used). The test-era offense effect rests on 1504 team-games from three seasons and does not replicate with the blend features.
theories.data_used: same pbp/feature set as T1; nfelo Elo and QB adj; closing spread and total for implied team totals

theories.hypothesis: Pass rate over expected (PROE) — and neutral pass rate — is a totals signal: pass-heavy matchups go over the market total.
theories.method: Own expected-pass logit fit ONLY on 2009-19 scrimmage plays (down, distance, field position, score diff x time, half/game clock, win probability; pseudo-R2 0.14), applied to all seasons; PROE validated vs nflfastR pass_oe (team-game r=0.82, team-season r=0.89) and Cole pass_over_exp (r=0.80). Prior-only league-relative sums (rolling-8, blend), neutral-only PROE, max-of-two, |difference|, and a style-shift term (season-to-date minus prior-season PROE). Game-level residual regressions vs market, market-free LEAN baseline +/- PROE with calibration slope, rolling-origin 2013-19, team-level own/opp PROE vs implied team total (cluster SE).
theories.metric: MAE (paired bootstrap CI), HC1/cluster coefficients, O/U vs market, calibration slope
theories.result: VS MARKET: proe_sum train +0.044 pts per pct-pt (se 0.036, p=0.23; +0.34 per SD), test +0.022 (p=0.75), OOS dMAE +0.001 [-0.032,+0.034], O/U 378-369 (0.506); neutral PROE p=0.18/0.37; neutral pass rate p=0.14/0.995; proe_max p=0.11/0.39; style shift p=0.41 (n=1699) / 0.47 (n=416); team-level own/opp PROE p>=0.26 train and test. The market prices it: corr(proe_sum, market total) = +0.50 train, +0.29 test. MARKET-FREE: proe_sum +0.170 per pct-pt (se 0.041, p<0.001; +1.3 pts per SD; blend +0.223, +1.5 per SD), rolling-origin coefficient stable 0.14-0.27 — yet 2023-25 in-sample coefficient is +0.04 (se 0.08, p=0.60), OOS calibration slope +0.44 (se 0.40), OOS dMAE +0.018 [-0.063,+0.090] (blend +0.041 [-0.032,+0.114]); rolling-origin 2013-19 mean dMAE -0.014 with 4/7 seasons better. Pass-rate variants are worse (dMAE +0.04..+0.06). PROE + pace together: +0.066 [-0.024,+0.155] (worse).
theories.recommendation: No PROE or pass-rate adjustment to totals: the market fully prices play-calling style and the market-free increment has no OOS value (calibration ~0.4, CI includes 0). Keep as is. Compute PROE weekly only for diagnostics / QB-change context.
theories.parameter_change: totals.style_adj (pass rate / PROE): none (0). No change to the implied-total formula.
theories.effect_size: +0.17 pts per pct-pt of two-team PROE sum (1.3 pts per SD) in 2009-19, ~+0.04 in 2023-25; residual vs market +0.34 pts per SD (ns).
theories.uncertainty: market residual coefficient +0.044 (se 0.036) train, +0.022 (se 0.068) test; market-free OOS dMAE +0.018 [-0.063,+0.090]
theories.caveats: PROE uses my own xpass model (fit 2009-19 so 2023-25 is an out-of-era application; agreement with nflfastR pass_oe r=0.82). The in-sample 2009-19 coefficient is genuinely significant — the market prices it, so an originator ignoring PROE will differ from the market on pass-heavy matchups without gaining accuracy.
theories.data_used: same pbp/feature set; nflfastR pass_oe and Cole pass_over_exp for validation

theories.hypothesis: Which pbp-derived pace/style/efficiency features should the engine compute weekly, at what sizes; the only pbp term that improves the market-free total is an efficiency term (EPA/play for+against), not pace.
theories.method: Calibration-slope and OOS MAE/RMSE scoring of concrete adjustment rules on the market-free BASE total (fit 2009-19, test 2023-25 REG): EPA rule total_adj = clip(4.0*epa_sum, -3, +3) where epa_sum = sum over both teams of (prior-8 EPA/play offense - league) + (prior-8 EPA/play allowed - league); 3.0 cap 2 variant; points-per-drive rule; EPA + pace combined; rolling-origin 2013-19; modern-era in-sample refit for stability.
theories.metric: MAE and RMSE (paired bootstrap CI) vs BASE and vs market, O/U vs market, calibration slope
theories.result: epa_sum: train b=4.05 (se 1.69, p=0.016), 2023-25 in-sample b=3.73 (se 2.64, p=0.16) — same size; calibration slope 0.68 (se 0.55). Rule clip(4.0*epa_sum, +/-3): OOS MAE 10.239 vs BASE 10.290, dMAE -0.051 [-0.117,+0.012], dRMSE -0.011, mean |adj| 0.75 (SD 0.85 pts; 1st/99th pct -2.3/+1.9), O/U vs market 408-339-5 (0.546); refit jointly in the model dMAE -0.065 [-0.120,-0.014]. 3.0 cap 2: -0.043 [-0.092,+0.005]. Rolling-origin 2013-19: -0.006, 4/7 seasons. Points per drive: b=1.07 (2023-25 in-sample 2.76, p=0.028), calibration slope 1.26 (se 0.67), dMAE -0.033 [-0.085,+0.020], dRMSE -0.036 — usable fallback if EPA is unavailable. Stacking the pace rule on the EPA rule cancels the gain (+0.001). Still +0.08 MAE worse than the market close (CI [-0.09,+0.26]). Weekly feature spec printed in 05 section 6.
theories.recommendation: Replace the pace adjustment with an efficiency adjustment on the blended implied total: total_adj = clip(4.0 * epa_sum_dev, -3, +3). Weekly features to compute from pbp (all prior-only, prior 8 games, min 4, league-relative = minus prior-season league mean; before 4 games fall back to prior-season team mean then league mean): epa_off, epa_def (EPA per pass+run play for/against) — used; ppd (offensive drive points incl. XP / offensive drives) — fallback; spp_neut (neutral sec/play as defined in T1), plays/game_plays, pr_neut and PROE, expl_off/expl_def (pass>=20 or rush>=10 per play) — diagnostics only, weight 0.
theories.parameter_change: totals.pace_adj -> 0; add totals.eff_adj = clip(4.0 * epa_sum_dev, -3.0, +3.0) with epa_sum_dev = (h_epa_off + a_epa_off + h_epa_def + a_epa_def) - 4*league (prior-8, league-relative). Confidence-tag SD for totals unchanged (OOS RMSE 13.1). Optional team-total term tt_adj = clip(4.0 * off_epa_dev, -1, +1). Do not stack a pace term on top.
theories.effect_size: 0.85 pts per SD of epa_sum; OOS MAE -0.05 (-0.065 when coefficients are refit with it); O/U 54.6% on 747 decisions in one 3-season window
theories.caveats: Overlaps the totals expert's LEAN + EPA finding (their dMAE ~-0.03, O/U 0.517); treat the 0.546 O/U as one window, not an edge. pf/pa in the baseline already carries most efficiency signal, so the increment is small. 2020-22 missing means the rule's coefficient was never checked on 2022.
theories.data_used: same pbp/feature set; totals expert common.py baseline; closing totals

experts.summary: Bottom line: the market prices pace and play-calling style completely, and in 2023-25 pace no longer even predicts plays well; no pace, pass-rate, PROE or explosive-play feature adds out-of-sample value against the closing total or the implied team total (every residual coefficient p>0.1 in train, p>0.3 in test, OOS dMAE within +/-0.01 or worse). The spec's +/-1..2 pace adjustment should be deleted first: applied to the market-free total it RAISED 2023-25 OOS MAE by +0.078 [+0.027,+0.125] (half-size +0.033 [+0.009,+0.058]); the underlying 2009-19 effect was only -0.54 pts per second of two-team neutral sec/play (about +1.3/-1.2 for extreme fast/fast vs slow/slow in-sample) and is +0.13 +/- 0.52 in the modern era, because pace dispersion (SD 1.30 -> 1.02 s) and the pace-to-plays slope (-2.1 -> -0.95 plays/s) both halved and the market's own pace weighting went to zero. Second, drop explosive-play rates from the team-total reallocation: the offense-vs-defense mismatch is null in every specification, and the significant in-sample 'explosive plays allowed' term (+0.55 pts/SD) has an OOS calibration slope of 0.08 +/- 0.41. Third, keep PROE out of the engine (+1.3 pts/SD in-sample, calibration 0.44 +/- 0.40, dMAE +0.02 OOS). The one pbp feature worth adding is an efficiency term: total_adj = clip(4.0*epa_sum_dev, -3, +3) using both teams' prior-8 EPA/play for and against (coefficient 4.05 in 2009-19, 3.73 in 2023-25; OOS dMAE -0.051 [-0.117,+0.012], -0.065 [-0.120,-0.014] when refit; do not stack pace on it, that cancels the gain). Watch item, not action: in 2023-25 only, explosive offenses beat their implied team total by ~+0.5 pts/SD (p=0.03, n=1504 team-games) — absent in 2009-19. All fits 2009-2019 (pbp availability), tests 2023-2025 (752-816 REG games) plus rolling-origin 2013-19; features validated vs Cole (drives r=0.99, pass rate r=0.96, PROE r=0.80) and nflfastR pass_oe (r=0.82); sign checks passed (corr(mkt_spread, margin) = -0.44).

theories.hypothesis: Preseason (regressed) ratings are less predictive in Weeks 1-4 than in Weeks 5+, so a rating-driven originator is at a larger disadvantage to the market early in the season.
theories.method: nfelo starting Elo (the only rating series with history; PFF/Cole have none) + nfelo site HFA -> 'elo_line' (no QB adj, no market regression) and 'nraw' (with 538 QB adj). Per week bucket (1,2,3,4,5-9,10+): MAE vs market close with paired bootstrap CI; OLS slope of margin on each line (1 = calibrated) with an early-x-line interaction test (HC1); 'who is right' regression margin ~ rating line + market line, weights fitted on <=2021 and applied to 2022-25.
theories.metric: MAE vs realized margin (paired diff rating line minus market), OLS slopes, blend weights
theories.result: W1 (n=253): MAE elo_line 9.79 vs market 9.82, nraw-mkt +0.03 [-0.23,+0.29] p=0.79. W2-4: within +/-0.12 of market, all CIs include 0. W10+ (n=2010): market better by 0.22 [+0.11,+0.32] p<0.01 (TEST 2022-25: +0.37 [+0.18,+0.56]). Slope of margin on elo_line: W1 1.05 (se 0.19), early(1-4)-vs-late difference +0.03 (se 0.10, p=0.80). Blend weights: W1 rating 0.61 / market 0.38 (FIT), 0.72 / 0.47 (TEST); W10+ rating ~0 / market 1.06-1.29. OOS W1 blend vs market: MAE -0.105 [-0.48,+0.22] (n=64, not significant). The rating line's disadvantage vs the market GROWS through the season; it is smallest in W1-4.
theories.recommendation: Do not down-weight or hedge the rating-based number in Week 1; the regressed preseason ratings are as accurate as the closing market in W1-4 and only fall behind from mid-season. If anything the engine's rating trust should be highest in Weeks 1-4.
theories.parameter_change: Keep as is: rating weights (0.46 nfelo / 0.39 PFF / 0.15 Cole) and the 25 Elo-per-point scale unchanged in Week 1; no early-season down-weighting.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv (REG, closing spread) joined to nfelo_games.csv 2009-2025 (starting_nfelo_home/away, hfa_mod, nfelo_dif_base); 253 W1 games with ratings
theories.effect_size: W1 rating-vs-market MAE gap +0.03 pts vs +0.22 pts in W10+ (difference ~0.19 pts/game)
theories.expected_impact: None from a change; avoids a harmful one (shrinking or hedging W1 numbers)
theories.uncertainty: W1 bucket per test season is 16 games; blend-weight CIs are wide (se ~0.4-0.8). The directional pattern (rating share highest early) holds in FIT, TEST and ALL.
theories.caveats: Only nfelo's regressed preseason Elo could be tested; PFF/Cole preseason ratings may regress less and would need the same test once history exists. Schedule expert's 05_week_effects.py reaches the same MAE-by-week numbers independently.

theories.hypothesis: The Week-1 market is less efficient: larger errors and exploitable biases (home teams, favorites, totals over/under).
theories.method: 1999-2025 REG closing lines (n=428 W1 games): mean home residual with bootstrap CI, home ATS, favourite cover margin by |line| bin, dog ATS with binomial CI, Mincer-Zarnowitz slope, residual SD with Levene test vs W5+, totals residual; split FIT (1999-2021) / TEST (2022-25) and by era.
theories.metric: mean residual vs close (pts), ATS %, MZ slope, residual SD
theories.recommendation: No Week-1 home/favorite/underdog bias adjustment; the W1 spread market is as accurate as any other week and outcome variance is not larger, so confidence-tag thresholds should not be widened for Week 1.
theories.parameter_change: Keep as is: no W1 favorite/dog or home-side bias term; confidence-tag SD thresholds (1.2/2.2 spread, 1.8/3.0 totals) unchanged for W1.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv REG closing spread/total, 27 seasons of Week 1
theories.effect_size: All W1 bias point estimates within +/-0.8 pts with CIs spanning 0; big-favorite cell -5.7 pts but n=23
theories.expected_impact: None
theories.uncertainty: n=428 gives +/-1.2 pt CI on the home residual; a bias smaller than ~1 pt cannot be excluded.
theories.caveats: |line|>=10 W1 favorites (n=23, fav cover -5.7, p=0.01 vs W5+) is flagged as INCONCLUSIVE by the n<150 rule, not actionable.

theories.hypothesis: An originator should shrink its Week-1 spread toward zero (and its Week-1 total toward the league mean); the optimal shrinkage factor differs by week.
theories.method: Spread: pred = k*elo_line (rating+HFA) and pred = -(k*elo_dif + HFA) with k fitted through the origin per week bucket; (a) fixed split fit 2009-21 / test 2022-25, (b) rolling-origin fit seasons<t, test t for t=2015..2025, pooled; loss curve over k in [0.5,1.5] on 2022-25; paired bootstrap CI on MAE(shrunk)-MAE(k=1). Totals: implied_total = prior + c*(home_rating+away_rating), prior = previous season realized mean; c fitted per bucket vs engine c=0.35.
theories.metric: OOS MAE difference shrunk vs unshrunk (paired), fitted k with HC1 se
theories.result: Spread W1: fixed-split k_single 0.90 (se 0.20), k_rating 1.10 (se 0.25); TEST MAE diff -0.018 [-0.12,+0.08] p=0.73. Rolling-origin W1 (n=169): mean k 0.94 (0.88-1.01), MAE 9.787 vs 9.816, diff -0.029 [-0.08,+0.03] p=0.28; RMSE slightly worse (13.446 vs 13.432). W1-4 pooled k 1.06-1.07, diff +0.015 [-0.01,+0.04]. Loss curve 2022-25 W1: MAE at k=1 within 0.018 of the best k (0.9); RMSE best at 1.0-1.1. Slope of W1 margin on the pure preseason rating gap = 1.17 (se 0.20) [2022-25: 1.30 (se 0.35)] - preseason Elo is if anything too compressed, not too confident. Totals: W1 c_fit 0.363 (se 0.230) vs engine 0.35, W1-4 0.376 (se 0.113), W5+ 0.270 (se 0.055); fitted-c OOS improvement in W1 (-0.11 [-0.20,-0.03]) comes from the -0.37 intercept shift, not from c.
theories.recommendation: No Week-1 shrinkage of the rating-derived spread; keep the totals rating coefficient at 0.35. The only W1 totals change supported is the level (prior), handled in theory 3.
theories.parameter_change: Keep as is: W1 spread multiplier k = 1.00 on the rating line and on the rating gap; totals c = 0.35 in all weeks. Do not add a week-of-season shrink table.
theories.data_used: nfelo starting Elo + hfa_mod, games.csv margins/totals 2009-2025; previous-season mean totals from games 1999-2025
theories.effect_size: Best-case W1 MAE gain from shrinking 0.02-0.03 pts (CI includes 0); loss curve flat between k=0.8 and 1.1
theories.expected_impact: None; a shrink of 0.9 would gain <0.03 MAE and lose on RMSE
theories.uncertainty: W1 k has se ~0.2 (n=189 fit games); cannot distinguish k in [0.7,1.3] statistically, which is exactly why the flat loss curve says leave it at 1.0.
theories.caveats: Tested on nfelo only; a preseason PFF/Cole rating that is NOT regressed toward the mean could still need shrinking - nfelo's W1 rating SD is 3.0 pts vs 4.2 mid-season, so compare the engines' W1 rating dispersion to that before trusting them at face value.

theories.hypothesis: Week-1 totals: realized totals are systematically under (or over) the market, and the engine's W1 league prior (previous-season realized mean, 46.0) is mis-levelled.
theories.method: 1999-2025 W1 (n=428): per-season market vs realized, O/U record, pooled residual with bootstrap CI, W1 vs W5+ Welch and season-clustered test; W1 realized vs previous-season mean and vs same-season W2+ mean per season (t-test, sign test); rolling-origin (t=2005..2025) comparison of W1 priors: P0 = prev-season mean (engine), P1 = P0 + delta fitted on prior seasons, P2 = 3-yr mean, P3 = P0 + trend, M = market, M1 = market + fitted delta.
theories.metric: total residual (realized - line) mean and O/U %; OOS MAE / bias of candidate priors
theories.result: Market W1 residual -0.47 (se 0.64) [-1.67,+0.75] p=0.46; under 232-192 = 54.7% [49.8,59.5] p=0.058; 17 of 27 seasons under. 2022-25: -2.59 (se 1.55), under 65.6% p=0.017 (n=64). W5+ residual +0.76 (se 0.18, p<0.001) so W1 - W5+ = -1.23 (Welch p=0.066; season-cluster p=0.105). Scoring level: W1 realized is 1.30 pts below the same season's W2+ mean (se 0.71, p=0.078; 20 of 27 seasons negative, binomial p=0.019) and 1.32 below the previous-season mean (se 0.75, p=0.092); the market's W1 total is 0.61 (se 0.20) below the previous-season mean (prices about half the dip). Rolling-origin priors (n=335 W1 games 2005-25): P0 MAE 10.92 bias -1.38 [-2.92,+0.09]; P1 (delta ~ -1.3) MAE 10.80 bias +0.36, MAE diff -0.12 [-0.31,+0.07] p=0.21; P2 +0.05, P3 worse; market MAE 10.39 (-0.54 vs P0, p=0.008); M1 vs M -0.03 (n.s.). Splits: outdoor <80F -1.30 (n=193), dome +0.17 (n=109), mid totals 42-47.5 -1.41 (n=197). 2025 realized mean = 46.03 (engine 46.0 confirmed).
theories.recommendation: Not exploitable as a blanket 'under' (54.7%, CI includes the 52.4% break-even). But the engine's W1 prior is levelled at the previous-season mean, which has run ~1.3 pts above W1 scoring with a bias CI that barely touches 0, while the market already sits 0.6 below that mean; lower the W1 prior by 1.0 (about 2/3 of the point estimate, keeping the engine within 0.4 of the market level) and revert from Week 2.
theories.parameter_change: Week 1 only: league_prior_total = previous-season realized mean - 1.0 => 45.0 for 2026 Week 1 (46.03 - 1.0), reverting to 46.0 from Week 2. Rating coefficient c stays 0.35. Equivalent implementation: W1 flag adds -1.0 to every engine implied total before weather/pace adjustments.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv REG total_line and scores, 27 seasons of Week 1 (428 games) and all-season means
theories.effect_size: W1 scoring ~1.3 pts below both the previous-season mean and the rest of the season; engine-prior bias -1.38 pts; market residual -0.47 (all weeks +0.69)
theories.expected_impact: Removes ~1.0-1.3 pts of W1 total bias; OOS MAE gain ~0.12 (CI [-0.31,+0.07]); W1 team totals shift -0.5 each
theories.uncertainty: Each angle is p 0.06-0.10; the sign test on seasons (20/27, p=0.02) is the strongest. In 2009-25 alone the dip vs previous-season mean is -0.67 (se 0.83), smaller than the 27-season figure.
theories.caveats: Not a betting signal at -110; a level correction for an engine that otherwise ignores the W1 dip. Totals expert's work on the general +0.7 under-pricing of scoring in W5+ is complementary - W1 is the one bucket where that positive bias is absent.

theories.hypothesis: Teams with a new head coach in Week 1 are mispriced by the market (residual vs close differs from 0).
theories.method: Coach-change flags from games.csv coach names (1999-2025): new_hc = W1 head coach coached the team in no game of the previous season; hc_first = also never appears as HC before (>=2002). Game-level OLS err_mkt ~ (home flag - away flag) with HC1 se, FIT/TEST split; ATS of backing the flagged team; residual vs the rating line (2009+); persistence in W1-4, W5-18, full season; team-level mean cover margin by era.
theories.metric: residual vs market close per net flag (pts), back-flag ATS %
theories.result: W1 new HC: coef -0.18 (se 1.11) [-2.36,+2.00] p=0.87 on 412 games / 171 flagged team-games (6.6 per season); FIT -0.21, TEST +0.02; back ATS 73-75 = 0.493. First-time HC (n=104 team-games): -0.61 (se 1.42), ATS 50-45. Market prices new HC at only +0.19 (se 0.24) pts vs the rating line and the residual vs the rating line is -0.10 (se 1.40). W1-4: -0.02 (se 0.57, 556 events); full season -0.41 (se 0.27); TEST full season -0.94 (se 0.62). Era means (W1): 1999-2008 -0.6, 2009-16 +2.6, 2017-25 -2.7 (all se ~1.9) - noise. New HC AND new QB: +1.41 (se 1.61). 2026 W1 new-HC teams in the file: BAL, CLE, PIT, TEN, LV, MIA, NYG.
theories.recommendation: No Week-1 (or season-long) head-coach-change adjustment; the market and the ratings are both unbiased for these teams.
theories.parameter_change: Keep as is: new_head_coach_adj = 0 in Week 1 and all weeks.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv home_coach/away_coach, closing spreads; nfelo elo_line for 2009+ pricing check
theories.expected_impact: None
theories.uncertainty: 171 flagged team-games give a +/-2.2 pt CI; an effect under ~2 pts cannot be excluded but every window and split is centred near 0.
theories.caveats: Flag is from the schedule file's coach field; interim-turned-permanent coaches count as not-new. First-time HC before 2002 unknown (excluded).

theories.hypothesis: Teams with a new Week-1 starting QB (different from last season's primary starter) are mispriced by the market in Week 1.
theories.method: new_qb = W1 starter != previous season's most-frequent REG starter for the team (games.csv qb names); alternative qb_new_to_team = no REG start for the team last season. Same regressions/ATS as 4a; pricing vs rating line (mkt - elo_line), residual vs elo_line and vs nfelo raw (with 538 QB adj), persistence W1-4 / W5-18.
theories.metric: residual vs market close per net flag (pts), back-flag ATS %
theories.result: W1 new_qb: +2.13 (se 0.98) [+0.22,+4.05] p=0.029 on 412 games / 265 flagged team-games; FIT +2.10 (p=0.07), TEST +2.31 (se 1.77, p=0.19, 35 events); back ATS 99-71-3 = 0.582 [0.504,0.657] p=0.038; team-level mean cover +1.41 (se 0.84). 2009+ (n=253): market prices the flag only +0.39 (se 0.22) worse than the rating line; residual vs rating line +1.58 (se 1.13), vs nfelo raw +1.77 (se 1.13): new-QB teams beat both the ratings and the market. Alternative definition weaker: +0.94 (se 1.13), ATS 0.550. Effect is W1-specific: W1-4 +0.62 (se 0.50), W5-18 -0.04 (se 0.28), ATS 0.496. Joint with new HC: new_qb +2.15 (p=0.03), new_hc -0.30.
theories.recommendation: Small, capped Week-1-only lean toward teams whose planned W1 starter differs from last season's primary starter, at half the point estimate; and never apply the engine's 'starter->backup' downgrade (-2.0..-4.5) to a planned new starter in Week 1 - those teams have outperformed, not underperformed, the number.
theories.parameter_change: Week 1 only: spread_adj = +1.0 pt toward the team with a new planned starting QB (vs previous-season primary starter); 0 from Week 2; counts against the W1 context-adjustment cap; QB starter->backup downgrade applies only to in-week injury replacements, not to offseason changes.
theories.data_used: games_1999_2025.csv home_qb_name/away_qb_name, closing spreads; nfelo 2009+ for pricing vs ratings
theories.effect_size: +2.1 pts vs market (CI +0.2 to +4.1); +1.6 vs rating line; ATS 58%

theories.hypothesis: Home-field advantage is different (lower) in Week 1 and the engine should use a Week-1-specific HFA.
theories.method: Non-neutral games 2009-2025 with nfelo: OLS margin ~ rating gap by bucket and era, intercept = HFA at equal ratings; interaction test margin ~ elo_dif + W1 + elo_dif*W1; market home residual by bucket 1999-2025 (n=425 W1) and market-implied HFA (intercept of -mkt ~ elo_dif).
theories.metric: HFA at equal ratings (pts) with HC1 se; W1 shift with p-value; market home residual
theories.result: HFA other weeks +2.09 (se 0.22); W1 shift -1.04 (se 0.84, p=0.22) [W1 est +1.05, se 0.82, n=250]. 2021-25: other weeks +2.10, W1 shift -2.07 (se 1.42, p=0.14); 2022-25: -1.47 (se 1.54, p=0.34). Market home residual W1 1999-2025: -0.83 (se 0.64, p=0.20) vs +0.30 (se 0.23) in W10+; market-implied HFA W1 +2.04 vs nfelo hfa_pts 2.21. Same sign in every era and both measures, none significant.
theories.recommendation: Keep nfelo's per-game site HFA in Week 1. If a haircut is wanted for consistency with the consistent negative sign, limit it to -0.5 (half the shrunk estimate) and label LOW; do not go to the -1.0 point estimate.
theories.parameter_change: Keep as is (site HFA unchanged in W1); optional W1 HFA = site HFA - 0.5, LOW confidence.
theories.data_used: nfelo starting Elo + hfa_mod 2009-2025 non-neutral; games.csv closing spreads 1999-2025
theories.effect_size: W1 HFA ~1.0 pt lower than other weeks (se 0.8); market home residual -0.8 (se 0.6)
theories.expected_impact: At most ~0.5 pt on W1 spreads if adopted; 0 if kept
theories.uncertainty: 250 W1 games with ratings give se 0.8 on the intercept; a W1 HFA anywhere in [0, +2.6] is consistent with the data.
theories.caveats: HFA expert covers the league-wide HFA level and era trend; this is only the W1 increment on top of whatever base they recommend.

theories.hypothesis: Information beyond preseason ratings (news, context adjustments, market moves) is worth less in Week 1, so W1 adjustment caps should be tighter and the engine should not chase the market's deviation from its ratings.
theories.method: Regress err_elo_line (margin + rating line) on dev = market close - rating line by bucket; info share = -slope (1 = market's deviation from ratings fully earned, 0 = noise); interaction tests dev*W1 and dev*(W1-4) with HC1 se on 2009-25, 2015-25, FIT, TEST; OOS cap test: pred = rating line + clip(dev, -c, c), c chosen on FIT, MAE vs market on TEST with paired bootstrap; open->close line movement and residual dispersion by bucket.
theories.metric: info share of market deviation (regression slope), OOS MAE vs market of capped line
theories.result: Info share: W10+ 1.09 (se 0.09), W5-9 0.64 (se 0.15), W1 0.41 (se 0.35), W2 0.86, W3 0.25, W4 0.81. Interaction 2009-25: other weeks 0.93 (se 0.07), W1 change -0.52 (se 0.35, p=0.14); W1-4 vs W5+: 0.97 -> 0.58, change -0.40 (se 0.18, p=0.028); 2015-25: W1 change -1.10 (se 0.45, p=0.015), W1-4 change -0.50 (p=0.015); FIT W1-4 -0.37 (p=0.08), TEST W1-4 -0.38 (p=0.29). When the market is >2.5 from the ratings the market side wins by +4.9 (se 0.5) in W10+ but only +1.7 (se 1.6) in W1 (TEST W1: -1.3, n=16). OOS cap test TEST 2022-25: W1 best cap on FIT = 1.0 -> MAE vs market -0.23 [-0.57,+0.10] p=0.19 (n=62); W1-4 -0.03 to -0.07 (n.s.); W5+ any cap hurts (+0.17 at c=2.5, p<0.01). W1 lines move more open->close (1.38 vs 1.25, p=0.15) but the W1 close is not better than the open (-0.11 [-0.35,+0.14]) whereas W10+ close is (-0.19, p<0.01). Residual SD W1 12.97 vs 13.13; SD(market - rating line) 2.25 in W1 vs 3.27 in W10+.
theories.recommendation: In Week 1 trust the preseason ratings: tighten the context-adjustment caps and do not let a large gap to the market pull the number. Keep confidence-tag thresholds unchanged (outcome variance and engine-market dispersion are not larger in W1).
theories.parameter_change: Week 1 only: cap on the SUM of section-5 context adjustments 1.5 pts on the spread (from 2.5) and 2.0 on the total (from 3.0); each individual adjustment scaled by 0.6 before capping; from Week 5 revert to 2.5/3.0 (Weeks 2-4 may use 2.0/2.5). No W1 change to confidence-tag SD thresholds.
theories.data_used: nfelo starting Elo + hfa_mod (rating line), nfelo market open/close, games.csv closing spreads 2009-2025 non-neutral
theories.effect_size: Market information beyond ratings is worth ~40% of face value in W1 and ~60% in W1-4 vs ~95-100% from W5+ (W1-4 difference -0.40, p=0.03)
theories.expected_impact: Capped-at-1.0 rating+market line beat the market by 0.23 MAE in W1 2022-25 (CI includes 0); the parameter change mainly prevents over-adjusting ~20-25% of W1 games where |market - ratings| > 2.5
theories.uncertainty: W1 alone is p=0.14 (2009-25) / p=0.015 (2015-25); the pooled W1-4 test is the significant one. The cap value 1.5 is a judgement (between the FIT-optimal 1.0 and the current 2.5), not a fitted optimum.
theories.caveats: The market's deviation from ratings is a proxy for the engine's own news-driven adjustments, which cannot be backtested directly; the claim is about the value of non-rating information early, not about the engine's specific adjustment list. Market expert's open-to-close work is complementary.

experts.summary: All scripts and logs: /home/user/originator-2026-w01/research/experts/earlyseason/ (00-06 + run_all.sh; common.py defines the lines; sanity: corr(mkt, margin) = -0.43, decomposition nfelo_dif_base = elo_dif + hfa_mod + qb exact). Rating series = nfelo starting Elo (no PFF/Cole history exists). Headline: Week 1 is NOT a week to distrust preseason ratings. The regressed preseason Elo + site HFA line matches the closing market in Weeks 1-4 (W1 MAE 9.79 vs 9.82, diff +0.03 [-0.23,+0.29]) and only falls behind from Week 10 (+0.22, p<0.01); its slope is ~1.05-1.17 (no shrink), the optimal W1 multiplier is 0.94 with a flat loss curve (MAE gain -0.03 [-0.08,+0.03]), and the market's W1 home/favorite/dog residuals are all within +/-0.8 of zero (n=428) with no extra variance (Levene p=0.69). What IS different in Week 1 is the value of information beyond the ratings: the market's deviation from the rating line is worth ~40% of face value in W1 and ~60% in W1-4 vs ~95-100% from W5+ (W1-4 change -0.40, p=0.03), and W1 closes are not better than W1 opens. Totals: W1 scoring runs ~1.3 pts below both the previous-season mean and the rest of its own season (20 of 27 seasons, p=0.02), the market prices about half of that (-0.6), the engine's prior (prev-season mean) none of it (rolling-origin bias -1.38 [-2.92,+0.09]); blanket unders are 54.7% (not bettable). New head coach: nothing (-0.18, se 1.1, ATS 0.493). New planned starting QB: +2.1 vs market (p=0.03, ATS 0.58, TEST same sign) but definition-sensitive. Change first: (1) Week-1 total prior = previous-season mean - 1.0 -> 45.0 for the 2026 card (2025 realized 46.03), reverting to 46.0 in Week 2 - cheapest, three independent angles agree, moves the engine toward the market; (2) Week-1 context-adjustment cap 1.5 spread / 2.0 total (from 2.5/3.0) and do not chase the market gap - the ratings are the strongest thing the engine has in Week 1; (3) LOW-confidence +1.0 W1 lean toward teams with a new planned starting QB and never apply the starter->backup downgrade to a planned offseason change; (4) keep everything else as is: k=1.0, totals c=0.35, site HFA (optional -0.5 W1 haircut, LOW), confidence tags, no new-HC term. Rating weights and scale should not be reduced early; if anything W1-4 is where the rating engines deserve the most trust.

verdicts.reason: All numbers reproduce (01_league_hfa_by_season.py, 01b_hfa_constant_bootstrap.py). Two methodological problems, neither fatal: (1) the 1.75 point estimate and the 1.5-2.0 band were read off the 2022-25 test-window MAE curve (test-optimal k on a 0.25 grid is 1.25), i.e. the constant was selected on the test set; (2) the 'decline since 2009' is not significant on mean-based tests (2009-13 vs 2014-25 rating-HFA diff +0.78, Welch p=0.109; raw margin +1.03, p=0.055; game-level trend -0.057/yr, p=0.19) - it is significant only for medians (Mood median test p=0.019, 2.60 vs 1.47; median-HFA trend -0.114/yr, p=0.018) and for the market line (2.43 -> 1.63, p<0.001). Both survive because pre-2022 information already gave the same answer (last-5-season fit 2016-21 ex 2020: MAE-optimal k=1.50, median 1.50, mean 1.73) and a pre-specified rolling-origin test over 2015-2025 (n=2511) confirms the ranking: fixed 2.5 is worse than fixed 1.75 by +0.044 [+0.016, +0.073], than fixed 2.0 by +0.034 [+0.016, +0.053], and than a trailing-5-season mean by +0.028 [+0.004, +0.051]; leave-one-season-out MAE(2.5)-MAE(1.75) stays +0.034..+0.051 in every fold. 1.5/1.75/2.0 remain indistinguishable (fixed2.0 - fixed1.75 = +0.010 [+0.001, +0.020] in 2015-25, +0.013 [-0.002, +0.027] in 2022-25). No dome/outdoor split: Welch p=0.67 (2021-25) and p=0.72 (2009-25). ATS: no constant yields an edge vs the close (0.492-0.501 in 2022-25); k=2.5 would make the model pick home 70% of the time vs the market for zero cover gain. Sign check corr(mkt_spread, margin) = -0.438.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: critic_01_hfa1.py: rating-free measures agree (2022-25 mean margin 2.19, median 2.0, mean line 1.61; median-regression intercept 1.37 se 0.43 vs mean 2.13 se 0.39). Rolling-origin 2015-2025 ex 2020 (n=2511): MAE fixed1.5 9.959, fixed1.75 9.964, fixed2.0 9.974, roll5_median 9.967, roll5_mean 9.980, allprior_mean 9.997, fixed2.5 10.008, nfelo per-game 10.009, market 9.853; nfelo per-game minus fixed1.75 = +0.045 [-0.003, +0.092]. Market residual 2022-25: mean +0.58 but median 0.00 - the mean is skew (home blowouts), so the median-optimal constant (~1.4-1.5, the market's 1.55) is the right target for a spread meant to be compared to the market.
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep HFA_PFF = HFA_COLE = 1.75 (band 1.5-2.0), no dome split. Confidence HIGH that the constant should be <= 2.0 and not 2.5; MED for the exact 1.75 (post-hoc choice, but 1.5-2.0 are within +/-0.01 MAE of each other). If the spread's purpose is ATS comparison against the close, lean to 1.5; if mean-margin calibration, 2.0.

verdicts.reason: Numbers reproduce, but 'REJECTED, HIGH confidence, zero OOS predictive slope' over-states a low-power null. The 2022-25 window (n=1064, slope se 0.36-0.40) cannot distinguish a slope of 0 from 0.6. A pre-specified rolling-origin test over 2014-2025 ex 2020 (fit = all prior seasons, n=2726) gives: nfelo hfa_mod/25 excess slope 0.70 (se 0.28, p=0.011; 0.66 with season FE), nfelo hfa_pts excess 0.45 (se 0.21, p=0.033), EB team excess 0.25 (se 0.38, p=0.51), raw excess 0.12 (se 0.13). The nfelo slope is 0.63 (p=0.014) in 2014-19 and 0.13 (se 0.36) in 2021-25 - the expert's 'collapsed to zero' reading is one of two readings consistent with that se, and nfelo's hfa_mod provenance (possibly fit on 2009-19) is unknown, so the 2014-19 number may be optimistic. Team heterogeneity is weakly present: odd/even-season split-half r=0.23 (p=0.22, 30 teams), 2009-14 vs 2015-25 r=0.27 (p=0.16), one-way ANOVA of residual by home team p=0.083 (market residual p=0.054). MAE is unable to adjudicate either way: pooled OOS MAE(nfelo hfa_mod/25) - MAE(const) = +0.001 [-0.031, +0.034]; hfa_pts (with tz) +0.031 [-0.013, +0.073]; EB +0.013 [-0.011, +0.037]. So the correct statement is 'team/site HFA is small (sd ~0.7-0.9 pts), partially predictive pooled, undetectable in MAE' - not 'noise'. The parameter change itself (constant; drop the separate tz add-on) still stands because it is MAE-neutral and the double count is confirmed and larger than stated: hfa_mod ~ 0.96*hfa_base_mod + 1.16*tz (R2 0.57; b_tz 1.19 in 2021-25; 2022-25 mean hfa_mod - hfa_base_mod = -9.6 / -1.5 / +14.2 Elo for tz<0 / 0 / >0), so ORIGINATOR's (hfa_mod + tz) carries ~2.2x the time-zone term. Denver: excess positive in 10 of 16 seasons, market residual +1.52 (se 1.21), home cover 0.513 - no basis for a +0.75 bump.
verdicts.rerun_result: Reproduced: tau 0.67 fit / 0.00 test, shrink 0.18, team corr r=0.21 (p=0.243), OOS slopes EB 1.35 (se 1.37), raw 0.23, nfelo 0.15 (se 0.40); OOS MAE const 9.795, const+EB 9.797 (+0.002 [-0.016,+0.021]), nfelo hfa_pts 9.802, hfa_mod/25 9.793; calibration slope 0.67 (2009-19) vs 0.02 (2021-25); corr(hfa_mod, tz) 0.62; DEN +2.00 (se 1.21, p=0.10).
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: critic_02_site.py and critic_06_extra.py: rolling-origin pooled 2014-25 slopes as above; MAE differences vs constant all inside +/-0.035. Composition: nfelo's OWN published line reconstructs as Elo dif + QB + bye + div + surface + hfa_base_mod + home_time_advantage_mod in 88-92% of games every season (the rest are 70% bye-mod games); it matches core + hfa_mod in only ~27% and core + hfa_mod + tz in ~10%. hfa_base_mod is a league-level series (sd 5-9 Elo); the hfa_mod column has sd ~27 Elo (~1.1 pts), of which hfa_base_mod + tz explain 50-57% and home-team fixed effects add only 1.3% (2021-25 R2 0.495 -> 0.508).
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Adopt the constant 1.75 in the PFF/Cole paths and remove the home_time_advantage_mod add-on (confirmed double count). Restate the evidence as 'MAE-neutral simplification', not 'nfelo site HFA is noise' (pooled slope 0.45-0.70, p 0.01-0.03; modern-window slope 0.13 +/- 0.36). If a per-game site term is ever retained, use hfa_mod/25 alone, never hfa_mod + tz. Drop the optional Denver +0.75 (unsupported). Confidence for 'do not build a team HFA table': MED.

verdicts.reason: Numbers reproduce and the recommendation (no slot HFA) survives every alternative I ran, though the SNF null is less clean than 'HIGH confidence' implies. Pooled 2009-25 ex 2020 with season FE: SNF +1.86 (se 0.90, p=0.039), MNF -0.38, TNF +0.17, SAT -1.80 (p=0.17), wk1 -1.39 (p=0.12); market residual SNF +1.65 (p=0.07). A within-season label-permutation placebo puts the fit-window max |t| (2.74, SNF) at p=0.043 across the 5 slot dummies, and SNF has the same sign in odd (+1.30) and even (+2.36) seasons - so it is borderline rather than nothing. But it fails the tests that matter: 2022-25 deviation -0.97 (se 1.39); rolling-origin 2014-25 ex 2020 (n=2726) applying prior-season slot coefficients gives slope 0.36 (se 0.20, p=0.081) on the residual and RAISES MAE (10.080 -> 10.094); market residual slope 0.34 (p=0.09). Week 1: 0.89 vs 2.25 (Welch p=0.125), market residual -1.17 vs +0.24 (p=0.11), below the season's own HFA in only 9 of 16 seasons - noise. Classification confound checked: TNF unchanged with rest_dif control (expert), Thanksgiving/other slots too small.
verdicts.rerun_result: Reproduced: full-sample SNF 3.90 (se 0.86, p=0.049), MNF 1.62, TNF 2.18, SAT 0.47, WK1 0.89 (p=0.16); fit regression SNF +3.01 (p=0.006), wk1 -1.32; OOS deviations SNF -0.97, MNF -2.41, TNF -1.13, SAT -1.03, WK1 -1.93; OOS slope 0.30 (se 0.34); MAE 9.795 vs 9.797; home cover by slot all CIs contain 0.50.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: critic_03_slot.py: pooled season-FE regression, permutation placebo (B=400, p=0.043), odd/even split (SNF +1.30/+2.36, MNF -0.22/-0.92, TNF +0.61/-0.69, SAT -1.57/-1.79, WK1 -2.32/+0.10), rolling-origin 2014-25 (slope 0.36 se 0.20; MAE worse by +0.014).
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep as is - no slot or Week-1 HFA. Lower the stated confidence to MED and flag SNF (+1.9 pooled, p=0.04, consistent across odd/even seasons but negative in 2022-25) for re-test after two more seasons; do not act on it now.

verdicts.reason: INCONCLUSIVE is the right label and the numbers reproduce; n is far too small for any constant between 0 and 2. Two corrections to the narrative. (1) The expert missed four Bills-in-Toronto games coded location==Home (2009-2012, Rogers Centre); including them moves the international edge from 0.96 to 0.79 (CI [-2.71, 4.38], n=52) - immaterial. (2) 'nfelo does not zero HFA at neutral sites' is only half right: nfelo's base HFA IS zeroed (hfa_base_mod = 0 in 55/55 neutral REG games); the non-zero hfa_pts comes from the time-zone mod, computed from the teams' home cities regardless of venue (|tz|>0.1 in 30/61 neutral games; e.g. LA@JAX in London 2025: tz +0.89, hfa_mod 1.47, hfa_pts 2.37) plus the tz component embedded in hfa_mod. corr(nfelo hfa_pts, realized designated-home edge) at neutral sites is -0.34 (n=55). So the override recommendation is right, and it is specifically the time-zone term that must be killed at neutral sites. OOS n=22 paired-bootstrap MAE differences vs k=0.75: k=0 +0.25 [-0.04, +0.53]; k=2.0 -0.24 [-0.69, +0.23] - nothing separable.
verdicts.rerun_result: Reproduced: 54 international REG games (48 rated), edge 0.96, bootstrap CI [-2.54, 4.79] (seed differs from the expert's [-2.59, 4.69]), market residual -1.07, home cover 26-28, Welch vs regular HFA p=0.53; OOS n=22 MAE k=0 8.16, 0.75 7.91, 2.0 7.67, nfelo 8.15, market 7.59; |hfa_pts|>0.25 in 34/55 neutral games.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: critic_04_neutral.py: with Toronto Home games edge 0.79 [-2.71, 4.38]; ex Toronto entirely 1.06 [-2.58, 4.85]; London-only n=36 edge 1.01 (se 2.35), home cover 18-22; nfelo component audit as above.
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep the spec constants (0.75 international, 0.0 domestic neutral / Super Bowl) and hard-override nfelo at location==Neutral; specifically zero home_time_advantage_mod there, since that (not hfa_base_mod) is the leak. LOW confidence on the 0.75 vs 0 vs 2 choice remains correct; JAX-London or country tweaks unsupported.

verdicts.reason: Spread part (the hypothesis as stated) is correctly rejected and reproduces; rolling-origin 2014-25 ex 2020 (n=2726) gives div-specific HFA no value (MAE 10.080 vs 10.079; residual-on-adjustment slope 0.51, se 0.60, p=0.40). The secondary totals recommendation is what gets downgraded. In-sample it is robust: the market total residual div coefficient survives week fixed effects and weather/roof controls (-1.35, se 0.47, p=0.004 full sample; -1.50, p=0.007 fit; test 2022-25 -0.67, p=0.45), and the raw total gap after the same controls is -1.49 with the market pricing only -0.13. But the market-relative OOS evidence is weak and presented too favourably: (a) the season count is 12 of 16 ex 2020 (binomial p=0.077), not 13/17 - the extra season is 2020, which the expert excludes everywhere else; (b) rolling-origin 2014-25 pooled market residual gap is -0.69 (se 0.52, p=0.19) and the divisional under rate is 0.521 with 95% CI [0.489, 0.552] (n=1002); (c) MAE vs the market is unchanged with any version of the adjustment (-0.002 [-0.042, +0.037]) and O/U picks vs the market go 0.508 -> 0.505; (d) the gap is concentrated in weeks 14-18 (-2.19, p=0.011) and is driven by NON-divisional late-season games going over (+2.00, n=496) more than by divisional games going under (-0.19), which undercuts the 'div games are under-priced' framing. What does survive is the model-calibration argument: an engine that ignores div_game (proxy = prior-season mean + 0.35*rating_sum) shows an OOS bias gap of -1.32 pts (div -0.97 vs non-div +0.34, se 0.55, Welch p=0.016), and the recommended -1.0/+0.5 zeroes it (bias +0.03 / -0.16) with MAE -0.011 [-0.038, +0.017].
verdicts.rerun_result: Reproduced: HFA div vs non-div -0.51 (p=0.25) full, -0.77 fit, +0.16 test; rating slope x div +0.02 (se 0.08); market slope x div +0.08 fit / -0.13 test; fav cover div 0.468 [0.417, 0.520] test; OOS div-specific HFA MAE 9.531/9.941 vs const 9.571/9.921; nfelo close bias +0.77 (se 0.62) in div games; totals residual gap -1.57 (p=0.002) fit, -0.90 (p=0.28) test; 13 of 17 seasons negative; OOS totals MAE 10.237 -> 10.236.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: critic_05_div.py, critic_06_extra.py: controls (season FE + week FE + dome + temp + wind) leave the div coefficient at -1.35 (p=0.004); by week bucket gap -0.96 / -1.09 / -2.19 (p=0.17 / 0.19 / 0.011); by roof dome -0.75 (p=0.39), outdoor -1.42 (p=0.006); rolling-origin pooled gap -0.69 (p=0.19), under rate 0.521 [0.489, 0.552]; engine-proxy bias gap -1.32 (p=0.016); MAE deltas all within [-0.04, +0.04]; season sign count 12/16 (p=0.077), with within-season week FE 11/16, mean -1.39 (se 0.46).
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Spread: keep as is (UPHELD). Totals: treat the divisional term as a calibration fix for a model that otherwise ignores div_game, not as an edge against the market. Apply model_total += (-0.75 if div_game else +0.40) (mean-preserving at the 36% div share; sized between the OOS market gap -0.7 and the engine-proxy gap -1.3), LOW-MED confidence, and hand it to the totals expert with the note that the late-season (weeks 14-18) non-divisional over pattern (+2.0) deserves its own look. Do not expect an O/U gain vs the close.

critics.notes: All nine expert scripts were re-run unchanged from /home/user/originator-2026-w01/research/experts/hfa/ and every reported number reproduced (logs in the scratchpad; only the bootstrap CI bounds differ in the third decimal by seed). Sign convention verified: corr(mkt_spread, margin) = -0.438, corr(rating_dif, margin) = +0.423. Critic scripts (all re-runnable, printing every number cited): critic_01_hfa1.py (rating-free/median HFA by block, era and trend tests, pre-specified rolling-origin 2015-25 and 2022-25 with paired bootstrap and ATS), critic_02_site.py (nfelo hfa_mod composition, rolling-origin team HFA 2014-25, odd/even split, ANOVA, Denver by season), critic_03_slot.py (pooled season-FE, permutation placebo, odd/even, rolling-origin, Week 1), critic_04_neutral.py (Toronto games, nfelo component audit at neutral sites, n=22 bootstrap), critic_05_div.py (spread rolling-origin; totals confounds week/weather/roof; rolling-origin totals vs market and vs an engine proxy; season sign tests), critic_06_extra.py (nfelo_dif_base reconstruction by season, dome/outdoor Welch, leave-one-season-out, engine-proxy bias gap). General methodological notes: (1) the expert's HFA-1 constant grid was evaluated on the test window, so the specific 1.75 is post hoc; I substituted pre-specified rolling-origin constants and the conclusion held. (2) Several 'REJECTED / HIGH confidence' verdicts rest on 2022-25 slopes with se 0.3-0.4, which cannot reject moderate effects; I pooled rolling-origin 2014-25 (n~2700) to raise power and reported both windows. (3) MAE on a 13-14 pt SD margin/total cannot detect 0.5-1 pt adjustments applied to a subset of games; wherever the expert cites 'MAE unchanged' as evidence of no effect, treat it as 'undetectable', and use slope/bias/cover-rate tests instead. (4) The rating series is nfelo Elo + nfelo QB mod throughout; no PFF/Cole history exists locally, so all HFA levels are conditional on that series being unbiased, which the rating-free checks (mean margin, mean line) support.
critics.additional_findings:
1. nfelo's published line is NOT built from the hfa_mod column. nfelo_dif_base reconstructs exactly (|res|<1 Elo) as Elo dif + QB mod + net bye mod + div mod + surface mod + hfa_base_mod + home_time_advantage_mod in 88-92% of games in every season 2009-2026 (remaining games are 70% bye-mod cases), versus ~27% with hfa_mod and ~10% with hfa_mod + tz. hfa_base_mod is a smooth league-level series (mean 62 Elo in 2009 falling to 41 Elo in 2022-25, sd 5-9 Elo within season); hfa_mod has sd ~27 Elo (~1.1 pts), is ~0.96*hfa_base_mod + 1.2*tz + unexplained residual, and home-team fixed effects explain only 1.3% of it in 2021-25. ORIGINATOR's PFF/Cole site HFA = (hfa_mod + home_time_advantage_mod)/25 therefore (a) double-counts the time-zone term at ~2.2x and (b) imports ~1 pt SD of per-game variation that nfelo itself does not use in its line. This strengthens the HFA-2 parameter change on grounds the expert did not state. Script: critic_02_site.py, critic_06_extra.py.
2. The market residual in 2022-25 has mean +0.58 but median 0.00 and home cover 0.498 (skew 0.17): home teams win big more often than they lose big. A spread meant to be compared with the close should target the median (market's ~1.55), which is why 1.25-1.5 is MAE-optimal in the test window and why leaning home (k=2.5 picks home 70% of the time vs the market) buys nothing ATS. Script: critic_01_hfa1.py.
3. In the rolling-origin ATS check, the nfelo-Elo + constant-HFA spread went 0.519-0.527 ATS vs the closing line pooled 2015-2025 but 0.487-0.501 in 2022-2025 for every HFA constant. Whatever ATS value the nfelo rating series has is concentrated pre-2020 (possibly in-sample for nfelo); relevant to the 0.46 nfelo blend weight, not to HFA. Script: critic_01_hfa1.py.
4. Late-season non-divisional games (weeks 14-18, n=496, 2009-25 ex 2020) have a market total residual of +2.00, versus -0.19 for divisional games in the same weeks and +0.4..+0.8 for non-divisional games earlier; the 'divisional under' gap is largely this late-season non-divisional over. Worth a dedicated look by the totals expert (rest/motivation/weather pricing). Script: critic_05_div.py.
5. nfelo applies its time-zone mod from team home cities even at overseas venues (e.g. LA@JAX London 2025 gets +0.89 pts tz and 2.37 pts total 'HFA'); corr(nfelo hfa_pts, realized designated-home edge) at neutral sites is -0.34 (n=55). Any consumer of nfelo mods must zero home_time_advantage_mod at location==Neutral. Script: critic_04_neutral.py.
6. Four Bills-in-Toronto games (2009-2012, Rogers Centre) are coded location==Home in games_1999_2025.csv; they do not change the international result but should be excluded from any 'regular home game' sample.

verdicts.reason: All numbers reproduce and the finding survives every alternative I threw at it. Placebo: the MARKET close shows the same OLS>1 / median<1 split (OLS 1.058, median 0.974, Huber 1.047 vs nfelo 1.035 / 0.959 / 1.023), so that split is a fat-tail property of NFL margins, not evidence against 25 Elo/pt. A results-only Elo with canonical 538 parameters (nothing fitted) also calibrates at 25/pt (slope 1.003 +/- 0.067), so 25/pt is not an artifact of nfelo's market-informed ratings. Direct MAE-optimal grid search picks 26.5-27 Elo/pt every rolling year but the pooled rolling gain is -0.004 [-0.017,0.009] p=0.56; test -0.012 [-0.032,0.009] p=0.245. The expert's best OOS candidate (piecewise median, -0.025 p=0.105 on 2022-25) is -0.011 [-0.028,0.007] p=0.23 in rolling-origin 2013-25, i.e. noise. Big-favorite shrink/expand with no fitting: at |proj|>=7, x1.10 costs +0.084 (p=0.005) and x1.15 +0.150 (p=0.001) over all seasons while x0.90 is neutral (-0.011, p=0.71); at |proj|>=10 both directions hurt, so 1.0 is at the optimum. Signed deciles (home perspective) show nfelo within +/-0.9 pts of realized in all 10 deciles (all seasons). Minor correction: live nfelo v3 (historic file) maps Elo to points at exactly 25/pt pre-regression (59% of rows exact, mean |diff| 0.15); the '~27 Elo/pt' the expert cites is a property of the rounded unregressed line in the backfilled scored file (reproduced: median 26.97, IQR 26.39-27.61), not of live nfelo.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: critic_01_scale.py: Huber slopes nfelo 1.023 (all) vs market 1.047; per-season nfelo OLS b<1 in 5/17 seasons, median b<1 in 13/17 (market 5/17, 9/17) -> mild hint MAE-optimal scale is 26-27, but MAE grid: train-opt 26.5 -> test 9.762 vs 9.774 (dMAE -0.012 [-0.032,0.009] p=0.245); rolling pooled picked-scale -0.004 p=0.56, fixed 26 -0.005 [-0.013,0.004] p=0.25; piecewise-median rolling -0.011 [-0.028,0.007] p=0.23; POST-only slope 0.89 +/- 0.26 (n=196, uninformative); big-favorite factor test as described. critic_06_pure_elo.py: results-only Elo calibration slope 1.009 (train), 0.983 (test), 1.003 (all).
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep ELO_PER_POINT = 25, linear, no hinge/shrink. If an MAE-optimal constant is ever wanted, 26-27 Elo/pt is the defensible value (rolling-origin picks it every year) but the gain is <=0.012 MAE and not distinguishable from zero.

verdicts.reason: Every number reproduces, but the theory's central label is wrong: the nfelo number is NOT market-blind, so the 0.238 MAE loss and the 1.7-pt gap are LOWER BOUNDS on what a truly market-blind origin number loses. (a) Empirical: regressing each team's within-season Elo change on its own-forecast error and the market gap (market line minus nfelo line, team perspective) gives -3.1 Elo per point of gap (+/-0.14), which survives full Elo-update controls (538-style K*MOV*(W-p) term, own line, interactions, R2=0.85), is present even in games where nfelo's own forecast was within +/-1 pt (slope -0.56 +/- 0.17; mean Elo change +1.5 / -0.2 / -1.3 across market-gap terciles), and is stable across eras (-2.8 to -3.3). That is ~26% of the per-team rating gap implied by 1 pt of line disagreement closed per game. (b) Source-verified (greerreNFL/nfelo, config.json v4.3.1, Utilities/elo_shift.py): calc_shift inflates k by (1 + |model_error - market_error| / market_resist_factor[=1.5039]) whenever nfelo missed the result by more than the closing line did; the rating 'observations' blend actual margin 0.7382 / PFF point margin 0.1113 / WEPA 0.1506; the offseason prior uses market win totals (wt_ratings_weight 0.4496) and DVOA 0.3637. (c) Bound: a results-only Elo with canonical unfitted 538 parameters (K=20, log MOV, 1/3 reversion, nfelo's own per-game HFA) loses 0.434 [0.262,0.606] MAE vs the close in 2022-25 without a QB term and 0.366 [0.222,0.514] with nfelo's QB term (vs 0.238 for nfelo_lin); it sits 2.53 pts from the close (nfelo 1.82) and goes 48.4% ATS vs the close in 2022-25 (50.0% over 2009-25). K=15/25 give 0.345/0.419. (d) Era structure the expert did not report: nfelo_lin vs close dMAE 2009-13 +0.109 (p=0.12), 2014-18 -0.028 (p=0.67), 2019-21 +0.206 (p=0.013), 2022-25 +0.238 (p<0.001); the pooled 2009-25 ATS of 52.5% is entirely 2014-18 (55.7% [0.525,0.589] p<0.001 at |gap|>=0.5; 59.1% at >=2), with 51.2% in 2019-21 and 49.5% in 2022-25 (by season 54.8/47.5/45.2/50.9). So 'no edge since 2022' should read 'no edge since 2019'. OLS w by era: 0.31, 0.68, 0.20, -0.12 (+/-0.31-0.38); a 4-season recency-window rolling w picks 0.00-0.16 since 2021 and the pooled blend is +0.008 [-0.017,0.034] vs the market.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: critic_02_market.py (sections A-D), critic_05_elo_update.py, critic_06_pure_elo.py as described. Also informational (critic_02 E): against the OPEN line nfelo_lin is as accurate as the opener over 2009-25 (dMAE +0.017 [-0.049,0.080], p=0.62) but worse in 2022-25 (+0.114 [-0.012,0.246] p=0.08); ATS of nfelo_lin vs the open 53.9% (n=3394, p<0.001; 56.1% at >=2, n=1445) over 2009-25 and 52.9% (n=900, p=0.09; 54.4% at >=2, n=373, p=0.10) in 2022-25; nfelo predicts open->close movement with slope 0.29 +/- 0.07 (R2 0.16). This inherits the market-informed caveat (nfelo already contains the previous weeks' closes) and the open column has a few sign errors.
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep 'no market term'. Replace the informational constants: (1) relabel the nfelo component as market-, PFF- and WEPA-informed (it embeds prior closing lines through market_resist_factor=1.5039 and PFF point margins at 0.1113 weight), not market-blind; (2) a truly market-blind origin number should be expected to sit ~2.5 pts from the close and lose ~0.37-0.43 MAE (nfelo's 0.24 is the floor); (3) nfelo's edge vs the close existed only in 2014-18 and has been absent since 2019, not just since 2022; (4) w_engine vs close ~0.2-0.3 pre-2019, ~0 since; (5) confidence tags built on inter-engine SD measure agreement between engines that share market and PFF inputs and must not be read as edge. For the blend expert: the 0.46 nfelo / 0.39 PFF weights double-count PFF.

verdicts.reason: The expert's INCONCLUSIVE verdict is correct and the numbers reproduce; my alternatives sharpen it. Placebo engines (critic_03 D): clamping a pure-noise engine X = nfelo + N(0, 2.31) to nfelo+/-4.5 'helps' by -0.004 MAE (200 draws), while clamping the MARKET close (a better engine) to nfelo+/-4.5 hurts by +0.018 [0.006,0.033] p=0.009 in 2022-25 and +0.015 [0.008,0.023] p<0.001 over 2009-25. So the clamp's sign is set purely by which engine is more accurate, exactly as the expert says, and the effect is bounded at +/-0.02 MAE either way. Weight dominates clamp: reducing qbelo's weight from 0.459 to 0.2 with no clamp (test 9.784) beats the 0.459 blend with the k=4.5 clamp (9.808). The expert's proposed anchor rule (lower trailing-3-season MAE) picks nfelo in 13 of 14 seasons (qbelo only in 2015), so it cannot be validated with this proxy. New finding relevant to the confidence tags: inter-engine disagreement |qbelo - nfelo| does not predict the error magnitude of nfelo, the blend or the market (slopes +0.05/+0.06/-0.02 per pt, all p>0.48, Spearman ~0 over 2009-25); in the >=4.5 bin the market's MAE is actually lower (9.71 vs 10.12 overall). Disagreement measures engine noise, not game difficulty. New confound: nfelo's ratings ingest PFF point margins (pff_weight 0.1113, source-verified), so a PFF-vs-nfelo gap partly reflects PFF disagreeing with a lagged version of itself; qbelo is a poor proxy for that.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: critic_03_clamp.py: placebo noise engine -0.004 (test and all); market-as-X clamp +0.018 p=0.009 test, +0.015 p<0.001 all; weight grid (test): w_qbelo 0.459 no clamp 9.827 / clamp 9.808; 0.3: 9.797 / 9.787; 0.2: 9.784 / 9.778; 0.1: 9.776 / 9.774; nfelo alone 9.774. Trailing-3-season rule: nfelo anchor 13/14 seasons. |gap| vs |err| slopes ~0 (all seasons), +0.22/+0.29/+0.16 in test (p=0.14/0.06/0.23).
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep k=4.5 as cheap insurance and do not tune it (as the expert says), but the cleaner fix is to drop the clamp and set PFF's weight by rolling backtest once PFF history exists; the anchor-by-trailing-MAE rule is reasonable but unvalidated. Do not use inter-engine SD as a proxy for game difficulty or edge.

verdicts.reason: Numbers reproduce and the finding survives the attacks that matter for the parameter decision. The strongest attack is that 'nfelo_noqb' strips the QB term from ratings that were maintained with it, which is not a self-consistent no-QB model; but ORIGINATOR's actual choice is exactly 'apply nfelo's term (multiplier 1) or strip it (0)', so the strip test is the right test for QB_MOD_MULTIPLIER. The decisive new evidence is the LIVE nfelo series (historic_projected_spreads.csv, v3.x, no backfill, 2022-25 n=972): the live pre-regression line with vs without its own live QB term is -0.138 [-0.229,-0.045] p=0.004; in |qb|>=1.5 games (n=222) -0.463 [-0.834,-0.111] p=0.014; |qb|>=2 (n=142) -0.726 [-1.257,-0.194] p=0.008; live coefficient on the QB term 1.55 +/- 0.56. Live and backfilled QB terms correlate 0.871 and differ by >1 pt in 8.9% of games, so the backfill is not what drives the result. Per-season the term helps in 14/17 seasons (sign test p=0.013). Inside |qb|>=3 games the realized fraction is 1.19 [0.92,1.46] (n=410), so 3-4.5 pt adjustments are not overstated. Caveats that limit but do not overturn: (1) the self-consistent FiveThirtyEight pair (pure Elo 538_se vs qbelo_se) shows the QB term worth -0.161 [-0.230,-0.090] in 2009-21 but +0.068 [-0.033,0.175] in 2022-25 and +0.133 [0.034,0.235] p=0.012 in 2023-25 (where the '538' values are nfelo's reproduction), i.e. the value of a QB term is implementation-dependent and 538's version stopped adding value OOS; (2) because nfelo's ratings are market-informed (see T2), some QB information already leaks into the no-QB rating, so -0.11 is if anything a lower bound; (3) the extrapolation to the section-5 starter->backup range is weak: the term is a continuous QB-quality delta, not a backup-swap event, and the |qb|>=3 subset (n=410) is the closest analogue.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: critic_04_qb.py: 538 self-consistent pair as above (all 2009-25 -0.101 [-0.157,-0.042] p=0.001); live nfelo test as above; realized-fraction slopes: |qb|>=1.5 all 1.28 [1.04,1.52], >=2 all 1.29 [1.04,1.54], >=3 all 1.19 [0.92,1.46], test 1.33-1.53; per-season 14/17 negative. critic_06_pure_elo.py: adding nfelo's QB term to a results-only Elo improves it by -0.068 in 2022-25 (9.970 -> 9.902) and -0.067 over 2009-25, a smaller but same-signed effect.
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep QB_MOD_MULTIPLIER = 1.0 (points = home_net_qb_mod/25). Every specification puts the realized coefficient at 1.2-1.5 with CIs touching 1.0 and a multiplier of 1.1-1.3 buys <=0.005 MAE, so do not tune. Treat the section-5 starter->backup range as consistent with, not validated by, this result.

critics.additional_findings:
1. nfelo's Elo is market-, PFF-, WEPA- and win-total-informed by construction (source-verified in greerreNFL/nfelo: config.json v4.3.1 market_resist_factor=1.5039, margin_weight 0.7382, pff_weight 0.1113, wepa_weight 0.1506, wt_ratings_weight 0.4496, dvoa_weight 0.3637, qb_weight 1; Utilities/elo_shift.py calc_shift inflates k by (1+|model_err-market_err|/1.5039) when the model missed by more than the close). Empirically (critic_05_elo_update.py, n=7912 team-games): the per-game Elo update pulls a team's rating toward the market by -3.1 Elo per point of line disagreement (+/-0.14, R2 0.85 with full controls; -0.56 +/- 0.17 even when nfelo's own forecast was within 1 pt; stable -2.8 to -3.3 across eras), closing ~26% of the implied per-team rating gap per game. Consequences for the panel: (a) the ORIGINATOR nfelo component is not market-blind; (b) the 0.46 nfelo / 0.39 PFF blend double-counts PFF; (c) inter-engine SD measures agreement between engines that share inputs; (d) all 'no market input' claims about the v5 build need this footnote.
2. Bound on a truly market-blind number (critic_06_pure_elo.py, canonical unfitted 538 Elo with nfelo's own HFA): vs the close 2022-25 +0.434 [0.262,0.606] MAE without QB, +0.366 [0.222,0.514] with nfelo's QB term; 2.53 pts from the close (nfelo 1.82); ATS vs close 48.4% test, 50.0% all; corr with nfelo_noqb 0.922, mean gap 1.70 pts; it still calibrates at 25 Elo/pt (slope 1.003 +/- 0.067). Sensitivity K=15/25: +0.345/+0.419 with QB.
3. nfelo's historical edge vs the close is a single era: 2014-18 ATS 55.7% [0.525,0.589] p<0.001 (59.1% at |gap|>=2, n=433); 2009-13 52.8% (p=0.10); 2019-21 51.2%; 2022-25 49.5% (by season 54.8/47.5/45.2/50.9). dMAE vs close by era: +0.109 / -0.028 / +0.206 / +0.238. The pooled 52.5% the expert reports is not a stationary property.
4. Against the OPEN line (informational, critic_02 E): nfelo_lin matches the opener's MAE over 2009-25 (dMAE +0.017, p=0.62) but not in 2022-25 (+0.114, p=0.08); ATS vs open 53.9% (n=3394, p<0.001) all seasons and 52.9% (n=900, p=0.09; 54.4% at >=2, n=373) in 2022-25; nfelo predicts open->close movement with slope 0.29 (R2 0.16). Inherits the market-informed caveat and the open column's occasional sign errors (25 sign disagreements between nfelo's market column and the nflverse close, 8 with |diff|>3).
5. Inter-engine disagreement is not game difficulty: |qbelo - nfelo| has zero relation to |error| of nfelo, the blend, the market or nfelo's close (slopes -0.02 to +0.06 per pt, p>0.48, Spearman ~0, 2009-25); in the >=4.5 bin the market's MAE is 9.71 vs 10.12 overall. Confidence tags built on inter-engine SD should be labeled 'engine agreement', not 'confidence'.
6. Elo-to-point mapping in live nfelo v3 is exactly 25/pt pre-regression (home_line_pre_regression == -home_dif_pre_reg/25 in 59% of rows to 0.01, mean |diff| 0.15, live decomposition holds within 1 Elo in 91.5% of rows); the '~27/pt' is the backfilled scored file's rounded unregressed line (reproduced median 26.97, IQR 26.39-27.61; 4.4% of games have an ambiguous root in the reconstruction).
7. Market top-decile favorites (>=10.5) beat the close on average by +1.35 (n=342, realized 14.39 [13.02,15.68] vs 13.04) and +2.49 in 2022-25 (n=96, 14.98 [12.65,17.42] vs 12.49), while nfelo's top decile is +0.67/+0.83; but market cover rates in the 10-14 and 14+ bins are 49.3% and 46.0% and medians sit below projection, so this is a blowout-tail (MAE) feature, not an ATS edge. INCONCLUSIVE; for the favorites/key-number expert.
8. The QB-term coefficient is >1 in every specification (1.24 backfill, 1.55 live, 1.19-1.29 in large-adjustment subsets) which hints nfelo's qb_weight=1 slightly understates QB effects, but a 1.1-1.3 multiplier changes OOS MAE by <=0.005; not worth tuning (agrees with expert).
9. The 538 qbelo vs pure-Elo pair shows the QB term's value is implementation-dependent: -0.16 MAE in 2009-21, +0.07 (n.s.) in 2022-25, +0.13 (p=0.012) in 2023-25. Any PFF/Cole QB table used in section 5 should be validated on its own, not assumed to inherit nfelo's result.

verdicts.reason: Every reported number reproduces exactly (01, 06, 09 re-run byte-identical). Sign convention verified independently on raw data: corr(spread_line, result) = +0.426, so mkt_spread = -spread_line gives -0.426. Attacks: (1) slope-only Wald tests the expert did not report for fav/dog on 1999-2021: fav p=0.19, dog p=0.023 — the dog |S| slope is -0.567 (t=-2.03 vs -0.5), and the favorite-margin slope on |S| is 1.103 (se 0.049) in train and 1.110 (se 0.107) in test. This is a small, stable SPREAD bias (favorites cover ~1.10 pts per pt of line), not an allocation error; the implied team-total mis-split is < 0.25 pts anywhere in |S| <= 10. (2) Huber robust regression gives slopes closer to the identity than OLS (T 0.475-0.487, S -0.519/+0.532). (3) Season-block bootstrap (games within a season share a bias): the expert's rolling-origin home CI for identity-vs-nonlinear-OLS widens from [-0.027,-0.001] to [-0.030,+0.002] (no longer excludes 0); away stays [-0.035,-0.004]. (4) Modern-only expanding window (fit from 2009, score 2014-2025, n=3295): identity better than nonlinear OLS in 12/12 seasons on away (p=0.003), 7/12 on home (p=0.35); never significantly worse. Conclusion 'keep the identity' survives all of it.
