Modern-only expanding window 2014-25: home-nl -0.0095 [-0.0262,+0.0066] (7/12 seasons), away-nl -0.0297 [-0.0458,-0.0136] (12/12). fav_margin ~ |S| + T: slope 1.103 (se 0.049) train, 1.110 (se 0.107) test.
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep as is: home = T/2 - S/2, away = T/2 + S/2, no intercept, no favorite/dog nonlinearity. The 1.10 favorite-margin slope is for the spread expert (effect < 0.25 pts on any team total).

verdicts.reason: INCONCLUSIVE is the right label, and the evidence leans further toward 'no effect' than the expert's caveat ('at most -0.5 below 15') implies. Numbers reproduce. Attacks: threshold sensitivity — train P(over) is 0.440 (p=0.004) at tt<=15 but 0.463 (p=0.39) at tt<=13 and 0.474 (p=0.10) at tt<=16; the 2009-2025 subset at tt<=15 is 0.459 (n=231, p=0.24); Holm-adjusted minimum p across the 8 bins is 0.033; season clustering: only 17/27 seasons have P(over)<0.5 at tt<=15 (p=0.25). A -0.5 shade at tt<=15 lowers MAE in-sample on 1999-2021 (+0.048 [+0.016,+0.079], season-block CI) but not in 2009-2025 (+0.028 [-0.056,+0.095], n=235) and hurts in 2022-25 (-0.079 [-0.167,+0.024], n=57). At tt<=17.5 no shade helps anywhere (test flat -0.5: -0.021 [-0.051,+0.003]).
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep as is; no median/skew shade at any team-total level. The '-0.5 below 15' caveat is supported only in-sample on 1999-2021 and should not be implemented without a fresh OOS confirmation.

verdicts.reason: Numbers reproduce; the algebra (asymmetry = half the conditional spread error) is correct, so this theory is a test of market spread bias, not of the split. Attacks: HFA-scales-with-total: sp_err ~ T slope +0.017 (p=0.62) train, -0.10 (p=0.25) test — no T-scaling; home_fav x |S| interaction p=0.13 train / 0.85 test; home-share residual by T tercile: 5 of 6 cells have CIs spanning 0 (test mid-T +0.016 [-0.0003,+0.032] is the lone borderline cell). Per-season spread error: 2019 -1.86, 2020 -1.00, then 2022-25 +0.43/+1.13/+0.39/+0.69 — an HFA regime for the spread expert, not a share rule.
verdicts.rerun_result: Train non-neutral n=6071: r_home +0.350, r_away +0.357, spread err -0.006 [-0.341,+0.329]; home_fav coef on r_fav -0.129 (p=0.629); test r_fav home_fav +1.244 (p=0.028), tot_err +1.391 (p=0.086); neutral n=94 r_home -0.61; train k=-0.003 — identical.
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep as is (home share adjustment = 0). Route the 2022-25 +0.66 home spread error to the HFA expert.

verdicts.reason: Numbers reproduce. Larger-n alternative: rolling-origin reallocation (fit on all prior seasons, score season s, 2005-2025, pooled n=5698) makes the identity WORSE (home -0.018, season-block CI [-0.036,-0.000]; away -0.013 [-0.025,-0.000]; rule better in only 7/21 seasons), and the same holds with a last-16 window and a season-to-date variant. The sum-preserving single index is consistently but negligibly positive (+0.0026 MAE, season-block CI [-0.0007,+0.0056], 15/21 seasons, reallocation SD 0.22 pts) — it is a recent-form momentum effect in the spread (train sp_err ~ (X_home - X_away) +0.047/pt, p=0.011), not a split effect. Rating levels (nfelo Elo) predict spread error in 2009-21 (home +0.28 pts/pt, p=0.01) but not in 2022-25 (-0.08, p=0.62).
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Matchup reallocation from PF/PA profiles: 0. (Spread expert may note the negligible recent-form momentum: ~0.05 pts per point of net last-10 PF/PA differential.)

verdicts.reason: Numbers and the pbp feature file reproduce exactly (rebuild max diff 0.0). The practical conclusion (no reallocation) survives, but one claim is over-stated: the 2023-25 'sign flip / no replication' is a low-power result. Power of the n=773 test to detect the train epa_home (-0.51/unit) and expl_home (-0.31/unit) effects is only 0.36 and 0.25; z(test - train) = +1.32 (p=0.19) and +1.48 (p=0.14), so the test is consistent with both zero and the train effect. Split-half of train: expl_home is -0.445/SD (2009-14) and -0.430/SD (2015-19), same sign both halves (p=0.15 each); epa_home is -0.25 (p=0.51) vs -1.12 (p=0.00), unstable. Decisive check: rolling-origin reallocation fit on all prior seasons, pooled OOS 2013-2019 + 2024-2025 (n=2362), is WORSE than the identity (home -0.019 [-0.039,+0.001], away -0.013 [-0.029,+0.004]; better in 3/9 and 2/9 seasons). Pipeline placebo with the team's NEXT-10-game features gives +1.1 to +1.3 pts/SD (p<1e-4), so the pipeline can detect a 1-pt/SD effect; prior-10 features show none in the spec's direction, and the only in-sample signal is the wrong sign.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: Split-half per-SD effects (2009-14 | 2015-19 | 2023-25): expl_home -0.445 | -0.430 | +0.163; epa_home -0.254 | -1.116 | -0.033; rz_away -0.226 | -0.450 | +0.573. Rolling-origin 3-index reallocation pooled n=2362: home -0.0188 [-0.0391,+0.0007], away -0.0125 [-0.0292,+0.0038]. Power in test: epa_home 0.36, expl_home 0.25. Future-feature placebo: epa_home +1.111 pts/SD (p<0.0001), epa_away +1.338, expl_home +0.625 (p=0.0007).
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Explosive / red-zone / pace reallocation default 0 with a +/-0.5 hard cap, as the expert says. Wording: the test period does not replicate the train effect but is under-powered (0.25-0.36), so 'sign flips OOS' should read 'no stable effect; every OOS application of the fitted rules raises MAE'.

verdicts.reason: Numbers reproduce. The coherence claim is exact algebra (max |(home_tt - away_tt) + S| = 0.0 across 7276 games; +d/-d implies S' = S - 2d). The noise cost is not period-specific: U(0.5,1.5) random reallocation costs +0.048 MAE on 2010-2021 (n=3224) and +0.042 on 2022-25. Replacing the Normal approximation with the empirical residual distribution, the break-even true (median) shift for a 0.5 reallocation is ~0.2-0.25 pts, for 1.0 ~0.5, for 1.5 ~0.9 — the expert's 'x/2' rule holds. No candidate in TT3a/TT3b reaches +0.25 OOS, so default 0 is the right setting. Rounding to .0/.5 is costless (-0.004).
verdicts.revised_recommendation: As the expert: derive team totals from the final adjusted spread and total; matchup reallocation default 0, cap +/-0.5, and any sum-preserving delta must be mirrored as spread_final = spread - 2*delta.

verdicts.reason: Numbers reproduce. The MEAN effect is actually more robust than the expert's INCONCLUSIVE suggests: an honest rolling selection (pick the bin with the largest prior-season r_fav, score it in the next season, 2005-2025) gives pooled OOS r_fav +1.02 (n=793), positive in 18/21 seasons, season-block CI [+0.63,+1.37], with 7-9.5 chosen 16/21 times; the bin's excess over the season-wide r_fav in 2010-25 is +0.79 [+0.25,+1.29]; a within-season permutation over the 5 bins gives P(max positive-season count >= 24) = 0.006, so it is not pure bin-fishing. BUT it is a right-tail (blowout) effect, and team totals and spreads are priced at the median: median fav_sp_err in the bin is -0.5, favorites went 345-378 ATS (47.7%, p=0.23) in the bin 2010-25 and 70-98 (41.7%) in 2022-25; in-bin P(total over) by era 0.469/0.518/0.491/0.519/0.544. No actionable rule clears zero in rolling OOS 2010-25 (bin fixed a priori, n=741): fav_tt += 0.5 dMAE +0.017 [-0.006,+0.039] (9/16 seasons; +0.003 per game overall), fav_tt += 1.0 +0.012 [-0.038,+0.058], total += 0.5 +0.009 [-0.023,+0.039], total += 1.0 +0.001 [-0.057,+0.057]. Bin-boundary sensitivity is poor: train r_fav is +1.61 at exactly |S|=7 (n=439) but +0.32 in [8,10] (n=642); test is the reverse (+0.53 at 7, +1.89 in [8,10]). The expert's optional 'spread toward favorite 0.5' would have lost ATS in train (49.4%) and test (41.7%) and must be dropped.
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep the allocation as is (agree). Delete the optional 'spread toward favorite 0.5 when 7 <= |S| <= 9.5' — favorites are under 50% ATS in that bin in every OOS period; the +1 mean is blowout skew, not a median edge. The totals expert may test at most +0.5 in the bin, but the rolling-origin evidence (+0.009 MAE [-0.023,+0.039]) does not justify it yet. Re-test after 2026.

critics.additional_findings: 1. Favorite-margin slope: fav_score - dog_score ~ |S| + T gives an |S| slope of 1.103 (se 0.049) on 1999-2021 and 1.110 (se 0.107) on 2022-25 — favorites cover about 1.1 pts per point of line (t=2.1 vs 1.0 in train, same point estimate OOS). This is a spread-side bias for the spread expert; for team totals it implies a mis-split of at most 0.25 pts for |S| <= 10 (0.5*(0.103|S| - 0.59)), which the rolling-origin OLS could not exploit. 2. Season clustering: the expert's game-level paired bootstraps understate uncertainty; with season-block bootstraps the home-side identity-vs-alternative advantages lose significance (though the identity is never worse), and the away-side ones survive. 3. PF/PA recent-form momentum in the spread: sp_err ~ (X_home - X_away) coefficient +0.047/pt (p=0.011, train), sum-preserving rule better in 15/21 rolling-origin seasons but only +0.0026 MAE — negligible, spread expert. 4. nfelo Elo level predicted the market spread error in 2009-2021 (+0.28 pts per pt of home rating vs avg, p=0.01; away -0.16, p=0.10) but not in 2022-25 (-0.08, p=0.62) — relevant to the spread expert's market-regression/blend weights, not to team totals. 5. Market total attenuation E[total|T] is 4.21 + 0.919T (se 0.035) on 1999-2021 but 1.59 + 0.982T (se 0.095) on 2022-25, i.e. weaker recently — totals expert. 6. HFA regime: non-neutral spread error (margin + S) by season 2019 -1.86, 2020 -1.00, 2022 +0.43, 2023 +1.13, 2024 +0.39, 2025 +0.69 (sem ~0.75 each) — HFA expert. 7. Pipeline sanity for the pbp features: using each team's NEXT 10 games (future info) the same indices predict identity residuals at +1.1 to +1.3 pts/SD (p<1e-4), confirming the feature construction works and that the prior-10 null is not a bug.
critics.notes: All critic scripts are saved under /home/user/originator-2026-w01/research/experts/teamtotals/ as critic_01_identity.py, critic_02_median.py, critic_02b_lowtt_shade.py, critic_03_home_away.py, critic_05a_pfpa_rolling.py, critic_05b_pbp_split.py, critic_07_noise.py, critic_08_favbin.py, critic_08b_favbin_rules.py, with logs _critic_*.log and critic_run_all.sh to re-run them (python3 from that directory; they import the expert's common.py and kit.py). Reproduction: I re-ran all ten expert scripts (run_all.sh order) and diffed against _run_all.log — output identical line for line; 04a's rebuilt _pbp_teamgame.csv is byte-identical (max numeric diff 0.0). Sign check done independently on raw games_1999_2025.csv: corr(spread_line, result) = +0.426, home favored in 65% of games, so kit's mkt_spread = -spread_line has corr -0.426 with margin as the README requires; identity home_tt = T/2 - S/2 = T/2 + spread_line/2 puts the home favorite above T/2 as intended. No leakage found: all features are strictly prior (shift(1) rolling, windows reset at the 2019->2023 pbp gap), z-scores use train moments, the benchmark is the closing line. Data: no local PFF/Cole history was used; the rating-level check uses nfelo Elo (starting_nfelo_home/away, 25 Elo = 1 pt) via kit.load_nfelo. Bootstrap CIs in my scripts are season-block (seasons resampled with replacement, 2000 reps) unless labeled game-CI; the expert's are game-level. The net verdict is that the expert's core recommendation is right — keep the identity, remove/zero the matchup reallocation block with a +/-0.5 cap and the spread-mirroring coherence rule — with two corrections: TT3b's 'sign flip OOS' language overstates an under-powered test (power 0.25-0.36), and TT5's optional favorite spread lean should be dropped because favorites in the 7-9.5 bin are below 50% ATS in every OOS period even though their mean score residual is robustly about +1.

verdicts.reason: Numbers reproduce exactly, but the headline (spec bias +1.32, dMAE -0.16) is a straw man: the README defines the spec constant as '46.0 = 2025 realized mean', i.e. the spec's own mechanism IS the prior-season mean (lg_prev), and lg_prev was also 46.0 in 2022. Against the fair reference (lg_prev + 0.35*elo, OOS MAE 10.714) the slope change 0.35->0.28 is worth -0.006 [-0.027,+0.017] and the whole recommendation -0.051 [-0.100,-0.004]; all of the gain is the in-season blend, none is the slope. Any slope 0.20-0.35 is within +/-0.005 MAE OOS. With the nfelo join repaired (+317 training games, see additional findings) b = 0.299 [0.208,0.390], Huber 0.327, so 0.35 is comfortably inside the CI. 'Market prices Elo fully' confirmed in every era (residual slope +0.08/-0.04/+0.01, all p>0.27).
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: Repaired join (train n=3344): OLS b=0.299 [0.208,0.390], Huber 0.327 (se 0.045). K_lg grid, no fitting, paired vs lg_prev: K=128 gives -0.043 [-0.081,-0.003] on 2010-2021 (n=3088) and -0.045 [-0.091,-0.004] on 2022-2025; K=256 -0.036/-0.035 with tighter CIs; K=16-64 CIs include 0. Gain concentrates in years when the prior-season mean was >2 pts off (2018, 2020-2022, 2024).
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep the level mechanism the spec already has (prior-season REG mean; 46.0 for 2026) and ADD the in-season blend LG = (K*L_prev + n*L_ytd)/(K+n) with K=128-256 (expected -0.04 to -0.05 MAE, CI barely excludes 0). Do not bother changing the slope: 0.35 is inside the CI and OOS-indistinguishable from 0.28; if a single number is wanted use 0.30. Confidence MED, not HIGH.

verdicts.reason: Reproduces and survives every attack. Repaired join: pf_dev +0.347 (se 0.061), pa_dev +0.269 (se 0.054), Wald pf=pa p=0.41, Huber 0.330/0.274. The obvious confound - that K_team=1 blends are really a fast tracker of the CURRENT season's league scoring level (lg_blend with K=128 is slow) - is excluded: an explicit league tracker alone adds nothing (-0.007 [-0.035,+0.018] vs Elo-only) while team-only deviations from the fast league mean give the full gain (-0.140 [-0.269,-0.006]; expert's version -0.147 [-0.279,-0.010]). Rolling-origin over 10 test seasons (2016-2025, n=2639) drop-S costs +0.111 [+0.028,+0.196]; Elo adds only +0.008 [-0.004,+0.019] once S and Q are in.
verdicts.rerun_result: 02_totals_model.py reproduced (K=1/K_lg=128 selected on 2015-21 validation; L+E 10.657 -> L+E+S 10.521; drop S +0.108). 05: pf_dev 0.340 / pa_dev 0.272, Wald p=0.51, gt_dev 0.304. critic_02: same on repaired join.

verdicts.revised_recommendation: Adopt as stated; prefer the single term 0.30*(sum of both teams' PF and PA deviations from league ppg) - same OOS MAE (10.295 vs 10.288) and one fewer parameter. K_team anywhere in 1-6 is fine (3 is a reasonable middle).

verdicts.reason: The model is sound and the feature ranking survives rolling origin, but two claims are overstated. (1) The precipitation term (-1.5) was sized on 2023-25 = the TEST period, and it is worth -0.024 of the headline: honest V3 OOS MAE is 10.312 (dMAE vs market +0.123 [-0.013,+0.257]), not 10.288; a full refit on the repaired join gives 10.331 [+0.000,+0.277]. (2) 'Statistically indistinguishable from the market' is absence-of-evidence: point estimate 0.12 worse, per-season 2022 +0.05, 2023 +0.00, 2024 +0.10, 2025 +0.33 worse than the close. Drop-one importances were computed on the test set; rolling origin confirms them (Q +0.094 [+0.052,+0.136], S +0.111 [+0.028,+0.196], ENV +0.066 [+0.020,+0.109], E +0.008 [-0.004,+0.019]). QB series: 100% coverage every season incl. 2026 W1, no leak (market residual ~ qb_sum p=0.17/0.44/0.92), market prices it at 0.63-1.04/pt; 2025 alone has a negative QB coefficient (-0.27, se 0.61) which is why FULL-Q beats FULL in 2025. Pace and rest conclusions confirmed (see alternative spec).
verdicts.rerun_result: 02/05/06 reproduced byte-for-byte (V3 10.288 bias -0.74, dMAE +0.099 [-0.038,+0.235], O/U 547-532). critic_02: V3 without precip 10.312 [-0.013,+0.257]; refit repaired join 10.331; rolling refit 2022-25 mean 10.337 vs market 10.189; info-beyond-market slope +0.225 (se 0.165, p=0.17).

FULL+rest/bye/week/late/neutral/grass: +0.011 [-0.013,+0.033] (n=2639), no REST coefficient p<0.17 in-sample.
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Adopt V3 without the precipitation term (or carry -1.5 flagged as untested). Quote MAE 10.31 vs close 10.19 and expect the number to run 0.1-0.3 pts/game worse than the close in a given season. Deleting the pace adjustment and not adding rest/bye/week terms are confirmed. Elo weight 0.10 is fine but immaterial.

verdicts.reason: The wind effect itself is more robust than the expert showed, but its OOS value and the slope size are overstated. Robustness: team-controlled slope with STADIUM fixed effects (within-venue identification, cluster-by-stadium SE) -0.212 (se 0.050) on 1999-2021, -0.227 (se 0.125, p=0.07) on 2022-25; Huber -0.205; negative in all five eras (-0.15 to -0.31); permutation placebo (wind shuffled within season x stadium, 300 draws) sd 0.040, zero draws as extreme. BUT: excluding the 38 games at 25+ mph the slope is -0.160 (se 0.051) in fit, so -0.2/mph is partly the 25+ tail. The claimed OOS gain '-0.099 [-0.189,-0.009]' is the WHOLE ENV table (dome + wind + cold + a test-fitted precip term) vs a mis-specified zeroed comparator; the wind piece alone is -0.033 [-0.075,+0.008] (the expert's own 03 script shows -0.031 [-0.074,+0.012]). Bins with stadium FE are not monotone (10-14 -0.99, 15-19 -2.56, 20-24 -1.25, 25+ -12.7; fine bins: 7-9 already -1.8 below 4-6). Recorded game-time wind is not the pre-game forecast the engine will have, so any realized-wind slope overstates the usable effect; the 'market exploitable at >=15 mph' framing should be dropped as a betting claim (market residual with stadium FE is consistently negative, -0.12 to -0.23/mph in every era, but only on realized wind).
verdicts.rerun_result: 03_weather.py reproduced byte-for-byte (market residual -0.166/mph; team-controlled -0.201 (2009-21), -0.214 (1999-2021, n=4193); OOS linear centered -0.031 [-0.074,+0.012]). critic_03 and critic_02 section E as quoted.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: Stadium FE + season FE: -0.224 (se 0.049). Stadium FE excl 25+: -0.160 (se 0.051, p=0.002) fit; -0.289 (se 0.137) test. Market residual bins with stadium FE: 10-14 -0.88, 15-19 -2.15, 20-24 -0.01, 25+ -10.9. Honest OOS (refit-without-ENV baseline, K=1): wind piece -0.033 [-0.075,+0.008]; ENV table without precip -0.091 [-0.180,-0.001]; rolling 10-year ENV group +0.066 [+0.020,+0.109].
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Use a linear -0.18/mph centered at 8.4 mph (binned: 0-5 +0.5 | 6-9 -0.5 | 10-14 -1.5 | 15-19 -2.5 | 20-24 -3.0 | 25+ -5.0), applied to the FORECAST wind; keep 25+ at -5 (data say -10 to -13 but n=38). Confidence MED: direction and rough size are certain, the OOS MAE payoff is ~0.03 and not individually significant.

verdicts.reason: Correctly labelled INCONCLUSIVE and the numbers reproduce. With wind linear and stadium FE: <32F -0.46 (se 1.03) fit / -0.10 (se 0.93) all - confirmed zero; <20F extra -1.88 (se 2.06, n=51) fit / -3.39 (se 1.62, n=66) all - direction supported, n far below the 150 bar. One correction: the precipitation flag exists only for 2023-25, which is the TEST period, so the -1.5 term was sized on test data and its -0.024 MAE must not be credited to V3's OOS number.

Alternative specs agree: the spread's predictive slope does not change with wind (margin ~ spread x wind interaction -0.0041, se 0.0065, p=0.53 fit; +0.0090 p=0.59 test; slope at 20 mph 1.05 vs 1.13 at 0); favorite cover margin ~ wind with stadium FE -0.053/mph (se 0.037, p=0.16) fit, +0.022 (p=0.86) test; spread MAE flat across wind bins.

verdicts.reason: +2.15 (se 0.52) reproduces; stadium-cluster se 0.55. The FE design is not biased toward positive home-venue effects: placebo pseudo-domes (home games of k random OUTDOOR teams per season, same participant-FE estimator, outdoor games only, 200 draws) give mean +0.04, sd 0.61, and 0.5% of draws >= 2.15. Leave-one-dome-team-out stays in +1.75..+2.62. The marginal dome coefficient inside the V3 spec (with PF/PA, QB, wind) is +1.97/+1.58/+2.28/+2.44 fitting on <2016/<2019/<2022/all and +2.78 (se 0.88) in 2022-25, so the table's dome vs average-wind-outdoor gap of +2.5 is consistent. Market residual dome-outdoor +0.80 (season-cluster se 0.31, p=0.010), but era-dependent: 1999-2010 +0.22 n.s., 2011-2021 +1.28 (p=0.013), 2022-25 +1.01 (p=0.08). Caveats: (i) the dome piece alone buys no OOS MAE (-0.030 [-0.098,+0.039]); it is a bias fix; (ii) within-stadium closed-vs-open at the 8 retractable venues is -1.5 (se 3.2, 128 open games) - no evidence that closing a roof per se raises scoring, the effect is identified across venues only; (iii) venue heterogeneity (per-team estimates IND -1.7, MIN 0.0, ARI +0.9 vs NO +3.1, LA +2.7, ATL +2.3, se ~1.5). Note the expert's 04 log prints 'dome vs AVERAGE outdoor = -1.84' because of a sign slip in the print formula (b_dome + b_wind*mw); the write-up's +1.8..+2.0 is the correct reading.

verdicts.reason: The formula is a sound replacement and every component reproduces, but the packaging carries three errors that change the numbers and the stated priorities. (1) Headline OOS MAE is 10.312 without the test-fitted precipitation term (10.331 on a clean refit), dMAE vs close +0.12 [-0.01,+0.26], and the model trails the close by 0.05/0.00/0.10/0.33 in 2022/23/24/25. (2) 'Order of value (1) league prior + slope 0.28 removes bias' is wrong: the spec already uses the prior-season mean, the slope change is worth -0.006 [-0.027,+0.017], and the in-season blend ~-0.05. Correct order by pooled rolling-origin 2016-25: QB term +0.094 [+0.052,+0.136] and PF/PA +0.111 [+0.028,+0.196] first, ENV table +0.066 [+0.020,+0.109] second, in-season league blend ~-0.045 third, Elo weight and slope choice last (+0.008). (3) The ENV table's OOS value is -0.091 [-0.180,-0.001] against a properly refit no-ENV baseline (no precip), with wind and dome pieces individually not significant (-0.033 [-0.075,+0.008]; -0.030 [-0.098,+0.039]). Everything else checks out: K_team 1-10 flat (rolling 10.584-10.593); Wald pf=pa p=0.41; repaired-join coefficients (elo 0.107, pf 0.347, pa 0.269, qb 0.717, div -1.64, dome +2.26, wind -0.224) match the rounded set; playoffs n=52 too small to matter; team-total identity trivially fine.

verdicts.revised_recommendation: total = LG + 0.10*elo_sum + 0.30*gt_dev (or 0.34*pf_dev + 0.27*pa_dev) + 0.72*qb_sum - 1.4*div + ENV, with LG = (K*L_prev + n*L_ytd)/(K+n), K=128-256, L_prev = prior-season REG mean (46.0 for 2026); team rates K_team=1..6. ENV: dome/closed +2.0; outdoor -0.5 - 0.18*(forecast wind - 8.4) binned 0-5 +0.5 | 6-9 -0.5 | 10-14 -1.5 | 15-19 -2.5 | 20-24 -3.0 | 25+ -5.0; <20F -1.0 provisional; no precipitation term until validated. If only ratings are available: total = LG + 0.30*elo_sum + ENV (0.35 is equally defensible). Expect MAE ~10.3 vs ~10.2 for the close and ~50% O/U; it is a pricing tool, not an edge. critics.notes: All six expert scripts (01-06) re-run from /home/user/originator-2026-w01/research/experts/totals/ and reproduce byte-for-byte (critic_repro_*.log; diffs empty after dropping the [common] header). Sign checks pass (corr(mkt_spread, margin) = -0.431 on REG 1999-2025; corr(mkt_total, total) = +0.320). Critic scripts, each with a .log: critic_common.py (helpers + repaired nfelo join), critic_00_data_checks.py, critic_01_T1a.py, critic_02_T1b_T2_T5.py, critic_03_T3_weather.py, critic_04_T4_dome.py, critic_05_qb_series.py, critic_06_pace_rest.py. Benchmark closing-total MAE 2022-25 REG = 10.189 (n=1087; the test set is complete: 4x272 minus the cancelled 2022 BUF-CIN game). Method notes: rolling-origin ablations pool 10 test seasons (2016-2025, n=2639) with paired bootstrap CIs; wind tests use stadium fixed effects with cluster-by-stadium SEs and a within-(season, stadium) permutation placebo; the dome FE design was checked with a pseudo-dome placebo under the identical estimator. Ratings series tested is nfelo Elo only (PFF/Cole have no history) - the 0.28-0.35 slope and 0.10 in-V3 weight apply to the 25-Elo-per-point conversion.
critics.additional_findings: (1) kit.py join bug affecting EVERY expert who uses kit.merged()/common.build(): games.gid only rewrites _LAR_/_OAK_, so STL/SD-id games (2009-2016) and 8 games/season 2017-2019 never match nfelo's normalized ids - 317 REG games 2009-2019 (all involving LA/LAC/LV ids) silently lose Elo/QB (coverage 0.931 -> 1.000 after normalizing both id parts with norm()). Training n is 3027 instead of 3344; the 2022-25 test set is unaffected. Totals coefficients barely move (b 0.282 -> 0.299; V3 terms within one se), but spread experts using nfelo lines on 2009-2016 have a non-random 7% hole (Rams/Chargers/Raiders games) - fix in kit.py: build gid from season_week_norm(away)_norm(home). (2) Honest decomposition of the ENV table on a refit no-ENV baseline (critic_02 E): whole table no precip -0.091 [-0.180,-0.001]; refit fitted dome/wind/cold -0.072 [-0.150,+0.006]; shape-only (centered) -0.069 [-0.158,+0.017]; wind piece -0.033 [-0.075,+0.008]; dome piece -0.030 [-0.098,+0.039]. The expert's 'ENV zeroed' comparator (10.388) happened to sit close to the honest baseline (10.403), so their -0.099 was not far off, but it includes the test-fitted precip term. (3) The 538/nfelo QB adjustment in nfelo_games.csv for 2026 W1 has about one third the dispersion of in-season values (sd 9.9 vs 27-38 Elo), so the 0.72*qb_sum term will contribute little in week 1 - not a leak, just a heavily regressed preseason value. (4) 2022 has observed wind for only 51% of outdoor games (no nflfastR fill source); common.py imputes 8 mph, so the ENV table assigns -0.5 to half of 2022's outdoor games; 2022 conclusions about weather rest on n=~140 observed games. (5) 04_dome.py prints 'dome vs AVERAGE outdoor = -1.84/-1.99' because the printout uses b_dome + b_wind*mean_wind instead of b_dome - b_wind*mean_wind; the correct values are +2.20 / +1.99 and the expert's write-up used the right sign. (6) Wind slope by era with stadium FE is negative in all five eras for both the team-controlled residual (-0.15, -0.27, -0.19, -0.31, -0.23 per mph) and the market residual (-0.13, -0.23, -0.16, -0.20, -0.12): the closing total consistently under-reacts to REALIZED wind, but because the line closes before game-time wind is known this is not by itself a bettable inefficiency; the actionable slope for an engine using forecasts is smaller than -0.2 by an unmeasured forecast-reliability factor. (7) Rolling-origin K_team 1-10 is flat (10.584-10.593 over 2016-25); the expert's validation pick of K=1 is not wrong but nothing hinges on it.

verdicts.reason: The core result is real and reproduces exactly, but three pieces of the finding do not survive. (1) The realized penalty is heavily right-skewed and the 'HIGH confidence 3.5 realized' is a full-sample, tail-driven number: fit-window (2009-21, n=221) mean +2.66 but median +1.64, QuantReg +2.42, Huber +2.71; test-window (n=75) mean +5.66 vs median +3.96 with raw residuals spanning -27..+43; leave-one-season-out realized ranges 2.99-3.84 (dropping 2024 alone moves 3.47 -> 2.99); per-season event means range -2.1..+12.4. The market-implied value, by contrast, is rock solid (2.6-2.9 under every estimator and window; jackknife 2.74-2.90). (2) The market-implied 2.8 is contaminated by a pre-existing team-level gap: the SAME teams show market-vs-no-QB-Elo gaps of +0.29+/-0.14, +0.38+/-0.14, +0.69+/-0.14 three/two/one games BEFORE the change, and already underperform by +2.7+/-0.8 two games before (events cluster after poor play, i.e. partly benchings). Stint-1 gap net of the week-before gap = +1.65+/-0.22; net of the lag-2/3 team-level gap ~2.45. (3) The sub-rule '3.5 when the displaced starter's nfelo 538 adj >= +3, 2.5 when <= +1' is non-operational and wrong-signed: the displaced starter's prior-game 538 adj ranges -5.4..+2.3 (ZERO events >= +3, because nfelo's adj is relative to the team's own baseline, not a quality level), and the slope of the market penalty on that adj is -0.29+/-0.14 (p=0.04), opposite to the rule; the +1..+3 bucket (n=17) shows market +0.55 and realized -1.45. Also: realized outcomes do not confirm the stint DECAY (fit-window realized 2.69/2.67/1.50 +/-0.8-0.9); the decay exists in market and nfelo pricing, not demonstrably in results. The 'x1.22 rescale of nfelo's adj' is worse than plain nfelo in rolling-origin (mean MAE 9.903 vs 9.887; hurts 6/10 seasons). Name-variant artifacts in games.csv (7 ids with two spellings) fabricate only 6 of 485 stint-1 events; id-keyed rerun: market +2.81, realized +3.30 (vs 3.47) - immaterial.
verdicts.rerun_result: All numbers reproduce: stint-1 in-season clean n_event=296, market +2.80+/-0.18, realized +3.47+/-0.78, 538 adj +2.30+/-0.14; 2nd-3rd +1.71/+2.31 (n=342); 4th+ +0.62/+1.51 (n=359); era 2009-15 2.57/2.72 (n=109) vs 2016-25 2.94/3.89 (n=187); OOS fit<=2021 in-season test 2022-25 n=960: no-QB line + 2.01 stint-1 penalty MAE 9.6522 -> 9.6012, dMAE -0.051 [-0.087,-0.014]; nfelo 538 adj vs no-QB dMAE -0.113 [-0.210,-0.021] (full sample); D1 look-ahead numbers (-4.26, -2.20 vs market, fade ATS 55.5% p=0.0004) reproduce and the expert is right to discard them. Permutation placebo (stint-1 flags shuffled within season, 2000 draws): null sd 0.78 = HC1 SE, p<0.0005.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: Rolling-origin 2016-25 (fit all prior in-season seasons, test one) on the no-QB line: fitted stint table beats base in 8/10 seasons, mean MAE 9.952 -> 9.908 (dMAE -0.044); expert's recommended 3.0/1.75/0.5 table 9.902 (7/10); stint-1-only 9.922; nfelo's continuous 538 adj 9.887 (better than any flat table, confirming the expert's preference for a continuous QB-gap input). Fit-window-only (2009-21) clean in-season table: market-implied 2.73/1.62/0.61 (+/-0.21/0.18/0.16), realized 2.69/2.67/1.50 (+/-0.88/0.79/0.82), nfelo embeds 2.39/1.65/0.83. Displaced-adj split: adj <= -1 (benching proxy, n=57) market +3.31, realized +0.89+/-1.69; market penalty ~ 538 drop: 2.16 + 0.41*drop.
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep a stint-indexed table but size it on the fit-window market-implied values net of the ~0.3-0.4 team-level contamination: 1st start with team this season = 2.5 (band 2.0-3.0), 2nd-3rd = 1.5, 4th+ = 0.5 (0.5-1.0 defensible: realized 1.5+/-0.7 at 4th+ in both windows). DELETE the '3.5 when displaced starter's 538 adj >= +3 / 2.5 when <= +1' conditional (no such events exist; sign is opposite). Delete the 'scale nfelo's adj by 1.15-1.2' option (hurts rolling-origin). Keep: apply only to inputs that carry no QB adjustment; when nfelo's 538 adj is available use it instead of the flat table (beats it OOS). Confidence: HIGH on the market-implied sizing, MED on realized (skewed; fit-window median 1.6-2.4). The spec's -2.0..-4.5 range: only its lower half (2.0-3.0) is supported, and only for the first start.

verdicts.reason: The parameter change (top-up = 0 on the nfelo component for in-season backup starts) survives every alternative specification. Robust estimators on the fit window put the residual after nfelo's 538 adj at stint 1 at mean +0.28, median -0.37, QuantReg -0.13, Huber +0.29 (n=221) - fully priced. The pooled any-stint residual (+0.79+/-0.41, p=0.054 full sample) is +0.68+/-0.47 (p=0.15) in the fit window and season-level values swing from -3.5 to +4.5 with n~60/season (SD across seasons ~2.2, consistent with noise). Rolling-origin 2016-25 (fit prior seasons, test one, in-season): 538 + fitted any-stint top-up mean dMAE -0.0009 (6/10 seasons), fitted stint-1 top-up +0.0017 (3/10), fixed 1.0 any-stint -0.0043 +/- 0.014, fixed 1.0 stint-1 -0.0042 +/- 0.008, nfelo close + 1.0 any-stint +0.0011, market + 1.0 stint-1 -0.0008: nothing reliable, so no top-up is the right call. One element of the recommendation is overturned: 'optionally scale nfelo's QB adj by 1.15-1.2' - the fitted-slope rescale is WORSE in rolling-origin (mean dMAE +0.0165, helps only 4/10 seasons), so drop it. The 2022-25 stint-1 residual (+4.01+/-1.57 on the all-in-season sample) is real as a watch item but is 2023-25 only (2022 was -1.2 / any-stint -3.5) and sits in the likely-injury subgroup (+4.63+/-1.78, n=63), not benchings.
verdicts.rerun_result: Reproduced: 538 adj charges 2.30 (stint 1), 1.64 (2nd-3rd), 0.91 (4th+) in-season; residual after 538 at stint 1: fit +0.31+/-0.89 (p=0.73, n=221), test +3.69+/-1.64 (p=0.02, n=75); all in-season stints +0.79+/-0.41 (p=0.05); scale slope 1.22 on <=2021 (03), 1.15+/-0.14 on the in-season fit sample; OOS: fitted stint-1 top-up -0.23 -> dMAE +0.005; fixed +1.0 on 538-adj line -0.019 [-0.038,+0.001], on nfelo close -0.013, on market -0.009; fade-backup ATS 2022-25 stint-1 48-35-3 (57.8%, p=0.19).
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: Rolling-origin 2016-25 per season (critic_02 B) and per-season residuals 2009-2025 (critic_02 A) as above; QuantReg/Huber/trimmed means (critic_01 B). Fit-window residual after 538 by stint (all in-season games): 1st -0.08+/-0.81, 2nd-3rd +1.14+/-0.73, 4th+ +0.86+/-0.72 - none significant.
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep: nfelo-component top-up = 0 for in-season backup starts; never add a QB penalty on top of a market-regressed (nfelo close) or market line. Remove the optional x1.15-1.2 rescale. Keep the 2023-25 stint-1 residual as a watch item to re-test after the 2026 season (needs ~150 events; currently 75-86).

verdicts.reason: The 59 late-season stint-1 games are not a 'rest' sample and the two headline claims do not hold once they are decomposed. Composition: 20 TRUE rest games (REG wk17/18, team made the playoffs AND the displaced starter started the next playoff game), 4 playoff teams whose starter did not return (injury), 25 ELIMINATED teams (injury/benching/evaluation), 10 playoff games (injury by definition). (i) 'Under-priced by the market': for true rest games residual vs market is +2.50+/-2.58 (median +0.2; fit +4.73+/-3.48 n=11, test -0.22+/-3.87 n=9); the broader prospective rest proxy (any wk17+ QB change on a playoff team whose previous starter started the playoff game, n=35) gives vs-market +1.74+/-2.00 (p=0.39; fit +2.17, test +1.15). The expert's +4.59 (p=0.007) comes from the ELIMINATED-team subgroup (vs market +6.96+/-3.14, n=25), which is +12.55+/-4.11 in 2009-21 (n=11) and +2.57+/-4.35 in 2022-25 (n=14) - not replicated, and not a rest phenomenon. (ii) The 'market charges 4.9' figure is a mixture: the market charges +8.88+/-1.21 for true rest (n=20; +9.54+/-0.70 for the n=35 proxy), +3.19+/-1.00 for eliminated-team changes (an ordinary backup start), +1.15+/-1.21 in playoff games. (iii) Hence the recommended 5.0-pt rule would under-price true rest by ~4 pts vs the market and over-price eliminated-team week-17/18 starts. What DOES hold: nfelo's 538 adj badly under-prices true rest (charges 3.4 vs the market's 8.9-9.5; residual after 538 +7.9+/-2.8 / +8.3+/-2.2), so a rest rule is needed for un-regressed rating inputs - but sized at ~9, not 5, and it is a whole-roster effect, not a QB parameter.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: Subgroup decomposition (critic_03): true rest n=20 market +8.88+/-1.21, realized +11.38+/-2.66, 538 +3.44+/-0.72, after-538 +7.93+/-2.79, vs market +2.50+/-2.58, resting team favored by 5.2 on average; broader rest proxy n=35 (fit 21 / test 14): market +9.54+/-0.70 / +9.75 / +9.43, realized +11.28+/-2.12, vs market +1.74+/-2.00 (p=0.39). Eliminated teams n=25: market +3.19, vs market +6.96+/-3.14 (fit +12.6 n=11, test +2.6 n=14). Playoff games n=10: market +1.15, vs market +3.55+/-3.46.
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Replace the 'starter rested -> 5.0 pts' rule. (a) Announced rest by a playoff-locked team (identifiable pre-kickoff from standings + announced starter): treat as a whole-roster event, not a QB event. The market's total discount is ~9-9.5 pts (n=20-35; SE 0.7-1.2, i.e. precisely measured but below the 150-game bar -> LOW confidence). If the un-regressed nfelo line is an input, its share needs ~0.46*(9.5-3.4) = +2.8 (not +0.9); PFF/Cole inputs need the full ~9 unless their rating post-dates the announcement; if nfelo's market-regressed close is the input, add nothing. Best practice: anchor these games to the market or do not publish (tag LOW). (b) Week-17/18 backup starts on eliminated teams: NO special rule - use the ordinary stint-1 value (2.5). (c) Playoff-game backups: ordinary stint value, no rest rule.

verdicts.reason: The expert's INCONCLUSIVE / keep-as-is verdict is correct and my alternative specifications make the week-1 effect look weaker, not stronger. The +2.24+/-1.11 (p=0.045, n=115) pooled estimate is fragile: leave-one-season-out range 1.75-2.67 and the p<0.05 survives dropping a season in only 9 of 17 cases; per-season event means range -7.5..+9.6. The 'new starter' flag also fires for RETURNING franchise QBs whose previous season was lost to injury (55 of 115 week-1 events): returning n=55 +3.05+/-1.74 (p=0.08), genuinely-new-to-team n=78 +1.15+/-1.38 (p=0.40); neither is significant in either window (returning <=2021 +2.90+/-2.10, 2022-25 +3.44+/-3.11; new <=2021 +1.28+/-1.84, 2022-25 +0.98+/-1.87). Id-keyed first-career-start n=31 +1.28+/-2.07 (2022-25 n=8: -4.21). Market move vs no-QB line: returning 0.00+/-0.33, genuinely new +0.55+/-0.28 - the market barely prices offseason changes, as the expert says. With ~20 tests in the family nothing clears any multiplicity correction.
verdicts.rerun_result: Reproduced: week-1 games 253; new-starter events 115: resid vs market +2.24+/-1.11 (p=0.045), fade ATS 48-65-2 (42.5%, p=0.13), fit +2.27 (p=0.10, n=81), test +2.25 (p=0.21, n=34); first-career-start n=32 +1.22+/-2.01; wk1-4 rookie proxy n=181 +2.06+/-1.02 (p=0.044), back-the-rookie ATS 109-68; fit +2.52 (p=0.027, n=139) vs test +0.57+/-2.26 (n=42); all-weeks <10 starts n=1083 -0.71+/-0.39.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: Returning-vs-genuinely-new split and leave-one-season-out jackknife (critic_04) as above.
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep as is: no week-1 new-starter or rookie adjustment (QB context adjustment = 0). If the flag is ever revisited, define 'new starter' as new-to-team (exclude returning franchise QBs) and key on qb_id.

verdicts.reason: The double-count logic and its numbers hold: no injury/WR/OL/pass-rush columns exist in any local file (confirmed), P=2.76 vs A_nfelo=2.31 at a first backup start reproduce (fit window), and the overshoot arithmetic is arithmetic. Two corrections to the implementation detail: (1) the proposed runtime proxy A_nfelo = -(qb_mod now - qb_mod in the last week with the starter)/25 UNDERSTATES what nfelo embeds: at stint 1 it averages +1.71 (median 1.59, sd 2.59, p10/p90 -1.4/+5.0; n=360) versus 2.08-2.30 from the regression, because the displaced starter was already rated -0.41 pts below his team's baseline on average. Since P is measured against the line with the QB adj removed entirely, the consistent A is the FULL current adj in points (= -own_538_qb_adj/25 for the backup team, i.e. exactly what nfelo adds), not the week-over-week change. (2) A per-game A is noisy: the pure gap rule tracks the market no better than a flat 2.75 (MAE of market penalty 2.87 vs 2.63 in <=2021; 2.51 vs 2.56 in 2022-25), while a shrunk 2.16+0.41*A does marginally better (2.52 / 2.38) - so shrink the per-game A toward its mean or use the stint mean. The PFF/Cole QB-adjustment assumption remains unverifiable locally (no history), as the expert states.
verdicts.rerun_result: Reproduced: no injury/WR/OL/status columns in games.csv or any other research/data file; fit-window P (market-implied) = 2.76 / 1.39 / 0.12 and A_nfelo = 2.31 / 1.57 / 0.37 by stint; overshoot 2.0/3.0/4.5 pts if the spec's -2.0/-3.0/-4.5 is added to a fully QB-adjusted blend, 0.3/1.3/2.8 if only nfelo is QB-adjusted.
verdicts.alternative_spec_result: A_proxy by stint (critic_05): 1st +1.71 (net538 regression 2.08 in the same sample, market 2.48), 2nd-3rd +1.05 (1.45 / 1.48), 4th+ +0.13 (0.53 / 0.32); share of stint-1 events with A_proxy < 1 pt = 39%, > 4 pts = 19%; market penalty ~ A_proxy: 1.78 + 0.41*A, R2 0.11.
verdicts.revised_recommendation: Keep the net-of-embedded rule QB_adj = sum_i w_i * clip(P_stint - A_i, -1.0, P_stint) with P from the revised qb-1 table (2.5 / 1.5 / 0.5), but define A_nfelo as the FULL current 538 QB adj in points for the backup team (observable in nfelo_games.csv as -home_538_qb_adj/25 or +away_538_qb_adj/25), shrunk 50% toward the stint mean (2.3 / 1.6 / 0.8) to damp per-game noise; A_nfelo = P if the input is nfelo's market-regressed close. Keep A_PFF = A_Cole = P when the rating post-dates the QB news (unverified assumption; tag LOW). Never apply the raw -2.0..-4.5 on top of the blend.

critics.additional_findings:
1. PRE-EVENT CONTAMINATION / ENDOGENEITY (critic_01b): for the same teams, the market-vs-no-QB-Elo gap is already +0.29+/-0.14, +0.38+/-0.14, +0.69+/-0.14 three, two and one games BEFORE a stint-1 downgrade, and realized underperformance vs the no-QB line is +2.7+/-0.8 two games before and +6.7+/-0.8 in the starter's last game (in-game injuries: 36% of those games were 14+ pt losses). Downgrade events are therefore partly benchings that follow poor play; ~0.3-0.4 pts of the 'market-implied backup penalty' is a team-level gap the market already had. Any market-implied QB value from this design should be read net of that (~2.45 at stint 1).
2. BENCHING vs INJURY (critic_06 b, n<150 -> INCONCLUSIVE): when the displaced starter's own 538 adj was <= -1 (benching proxy, n=59) the market charges +3.35+/-0.45 but realized is only +1.07+/-1.70 and residual vs market is -2.28+/-1.65 (fit window n=47: -2.34+/-1.79); likely-injury changes (adj > -1, n=237) show market +2.68, realized +4.07, vs market +1.39+/-0.87. Hypothesis to log: the market over-penalises benching-driven QB changes and under-penalises injury-driven ones; needs ~150 benching events.
3. STARTER-RETURN GAME (critic_01b, n=137, INCONCLUSIVE): on the first start of a more-experienced QB right after a downgrade stint the market still charges +1.37+/-0.25 vs the no-QB Elo line and nfelo +0.59+/-0.14; realized +0.59+/-1.34; residual vs market -0.79+/-1.33 (p=0.55). No evidence that the market's skepticism of returning starters is warranted, but not enough to fade it.
4. 4TH+ STINT NOT FULLY ABSORBED (critic_06 c): realized penalty vs the no-QB line at 4th+ starts is +1.51+/-0.69 (fit +1.49+/-0.82, test +1.59+/-1.25) vs market +0.62 and nfelo +0.91; residual vs market +0.89+/-0.67. The 0.5 table value is at the low end; 0.5-1.0 is defensible; no OOS test separates them.
5. ELIMINATED-TEAM WEEK 17/18 BACKUP STARTS (critic_03/06, n=25, INCONCLUSIVE): residual vs market +6.96+/-3.14 overall but +12.55+/-4.11 (n=11) in 2009-21 vs +2.57+/-4.35 (n=14) in 2022-25 - not replicated; do not build a rule on it.
6. DATA HYGIENE: nflverse games.csv has 7 qb_ids with two name spellings (Kurt Waner, Mitch/Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Herbery, Gardner Minshew (II), Michael Penix (Jr.), Taysom Kyler Murray) and Kyle Allen/Cam Newton share id 00-0034577. Name-keying fabricated only 6 of 485 stint-1 events here (immaterial), but any future QB work should key on qb_id with a manual fix for 00-0034577.
7. nfelo's fitted-slope rescale of its QB adj (1.07-1.44 depending on the training window, trending down to ~1.1 by 2023-25) does not help out of sample (rolling-origin mean dMAE +0.017, worse in 6/10 seasons): the adj's under-scaling was a 2009-2016 phenomenon that has since faded.

STRUCTURAL (largest finding, outside the expert's framing): nfelo's hfa_mod is the sum of ALL its per-game modifiers - hfa_mod = hfa_base_mod + home_time_advantage_mod + div_game_mod + dif_surface_mod + home_bye_mod + away_bye_mod exactly (OLS R2 = 1.000, residual sd 0.0000 over 4,646 games), and nfelo_dif_base = elo dif + hfa_mod + home_net_qb_mod exactly (critic_00_hfa_mod.py, critic_01_rest.py section a). The README's PFF/Cole HFA formula (hfa_mod + home_time_advantage_mod)/25 therefore injects nfelo's bye, divisional and surface mods into the 54% PFF/Cole share and counts tz 1.54x in the blend. With nfelo ratings as the stand-in, the as-built blend equals nraw_line - 0.54 x tz_pts; it carries 1.07 bye pts for the bye team before the spec clause (1.81 with it; market 1.0) and is biased -2.27 (se 0.67, p<0.001, in-sample) / -1.48 (se 1.31, test) toward the home team in west-team-at-1pm games. The correct site HFA is hfa_base_mod/25. (Cross-check: in historic_projected_spreads.csv 2021+, home_net_HFA_mod - base_hfa - time_mod is also non-zero, mean +21 Elo, so the 'net HFA' fields in both nfelo exports are composite.)
2. Sign error in the expert's T2/T3/T6 parameter text: 'subtract (home_bye_mod + away_bye_mod)/25 from its line' would DOUBLE nfelo's bye mod in ORIGINATOR sign; the strip is line + (home_bye_mod + away_bye_mod)/25 (common.py does it correctly).
3. The west-team-at-1pm-ET effect was real and unpriced before the expert's window: 1999-2008 market-only n=236, home vs close +3.09 (se 0.88, p<0.01), fade-west ATS 136-92 (0.596); it disappears from 2009 (-0.05, se 0.77). The spec clause is stale, not wrong-signed. Similarly the bye edge vs close was +1.35 (se 0.82) in 1999-2008 and -0.02 since; the market residual on rest_diff was +0.20/day (p=0.07) pre-2009 and +0.02 since.
4. Shrinking toward the market close is not a final-week phenomenon: a=0.25 shrink cuts test MAE by 0.20/game in weeks 4-16 (se 0.05; -0.143 on full-test MAE) versus -0.065 from the final-week rule; fit-set MAE-optimal engine weight is 0.20-0.30 in every bucket. This is a global engine-calibration question, and any such rule must use the line available at publish time (final-week |close - open| = 1.9 pts vs 1.0-1.2 elsewhere).
5. The 3-zone 'traveller edge' is matchup-specific rather than franchise-specific (demeaned by host and traveller team-season baselines: -3.82, se 0.90, p<0.001; SEA/SF, LA/LAC/LV and ET teams all show it only in 3-zone games), and 2018-25 is 8/8 seasons negative - but 2-zone games run the opposite way (+1.30 home, p=0.03; long 2-zone trips +2.27, p=0.004), and the 4pm-ET window (85% west-bound) carries most of it (-2.71, p=0.01). Whatever it is, it is not distance or zones-crossed monotonic.
6. The final-week engine deficit is confined to the week-18 era: 2009-20 (week-17 finals, n=175) +0.16 vs weeks 4-16 +0.05 (p=0.71); 2021-25 (week 18, n=80) +0.97 vs +0.22 (p=0.072). Plausible mechanism (17-game schedule, more clinched teams resting), but evidence is post-2021 only.
7. T5a caveat: all week-1 results test nfelo's preseason-regressed ratings only; PFF/Cole week-1 projections (54% of the blend) have no local history.

verdicts.reason: The descriptive half of the theory is UPHELD - masses reproduce (m_3 0.088 CI 0.078-0.099, m_7 0.062, 3.1x/2.2x a generic integer), are stable across windows and far-side conditioning (mass at 3 is 0.079-0.106 whether the line is 1, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5 or 6), and are a valid push/landing table. The operational recommendation - replace point-distance thresholds with the mass-table EV and act when EV>=0.02, with a -3/-7 guard - is not supported out of sample and would be harmful as specified. (1) The formula assumes the origin is the truth (shrinkage lambda=1). With an honest rolling-origin Elo+HFA+QB origin (fit on seasons < s, 2012-25, n=3625, MAE 10.11 vs market 9.96, SD gap 2.46), the regression of residual-vs-market on (market - origin) gives lambda = 0.273 (SE 0.089, p=0.002): only ~27% of an origin-vs-market gap is real. A 0.75-pt gap across 3 is then worth ~0.27 x 0.088 = 2.4 cover-prob points (EV ~ 0.00 at -110), not +0.11; origin-side cover is 51.4-52.7% at every gap size. (2) Direct test of the premise that crossed mass matters beyond point gap: logit(cover) ~ |gap| + crossed_mass on 2982 OOS bets gives b_cmass = -0.57 (p=0.54), cross3 -0.09 (p=0.43), cross7 -0.04 (p=0.75); by gap band, bets crossing 3/7 cover 46.8% vs 51.0% (gap 1-1.5), 49.8% vs 51.2% (1.5-2.5), 51.6% vs 54.8% (2.5-4), 50.6% vs 56.9% (4+) - never better than equal gaps crossing nothing. With nfelo's close as the model (n=2432, a much better series: lambda 0.73, raw gap b=+0.19/pt, p=0.001) crossed mass is again negative (b=-1.69, p=0.35; cross3 -0.10, cross7 -0.23). The gap 0.5-1.5 cross-3 vs no-key difference is +0.022 (p=0.68) for the Elo origin and -0.034 (p=0.69) for nfelo, against a formula prediction of +0.081 x lambda. (3) The rule 'act when EV>=0.02' fires on 59.4% of games with the Elo origin, cover 51.1% (CI 49.0-53.3), ROI -1.0% at actual closing prices (-20.7 units); realized cover by formula-EV bucket is non-monotone (0.02-0.04: 47.5%; 0.06-0.10: 51.7%; 0.15+: 51.7%). It looks good only with nfelo (54.3%, +4.1%) because nfelo's raw gap is itself predictive, not because of the table. (4) The -3/-7 guard rests on a non-persistent anomaly: dogs at exactly +3 won 55.8% / 53.3% / 49.0% by block (2009-14 / 2015-21 / 2022-25; all ns; ROI +10%/+4.5%/-5%), and the guard cell (latent 3.25 lay 3) has EV -0.045 / -0.064 / +0.064 - it reversed in the test era; at 7 it is -0.021 / +0.012 / -0.175 (n=108), noise. (5) Juice is not what kills this: the market prices only ~0.09 pt of the 3.5 half point in the juice (vig-free favorite prob 0.491 at 3.5, 0.511 at 2.5 in the 2009-22 low-vig book; ~0.50 in 2023-25); the table's failure is lambda. (6) m_3 is trending up across blocks (0.069 -> 0.091 -> 0.108), so a static full-sample 0.088 understates the current push probability at 3.

critics.additional_findings: 1) Totals league_prior is anchored to the wrong statistic (actionable, ~1 pt on every total). The spec sets league_prior = 46.0 = '2025 realized mean' (realized mean 45.96, confirmed). The market total tracks the MEDIAN, not the mean: 2025 mean closing total 44.88, realized median 45.0; 2022-25 realized mean 44.95 vs mean close 44.18 (+0.78, t p=0.044) while the median error is -0.5 and the over rate is 49.2% (over ROI -5.7% at actual prices); 2009-25 identical pattern (+0.51 mean, -0.5 median, 49.4% over, skew 0.32). MAE of (close + delta) is minimised at delta <= 0 (2022-25: 10.185 at -0.5, 10.189 at 0, 10.239 at +1.0; 2009-25: 10.481 at 0, 10.520 at +1.0). With ratings averaging zero, an origin total built on 46.0 sits ~1.1 pts above the average close and flags overs that hit ~49%. Parameter change: league_prior = prior-season mean CLOSING total (44.9 for the 2025 season; use the 2025 close mean for 2026), equivalently target the realized median. Source: critic_01 (f), critic_06 (1),(4). 2) Shrinkage of origin-vs-market gaps (drives every threshold and confidence tag): for an honest rolling-origin Elo+HFA+QB origin (fit on seasons < s, 2012-25, n=3625, MAE 10.11 vs market 9.96) the regression of residual-vs-market on (market - origin) gives lambda = 0.273 (SE 0.089): only ~27% of a gap is real, origin-side cover is 51.4-52.7% at every gap size, and break-even (52.4%) needs roughly 3+ pts of raw gap. nfelo's market-regressed close has lambda = 0.727 (SE 0.18, SD gap 1.11) and its raw gap predicts covers (52.2% at 1-2 pts n=866, 55.5% at 2-3 n=479, 64.2% at 3+ n=95), consistent with its regression toward the market. Recommendation: express edges as lambda x gap, calibrate lambda per engine when history exists; do not treat any origin gap as a fair-line difference. Source: critic_04 (b). 3) The mass at 3 is rising: 0.069 (2009-14) -> 0.091 (2015-21) -> 0.108 (2022-25); unconditional share of games decided by exactly 3: 14.4% fit vs 15.4% test. If a push term is used for -3 lines, use ~0.10, not the full-sample 0.088. Source: critic_04 (a). 4) Key-number value sits in the number, not the juice: vig-free implied favorite probability is 0.511 at 2.5, 0.502 at 3, 0.491 at 3.5, 0.492 at 7, 0.486 at 7.5, 0.487 at 10 in the 2009-22 low-vig book (~0.50 everywhere in the 2023-25 -110 book) - i.e. the market prices only ~0.09 pt of the 3.5 half point into the juice. Assuming -110 both sides is fine to within ~5 cents pre-2023 and exact after. critics.additional_findings: 1. What nfelo_b actually is (critic_01): nfelo_dif_base equals elo_dif + hfa_mod + home_net_qb_mod for 95.9% of games (mean residual 0.5 Elo) - it EXCLUDES the division-game (-20 Elo), surface, time-zone and bye mods that the real pre-regression line carries. On levels r=0.96 vs home_line_pre_regression, but on the disagreement itself corr(D_base, |pre_regression - close|) = 0.605 only (gap SD 1.55 pts). Every D_base-based slope in the expert's work is attenuated; I therefore re-ran the key tests on the real pre-regression line (2021-25, n=1326; 2022-25 n=1076) and on the independent 538 qbelo line, and the conclusions hold on both. 2. Engine independence changes the band shares (critic_01d): |qbelo - close| mean 2.08 vs nfelo_b 1.81; test-era LOW (D>=3) share 34% for qbelo, 22% for the real nfelo line, 16% for nfelo_b. ORIGINATOR's blend (0.39 PFF + 0.15 Cole are presumably not market-regressed) will sit closer to the qbelo case. 3. The close beats the open (critic_04): closing line vs opening line 2294-1916 (54.5%, p<0.0001) ATS; nfelo_b 53.9%, qbelo 51.4%; when the market moves (78% of games) it moves toward nfelo_b's side 61% of the time. This is why the sqrt rule over-predicts against the opener (2cov negative in every band) and why c should be 0 there. 4. Season RMSE 'drift' is mostly noise (critic_05): true between-season SD 0.51 pts vs sampling SD 0.59, lag-1 autocorrelation -0.05; long windows are as good as short ones. 5. Data hygiene (critic_06): 320 games are dropped by the nfelo join, all 2009-2016 (40/season, absent from nfelo_games.csv), market RMSE 13.47 vs 13.09 kept - fit-era only, no OOS survivorship. nflverse and nfelo closing lines differ in 33.5% of games (mean |diff| 0.23 pts) with 8 games off by >3 pts (one apparent sign error, 2020_01_ARI_SF); removing them changes nothing (T1a pooled slope +0.104, p=0.221). 6. The per-game sigma is practically a constant (critic_05): under the sqrt rule sigma/base has mean 1.015 and p90 1.037; the D term flips an 80%/90% interval verdict in 0.7% of games. The whole confidence-tag apparatus reduces to 'how far is our number from the market', which is known at publication without any model. 7. My own error, corrected: the first version of critic_06 compared T_elo's total error to the market's SPREAD error; the totals band table was rerun with e_tot (v2 logged) and the corrected numbers are the ones quoted.

verdicts.reason: The recommendation (totals.pace_adj = 0) survives, but three of the expert's supporting claims do not. (a) 'Every sized rule raised OOS MAE with CIs excluding zero' is mostly the mechanical cost of adding +/-0.5-pt noise plus a lagged-reference artifact: a placebo rule (pace shuffled across games within season, 500 draws) of the same size costs +0.036 +/- 0.024 MAE (95% band to +0.084); the real spec rule (+0.078) sits at the 95.6th percentile of that band and, with a leak-free season-to-date league reference, at +0.066 [+0.017,+0.110], inside it. The expert's reference compares 2024 pace with the 2023 league mean (33.86 vs 32.99 s), so every 2024 team was scored +0.86 s 'slow' (std-ref: +0.10) and the rules subtracted 0.4 pts in the season where BASE was already 1.88 pts too low; 2024 alone contributed +0.143 of the +0.078. On the rating-only totals that ORIGINATOR actually publishes (lg_blend + 0.35*elo_sum) the spec rule's cost is +0.040 [-0.013,+0.087] and the linear std-ref rule +0.015 [-0.019,+0.049], CIs including zero. (b) 'The effect vanished' is not established: the 2023-25 residual-vs-market coefficient has se 0.48 pts/s, giving 9% power to detect the train-sized effect (-0.30) and a minimum detectable effect of 1.34 pts/s; the 2009-19 market-free coefficient (-0.54) is only 1.3 se from the 2023-25 estimate, and with the corrected reference the 2023-25 in-sample coefficient is -0.26 (se 0.53), same sign as train, with calibration slope +0.53 (se 0.86). (c) 'The market's own pace weighting went to zero (+0.07)' is the reference artifact: with the std reference the market total's slope on prior pace is -0.28 (train, p<0.001) and -0.15 (se 0.086, p=0.087) in 2023-25 -- the market still prices pace, just less. The 06 narrative is also weaker than stated: compared with 2016-19 rather than 2009-19, prior-8 pace SD went 1.56 -> 1.46 (independent totals-expert definition 1.49 -> 1.43) and team persistence 0.228 -> 0.227, i.e. unchanged. What actually justifies zero with HIGH confidence is the upper bound: realized plays explain 9.1% of market-residual variance and prior pace predicts 1.4% of realized plays, so pace can explain at most ~0.12% of residual variance; vs the market, pooled 2009-19+2023-25 (n=3194) the residual slope is -0.21 (se 0.19, p=0.27; Huber -0.18) and rolling-origin market+adj is worse in 7/10 seasons.

verdicts.reason: The EPA term is real -- it survives attacks the expert did not run -- but the implementable rule is smaller and less certain than reported, the O/U edge is not established, and the parameter definition must change. (1) The expert's league reference (prior-season league EPA; 2019 nflscrapR EPA used for 2023 nflfastR EPA) gives the rule a mean adjustment of -0.88 pts in 2023 (mean epa_sum -0.221; +0.004 with a season-to-date reference) against a +0.79 under-prediction, and +0.50 pts in 2024 aligned with a +1.88 under-prediction; demeaning the rule within each test season cuts the gain from -0.051 to -0.033 [-0.084,+0.018]. With the leak-free season-to-date reference the fixed rule clip(4*epa_sum, +/-3) gives -0.039 [-0.089,+0.011] OOS (per-season 2023 +0.007, 2024 -0.023, 2025 -0.091), refit -0.060 [-0.128,+0.012], calibration 0.58 (se 0.39), 2023-25 in-sample coefficient +5.67 (se 3.23, p=0.079). (2) The 54.6% O/U is not an edge: always-over hit 51.1% in 2023-25 and BASE alone 52.3%; the EPA rule flips 91 picks and wins 54-37 of them (exact binomial p=0.093); 408-339 vs the always-over rate p=0.057. (3) What supports the term: pooled rolling-origin over all 10 available test seasons (n=2381) gives refit +epa_sum_s -0.049 [-0.092,-0.007], 6/7 pre-2020 seasons and 2/3 modern seasons better; the fixed 4.0 rule -0.029 [-0.057,+0.001] (7/10 seasons), 3.0 rule -0.024 [-0.046,-0.002]; single-season coefficients positive in 11/14 seasons, inverse-variance pooled +5.73 (se 1.66), Huber +6.68; a recency placebo (prior-8 points for+against over the same window) gives -0.009 [-0.047,+0.031] pooled and +0.006 OOS, so the gain is EPA, not the 8-game window; and the market prices EPA at the realized rate (market slope +6.54 train / +7.94 test vs realized +6.68 / +5.67; residual-vs-market -0.6 / -1.8, ns), so the term moves BASE toward the market (MAE vs market 2.131 -> 1.964). (4) Construction-sensitivity caveat: the totals critic's rolling-origin found +0.003 [-0.020,+0.026] for the totals expert's K=6-blend EPA on the FULL spec, so the gain depends on the prior-8 window and reference; and the expert selected epa_sum as the best of 11 candidates in one OOS window (winner's curse), which the 10-season rolling result partly but not fully de-biases. Net: a market-consistency term worth about -0.03 to -0.04 MAE, CI touching zero, not a betting edge.

critics.additional_findings: 1. Generic artifact in the expert's feature build (affects every 2023-25 OOS number in T1-T4): the '_r8d' league-relative features subtract the PRIOR season's league mean (2019's nflscrapR mean for 2023's nflfastR data). Per-season means of the features in 2023/2024/2025, in SDs: spp_neut +0.25/+0.60/+0.10, game_plays -0.04/-0.51/-0.34, epa_off -0.48/+0.25/+0.01, epa_def -0.58/+0.36/+0.09, expl_def -0.30/+0.27/-0.09, pr_neut -0.02/-0.31/+0.02 (critic_05_extra.log A). Since BASE's own bias was +0.79/+1.88/-0.76 by season, any linear rule's OOS dMAE picks up a season-level term unrelated to matchups (it hurt the pace and PROE rules and helped the EPA rule in 2024, hurt it in 2023). Engine spec recommendation: league-relative = minus the current season-to-date league mean once >= 64 team-games exist, else prior-season mean; and never mix pbp sources inside a reference. 2. Pace does not inform the totals confidence tag: |total - market| on prior pace, train -0.071 (se 0.127, p=0.58), test -0.027 (p=0.93); SD of market error FF vs SS 13.67 vs 13.75 train (Levene p=0.53), 16.82 vs 13.16 test on n=34/25 (p=0.34). Realized plays do (+0.061 train, +0.150 test pts of |err| per play, p<0.01) but are not knowable pre-kickoff. Keep the totals SD tag independent of pace. 3. The market still weights pace in the modern era: market total ~ BASE + prior spp (season-to-date reference) = -0.284 (se 0.036) in 2009-19 and -0.148 (se 0.086, p=0.087) in 2023-25 -- the expert's '+0.065, p=0.42' was the lagged-reference artifact. 4. Pace dispersion and persistence are unchanged vs the late 2010s: prior-8 neutral sec/play SD 1.56 (2016-19) vs 1.46 (2023-25) and team persistence 0.228 vs 0.227 (independent totals-expert definition: SD 1.49 vs 1.43, persistence 0.203 vs 0.181); the expert's 1.30 -> 1.02 and 0.35 -> 0.23 contrasts are driven by 2009-2013. 5. T2's 2023-25 'explosive offense' signal is one season: single-season market-residual coefficients 2023 +15, 2024 +57 (se 18), 2025 -0.0; fit 2023-24 -> 2025 OOS dMAE +0.030 [-0.041,+0.104]. 6. The EPA gain is not a recency effect: an 8-game points-for/against term with the same window gives -0.009 [-0.047,+0.031] pooled rolling-origin vs -0.049 [-0.092,-0.007] for EPA, and EPA stays significant (+5.2, p=0.013) when both are included. 7. Power note for the orchestrator: with 752 test games the residual-vs-market coefficient SE is 0.48 pts per second of pace (0.07 per PROE pct-pt), so 'not detected in 2023-25' should never be read as 'gone'; rolling-origin over all 10 seasons and the market's own weighting are the more informative tests, and the upper-bound argument (prior pace explains 1.4% of plays, plays explain 9.1% of market residual variance) is what justifies pace_adj = 0.

The specific evidence for a W1 cap does not survive: (1) era instability - W1 share is 1.12 (se 0.50) in 2009-14 and -0.14 (se 0.45) in 2015-25, so the 2015-25 p=0.015 the expert cites is the only window with the effect and the two eras disagree by 1.26 (se ~0.67); (2) the W1-4 pooled significance rides on Week 3 (share 0.25): W1,2,4 vs W5+ change -0.27 (cluster se 0.21, p=0.19), W1-2 vs W5+ -0.32 (p=0.26), while W2 (0.86) and W4 (0.81) are near fully informative - inconsistent with a smooth 'preseason ratings' story, and it undercuts the proposed W2-4 caps; (3) with a QB-aware rating line (nraw, the closer analogue of PFF/Cole), the W1 change is -0.20 (se 0.36, p=0.57) and W1-4 -0.18 (p=0.44) in 2009-25; (4) OOS: with the cap chosen on prior seasons (rolling 2015-25) the W1 gain is -0.09 [-0.27,+0.08] p=0.30 and W1-4 -0.06 [-0.18,+0.06]; fixed post-hoc caps do better (c=1.5 W1 -0.185 [-0.35,-0.03]) but W5+ caps hurt at every value (+0.13 to +0.23, p<0.01); (5) the new-QB flag does not explain the low W1 share (0.46 with the flag, 0.35 in games with no QB change), and large deviations (|dev|>2.5) still carry share 0.54 (se 0.38) in W1, so the information is not 'noise' so much as half-weight. Most importantly, the object tested (the market's deviation from a roster-blind regressed Elo) is not the engine's context adjustments, which sit on top of roster-aware PFF/Cole ratings; the expert acknowledges this. The confidence-tag part (no widening in W1) is upheld: residual SD W1 12.97 vs 13.13.

critics.additional_findings: (1) 2026 W1 rating dispersion answers the expert's open caveat on theory 2 (critic_06): outcome-supported W1 rating SD is ~3.6 pts (slope 1.17 x nfelo SD 3.04; 95% band 2.4-4.7). PFF 2026 'Point Spread Rating Points' SD 3.74 (implied k 0.95), Cole power 3.17 / betting 3.29 (k 1.08-1.12) - all inside the band, so no W1 shrink is warranted for PFF/Cole either. The 2026 nfelo W1 SD is 2.16, below every prior season (2.68-3.48): verify the 2026 nfelo rows are final preseason ratings before the card is built. (2) Leakage guard: nfelo hfa_base_mod becomes a rolling estimate from 2015 (up to 19 distinct values per season) but takes one value within each Week 1, so the W1 tests use no in-season information. (3) Rolling-origin blend weights (critic_01 D): W1 rating 0.40 / market 0.58, W2-4 0.60/0.51, W5-9 0.57/0.60, W10+ 0.06/1.06; the blend beats the market nowhere OOS (W1 -0.02 [-0.22,+0.17]). (4) The W1 scoring dip sits in a week profile (season-demeaned, cluster se ~0.6): W1 -1.23, W2 -0.50, W3 -0.15, W4 +0.96, W5 +1.22; the market's total is below the season mean in every week (-0.5 to -1.1), so W1 is the one week where the market's general under-pricing of scoring (+0.7 residual elsewhere) is absent - consistent with the totals expert. W1 residual distribution is skewed (median -2.0 vs mean -0.47; game-level W1 - prev mean Wilcoxon p=0.010). (5) New-QB signal is carried by 'took over during last season' incumbents (+3.29, se 1.57, n=93 team-games, ATS 49-34), not by QBs new to the team (+1.49, p=0.19): a candidate 'late-season form understated by the full-season record' hypothesis for the qb expert, INCONCLUSIVE at n=93. (6) New-HC teams underperform the close from W5 on: -0.53 (se 0.31, p=0.086), TEST 2022-25 -1.31 (se 0.69, p=0.057); not W1, inconclusive, flagged for the season-long parameter owner. (7) Post-hoc but consistent: market W1 home residual 2013-25 -1.55 (cluster se 0.70, p=0.026) vs -0.15 in 1999-2012, same sign as the 5a W1 HFA shift (-1.0 in both the nfelo and the naive-rating specification); keeps the optional -0.5 W1 HFA haircut on the table without establishing it.
